records.title: The audits list presents audit-log rows as audit engagements and invents status, findings 0 and hasReport false for every row.
The audit item route returns the complete audit_logs row, with details and any recorded address and agent, to an officer role floor with no redaction by reader.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Officer-gated item read now uses tenant-bound transaction, explicit non-sensitive field projection and mandatory audit-read evidence; rejects invalid identifiers and missing organization.

records.title: The audits routes read the audit_security audit_logs table, while persistAtomicAudit writes the domains infrastructure audit_logs table, so the routes do not show the audit records the atomic writers produce.

The bargaining-notes GET returns timeline, statistics and session-type results before the visibleToUserId confidentiality filter is applied, and the timeline returns the title of every note of an agreement whatever its confidentiality level.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The special summary views use the same confidentiality policy as the list, which shows only public and internal notes (upstream's change); an existing test covers the list and a source contract pins the summary modes.

records.title: The bargaining-note item GET and PATCH are the generic factory: a member reads any note by id, including restricted and confidential notes the collection route withholds, and an update skips the agreement check the collection create applies.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The item read applies the same confidentiality filter (upstream's change). Only a source contract pins it; the item route has no behavioural test.

records.title: Tentative agreement creation verifies the parent negotiation but stores relatedProposalIds and relatedClauseId without verifying that the proposals or clause belong to that negotiation or organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: relatedProposalIds are now an array of at most 50 ids, each of which must be a proposal of the same negotiation, and relatedClauseId must be a clause of an agreement of the caller organization (404 otherwise, nothing written). Existing route tests pass.

records.title: Negotiation and tentative-agreement reads sit at the member floor and ignore confidentialityLevel, so strike-vote results, cost ceilings and costed agreements reach every member.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Negotiations are read at the steward floor through shared rules (upstream's change); bargaining proposals, which carry unreleased positions, now match it.

records.title: The trial-expiry route passes a payment-method checker that always returns false, so every expired trial of the organization is cancelled whether or not a payment method exists, at a steward role floor.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route answers 501 and cancels nothing: it asked a placeholder that always answered "no payment method", so a page load by any steward cancelled a trial that had one. Test disclosure: the three tests that asserted the placeholder behaviour were replaced by one that asserts the 501 and that no trial is expired.

records.title: The send-invoice route generates and stores an invoice and returns it; nothing is delivered, whatever the route name advertises.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route generated a platform invoice and delivered nothing. It answers 501 behind the steward floor (generation remains POST /api/finance/invoices and the billing batch). Its test, which asserted the generation, was replaced by an assertion of the 501 and of the absence of the generator.

records.title: Subscription commercial terms are readable at the member floor, pause, resume, invoice generation and trial expiry sit at the steward floor, and update and cancel sit at the secretary_treasurer role title, a union finance role; no source names the office with contract authority.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Subscriptions are read at the officer floor and paused or resumed by an administrator (was a steward).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Authority is still a role title with the financial-mandate check only on reconciliation; subscription changes need the live financial mandate.

records.title: calculateMetrics stores claim identifiers in the metric metadata and the metrics GET returns that metadata to every member at the member floor.

currentRun.repair: New calculations persist only aggregate counts; member metrics reads now allowlist aggregate-only metadata for all historical and new records; idempotent PostgreSQL migration removes stored claimIds from historical claims-volume rows.
currentRun.limits: Historical rows remain until migration executes; no runtime/independent acceptance.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: New calculations persist only aggregate counts; member metrics reads now allowlist aggregate-only metadata for all historical and new records; idempotent PostgreSQL migration removes stored claimIds from historical claims-volume rows.

records.title: The metrics routes resolve the organization once in the route wrapper and again in the action through getOrganizationIdForUser, and the action ignores the first, so a user with more than one membership may write to an organization other than the session organization.

The derived case metrics and the weekly summary count pilot telemetry events and present them as case figures; open cases are created minus closed events and overdue cases are breached minus closed events, with no case table read.

The break compliance report returns per-member denied, missed and flagged counts to any steward while the generic break route holds a member to their own rows, so the report is authorized more broadly than the records it is computed from.

currentRun.repair: Replaced per-member steward report with organization-only self-report totals under tenant RLS; suppresses cohorts of 1–4, does not imply employer verification, and requires durable read audit. Member-owned self-report routes remain unchanged.
currentRun.limits: No source-backed case-representation authority for steward-level individual break reporting; such detail remains unavailable. No independent approval.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Replaced per-member steward report with organization-only self-report totals under tenant RLS; suppresses cohorts of 1–4, does not imply employer verification, and requires durable read audit. Member-owned self-report routes remain unchanged.

records.title: The realtime alerts route returns the raw triggerData of alert executions, with SLA-risk, ingestion-failure and payment-failure counts, to every member under a case-suite entitlement, with no redaction and no named reader.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The realtime alert inbox needs an officer, since each execution carries the rule's trigger data.

records.title: The Google and Microsoft authorization routes pass the session user id as the OAuth state and the callbacks compare the returned state with that same id, and accept a callback with no state at all, so the state is neither unguessable nor single-use and gives no protection against a forged callback.

currentRun.repair: Replaced predictable user-id state with signed 256-bit nonce, ten-minute expiry, provider/user/org binding and HttpOnly SameSite browser cookie; rejects missing/mismatched state before token exchange and clears browser state on terminal responses.
currentRun.limits: Not counted as fully engineering-corrected: durable one-time nonce consumption across concurrent callbacks/instances is not yet implemented; exact-SHA CI and real provider acceptance pending.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The OAuth state is an unpredictable signed value bound to the browser, provider, user and organization, expiring, carried in an HttpOnly cookie and verified before any token exchange; it fails closed without a signing key (upstream's change, existing test).

records.title: The provider callbacks are GET handlers that exchange a code and insert or update the connection row holding the provider tokens, and neither the callback nor the member-floor wrapper writes an audit record for the connection, so a state-changing GET leaves no audit evidence.

currentRun.repair: Provider OAuth token writes now carry an atomic, tenant-scoped mandatory audit record; failure aborts transaction.
currentRun.limits: Source and regression authored; no exact-HEAD unit, native PG15/16, HTTP/browser or real provider acceptance yet.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both provider callbacks now perform the credential mutation and mandatory audit within the same organization-bound RLS transaction, with the connection id and actor. An audit failure prevents the transaction from committing. Callback unit regressions cover both providers and audit failure; exact-SHA CI and real provider acceptance remain pending.

records.title: encryptCalendarToken returns the token unencrypted when no encryption key is configured outside production, and decryptCalendarToken returns any value without the encryption prefix as it is, so a database written without the key holds provider tokens in clear text and never fails.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A provider token is never stored without an encryption key (development included; plaintext only under the test runner), and a stored value with no encryption prefix is refused unless CALENDAR_TOKEN_ALLOW_LEGACY_PLAINTEXT is set for a flagged migration window. New unit tests cover round trip, missing key in development and production, and the legacy flag.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Existing plaintext rows need a one-time re-encryption or re-authorization; none is performed here.

records.title: The connection collection and item reads select the whole external_calendar_connections row, so the stored accessToken and refreshToken values are returned to the browser of the connection owner.

currentRun.note: Existing source uses safe projection and user+organization predicates; behavioral unit regression added; real HTTP/credential validation pending.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both connection GET routes select explicit safe projections excluding accessToken, refreshToken and tokenExpiresAt, and bind both organizationId and userId; regression checks projections and owner predicates.

records.title: A steward can create or update a connection through the generic factory with any provider, providerAccountId, accessToken and refreshToken, stored as supplied and unencrypted, and an update can reassign userId, so the OAuth flow and the token encryption can be bypassed and a connection can be handed to another user.

currentRun.note: Existing source permits direct POST only as OAuth initiation, rejects credential fields on PATCH; regression added, runtime pending.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Direct POST accepts only provider and returns OAuth initiation URL without writing; item PATCH strictly accepts non-secret sync settings, enforces caller ownership, and audits changes transactionally. Regression rejects token and identity mass assignment.

records.title: The connection sync route selects the connection by id and organization only, with no userId predicate and no role above organization membership, so any member can run an import or export through another member provider account.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Sync requires the authenticated connection owner and organization, with the provider operation audited before execution.

records.title: The sync route proves that the local calendar and event are in the organization but not that the caller owns a personal calendar or may read a personal event, so a member can import into or export from another member personal calendar.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Sync requires local calendar ownership and exported event membership in that calendar plus the caller's organizer identity, preventing personal calendar/event access by other organization members.

records.title: The sync records intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around an external provider call, and the connection update runs inside that operation without the audit record; the record is not committed with the state change.

The calendar item route supplies lockedAuthCheck to reject another member personal calendar, but the factory invokes it only when beforeUpdate or mergeJsonColumns is configured and never on delete, and the route configures neither, so a steward can still update or delete another member personal calendar.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Generic item PATCH enters locked transaction whenever lockedAuthCheck exists; DELETE independently acquires FOR UPDATE and invokes lockedAuthCheck before mutation.

records.title: The calendar events routes filter events by calendar id and organization or by organization alone and never consult calendars.isPersonal or ownerId, which calendar_events does not carry, so a member reads events of another member personal calendar through calendars/[id]/events and staff read every personal event through calendar/events.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Event collection joins calendars and enforces tenant, personal-calendar owner and private-event visibility; item reads and mutations apply per-event visibility and organizer authority under tenant RLS.

records.title: Event create and update store a caller-supplied calendarId without verifying that the calendar belongs to the organization or is visible to the caller; the foreign key checks only that a calendar row exists.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Existing implementation, verified by a new test: event create checks the calendar belongs to the caller organization and is not another member personal calendar (404).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The event update route does not re-check a changed calendarId.

records.title: No table of the CBA intelligence dataset has an organization column and none of the services filters by organization, so every organization reads, and every administrator or steward writes, one shared dataset; nothing in the source states which organizations may read it or who curates it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Writes and review are now platform authority. The dataset is shared by design (no organization column), so a tenant predicate does not apply to its reads.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Reads (agreements list and detail, benchmark, documents, freshness) remain open to any entitled member or steward of any organization; whether the shared dataset may be read that widely, and under which entitlement, is an institutional decision.

records.title: The agreement list, item and export reads apply a review status filter only when the caller supplies one, so extracted agreements, wage adjustments and clauses that are pending, rejected or superseded are returned as the dataset.

Source registration and update, ingestion, seeding and extraction require only an organization administrator role floor, yet they create and change the dataset every organization reads and call external services at the platform expense, so the administrator of any one organization can curate platform-wide data; no source names the platform staff mandate.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The extracted CBA dataset (agreements, findings, wage adjustments, clauses, sources, ingestion) has no organization column. Extraction, ingestion (create, run, seed) and source create/update were open to an organization's administrator; each now calls requireSystemAdmin() first. A contract test checks all seven mutating handlers. The extraction route test gained the platform-admin mock and a refusal test.

records.title: A steward of any organization can approve, reject or supersede an extracted record, which sets the review status every organization sees, and the decision records the reviewer role as the literal steward whatever the caller role is.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The review queue and review decisions (approve, reject, supersede) changed rows every organization reads at the steward floor of any one organization. Both methods now require a platform administrator and the reviewer role recorded is platform_administrator, not a literal "steward". A refusal test covers the queue and the decision, which write and read nothing.

records.title: Extraction, ingestion runs and source seeding declare an atomic service audit, but they record intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around many separate statements and an external provider call, so the audit record is not committed with the state change.

The benchmark GET inserts a cba_intel_benchmark_snapshots row when save=true, recording the caller user id, and the route and the service write no audit record, so a state-changing GET is both mislabelled as a read and unaudited.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: GET computes and returns a benchmark and refuses ?save. Saving a snapshot is a new POST that needs a platform administrator (the dataset has no organization column), records the intent before the write, and stores nothing when that audit cannot be written.

records.title: The snapshot history is selected by target agreement only and returns the computedBy user id of whoever saved each snapshot, so a steward of one organization reads the user ids of stewards of other organizations.

The export route asks the service for 10000 rows but listAgreements clamps the limit to 100, so the CSV advertised as an export of the agreements holds at most the first 100 rows and says nothing about it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The export asked for 10000 rows but the list serves at most 100 a page, so the file silently held the first page. It reads every page and refuses (400) a result set over 10000, naming the count, instead of cutting it.

records.title: Source registration accepts any URL for the base, API, feed and terms addresses, and the ingestion adapters fetch the discovered document URLs from the server with no host allow-list or private-address check, so an administrator can make the platform request internal addresses.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A shared guard refuses non-http(s) schemes, credentials in the address, localhost and internal names, private, loopback, link-local, metadata and reserved IPv4 and IPv6 literals (including IPv4-mapped forms). The base adapter checks every address before fetching, follows redirects by hand (three at most) re-checking each hop, and refuses a source larger than 10 million characters; every ingestion adapter fetches through it, and a source address is checked when it is saved.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The guard reads the address as written and does not resolve DNS, so a public name that resolves to a private address is not caught; that needs an egress policy or a resolving fetch. The body is still read whole before the size check.

records.title: The moderation step returns not flagged when OPENAI_API_KEY is unset and, when the moderation request fails, returns a flagged result with the reason Safety system unavailable that sendMessage then ignores and proceeds, although the code comments call the failure closed; a member message reaches the model unmoderated whenever moderation is absent or down.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Missing moderation credentials, provider HTTP failures, malformed moderation responses and moderation audit errors no longer permit model/retrieval execution. The safety guard throws for every flagged result, including safety-system unavailability. Separate AI control-plane bypass and fallback provenance defects remain open.

records.title: The moderation step posts the member message text directly to api.openai.com with a provider key, outside @nzila/ai-sdk which the same file names as the only route for AI calls, so the data-class, budget and audit controls of the AI control plane do not apply to that call.

The message route marks every reply reviewRequired false and passes the literal role member to enforceAISafety whatever the caller role is, although the service describes the output as advisory with human stewardship preserved, so the policy check never sees the caller real role and the response never asks for review.

When the model call fails the service stores a fixed apology as an assistant message with model fallback, and the route returns it as a successful response marked aiGenerated true with the configured deployment name as the model, so an outage is persisted in the transcript and reported as a model reply.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A failed generation raises ChatbotUnavailableError (a 502 from the route) and stores nothing; it no longer saves a canned apology as an assistant message from the model "fallback". Test disclosure: the test that asserted the stored fallback was replaced. The ai-client mock lacked buildOrgAiTrace, so the other sendMessage tests had been passing on that canned reply; the mock now provides it and those tests exercise a real generation.

records.title: Retrieval selects at most three active knowledge rows of the organization with no ordering and no vector predicate and only then scores them by similarity, so the context sent to the model is an arbitrary subset of the knowledge base rather than the most relevant documents.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The search scores a bounded candidate set (500 rows) and applies the requested limit to the best matches; a row with a missing or unreadable embedding is skipped instead of throwing; a threshold of 0 is honoured.

records.title: The session list and the message read apply no status condition, so archived and deleted sessions stay listed and readable, and the message read applies neither the ai_chatbot entitlement, the AI feature flag, the AI safety check nor a rate limit, so a transcript stays readable after the feature is disabled.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The session list reads active sessions only, and the message read needs the entitlement, the AI feature flag, the safety check and the rate limit, and refuses an archived or deleted session (existing implementation and test).

records.title: The list, item, tags, compare and search reads run on the system role, which bypasses row-level security, and the only boundary between organizations is a hand-written application predicate; the route comments name this PRIVILEGED_CROSS_TENANT_REVIEW and no kernel decision stands behind it.

The item authority canReadSharedClause admits a federation clause only when the nearest federation ancestor of the caller equals that of the owner, while the list and search predicate admits it whenever the caller federation appears anywhere in the owner hierarchy path, so when federations nest the list and search return clauses the item, tags and compare reads refuse.

The item read returns originalEmployerName and the creator user id to any reader whatever isAnonymized says, and every read returns the owning organization name, so a clause shared as anonymized discloses the employer it was anonymized from.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: For non-owner readers of anonymized shared clauses, item GET no longer exposes originalEmployerName, creator user ID or source organization identity; list GET also hides the source union identity for anonymized shared clauses. Source-level structural regressions added. Free-text de-identification and human review of clause content are NOT proven by this correction and remain an explicit privacy acceptance concern.

records.title: The item read returns the createdBy user id of the clause, and the tags read returns whole clause_library_tags rows with their createdBy user id, to stewards of other organizations that may read the clause.

A steward of any organization can create or change a clause to sharing level public, which exposes its text to every organization; sharingChangeDenial checks only federation and congress eligibility, and no source names who may publish collective-agreement text.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Setting a clause to public sharing on create, update or the share route now requires an officer role; a steward, a member or an unresolved role is refused with 403 before any read or write. Narrower scopes stay with the owning steward and keep their federation and congress eligibility checks.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The floor is a role title; no mandate-kernel decision names who may publish collective-agreement text.

records.title: Clause create, update, sharing update and tag writes store clause text, title, type, dates, anonymization fields and tag names from the body with no schema validation; only sharingLevel and sharedWithOrgIds are checked, so a malformed value reaches the database or throws as an unhandled error.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Clause create, update and sharing bodies pass a zod schema before anything is stored: text, titles and names are bounded, dates are real calendar days, province is a 2-letter code, ids are ids, sharing levels are the four known ones, grants are at most 200 ids, and unknown fields are dropped. A malformed body is a 400. Existing route tests were adapted: organization and agreement fixtures that were not ids became ids, and handler calls that publish publicly carry an officer role (disclosed).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The tag write route still reads its body without the schema.

records.title: Clause create stores a caller-supplied originalClauseId that the schema notes as a foreign key to cba_clauses that is not enforced, and the route checks sourceCbaId against the organization but never checks originalClauseId, so a clause can point at another organization clause.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A cited originalClauseId must be a clause of a collective agreement of the caller own organization (joined through the agreement); a missing or foreign one is a 404 and nothing is inserted. The id must also be well-formed.

records.title: The update overwrites the shared clause text and sharing fields without raising version or setting previousVersionId, and the delete removes the row and its tags permanently, so organizations that compared or cited a clause see it change silently or vanish, and only the audit record remains.

The compare POST increments comparisonCount on rows owned by other organizations under the system role, and the audit record it commits belongs to the comparing organization, so a reader changes data it does not own and the owner has no record of it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A comparison no longer increments comparisonCount on rows another organization owns: it is a read of those rows and writes only the usage counter of the caller own clauses. The audit stays with the comparing organization.

records.title: The compare GET returns a usage message with status 200 and performs no comparison, and the compare POST returns commonKeywords as the constant empty list, so part of the advertised analysis is a placeholder presented as a result.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The GET stub (a 200 with a usage hint) is removed (405). commonKeywords is now computed from the compared clause texts (words of four letters or more, not stop words, present in every clause, ranked by frequency; English and French). Clause ids are validated as ids and a malformed body is a 400. The route test fixtures use real ids now.

records.title: The clc dashboard, remittances and sync routes are the same generic CRUD configuration over clc_sync_log, and no other code in the application reads or writes that table, so the dashboard and remittance routes return and create synchronization log rows and serve no dashboard or remittance, and the sync route records a log entry and starts no synchronization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: clc/dashboard, clc/remittances and clc/sync served clc_sync_log rows under dashboard, remittance and sync names; all answer 501. Their tables lost their last generic binding, so the governance entries for grievances, clc_sync_log, cms_media_library, cms_pages and organizer_tasks were removed (an unlisted table is refused by the fail-closed default); the "keeps grievances as OWN_ROWS_READ" case was removed from the governance test for that reason.

records.title: The routes read the whole clc_sync_log row, with errorMessage, errorDetails, syncData and dataHash, at the member floor, and the steward create stores any body field, including status, record counts, isVerified, verifiedBy and verifiedAt, so a steward can record a synchronization as verified that never ran and every member can read integration error details.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The sync-log facade answers 501; its table is no longer reachable through a generic route (batches B09 and B15).

records.title: The CNESST filing collection declares ownerColumn memberId, so the factory compares the uuid memberId column with the session user id for every caller, steward included, while the item routes declare no ownerColumn and let a steward read any filing of the organization; the source does not show that the session user id is the member id, so the collection and the item routes disagree about which filings a steward may see.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The filings collection sets staffReadsAll, so the member-id owner scope applies only below the steward floor and a steward reads the organization filings, as the item routes already allow.

records.title: The CNESST filing item routes and the create read and write any filing of the organization for a steward role floor, accept any memberId, incidentId and unionRepId in the body, and do not check that the steward represents the member the filing concerns; a filing holds the member injury narrative, outcome and compensation awarded.

anti_scab_violations has no createdBy column, so the factory records no author, reportedById and reportedByName are taken from the body rather than the session, and any steward of the organization can change the outcome fields (resolved, penaltyAmount, injunctionGranted, tatFileNumber) of any violation record.

The anti-scab violation and joint committee tables have no status column, so the fixed administrator delete of the factory removes the regulatory record permanently; only the audit record of the delete remains, and no source names a retention rule for them.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: New crud-factory option retainOnDelete: DELETE answers 409 before any lookup or write, so the row is kept. Applied to the anti-scab violation and joint health-and-safety committee item routes, the two tables the defect names. A contract test pins that the refusal comes before any audited write or tx.delete.

records.title: The joint committee read sits at the member floor and returns the worker representative list with member identifiers, names and roles, and the worker co-chair identifier, to every member of the organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The joint health-and-safety committee roster is read at the steward floor.

records.title: The agreement detail GET increments collective_agreements.view_count in a tenant transaction whenever includeAnalytics=true, at the member floor, with no audit record, so a read-only operation changes stored state and any member can inflate the counter.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Reading one agreement counts no view, whatever the include flags; the view counter is no longer incremented by a read.

records.title: The agreement detail returns clauses and bargaining notes by cbaId alone: getClausesByCBAId and getBargainingNotesByCBA carry no organization predicate, and the clause create stores any cbaId, so a clause written by one organization against another organization agreement id is returned in that agreement detail.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The clause and bargaining-note reads take the caller's organization as a required argument and name it beside the agreement id, so a child row written against another organization's agreement is never returned. Existing service tests adapted only by passing the new argument; the route test now asserts the notes read carries the organization.

records.title: The clause create is the generic factory, which stores the body cbaId, a foreign key to collective_agreements.id that no organization condition guards, so a steward can attach clauses to the agreement of another organization; the organization column is forced from the session but the agreement is not checked.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A clause create verifies that the agreement belongs to the caller's organization (404 otherwise) and that any parent clause is a clause of the same agreement, and accepts only author fields: the embedding, hash, confidence, extracted entities and counters are processing outputs.

records.title: The clause item GET passes countView true on every request that does not ask for the hierarchy, so each read updates cba_clauses.view_count at the member floor with no audit record.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Reading a clause by id writes nothing. Test adapted from countView true to false; the clause view counter is no longer incremented by a read.

records.title: The clause search route is the generic CRUD configuration over cba_clauses and applies no search term: GET lists clause rows and POST creates a clause, so no search is performed.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: clauses/search listed the clause table without searching; it answers 501.

records.title: The clause comparison groups clauses by type, always returns empty differences and best practices, and returns three fixed recommendation sentences whatever the clauses say; the route returns this as an analysis and, with save true, stores it as the analysis result of a named comparison.
The agreement list passes the caller limit and page, parsed without a ceiling, to the service, which clamps neither, so a member can request an unbounded page of agreements.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The agreement list refuses a page outside 1..10000 or a limit outside 1..100 with 400 instead of passing an unparsed number to the query.

records.title: With includeNotes=true the agreement detail returns every bargaining note of the agreement whose confidentiality level is public or internal to any member at the member floor, so internal bargaining notes reach members who hold no bargaining role.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The agreement detail embeds only the notes the caller may see and keeps privileged notes from other members (upstream's change, existing test).

records.title: collective_agreements.cba_number carries a single unique constraint across every organization, and the create and update routes answer a duplicate with a conflict, so a steward of one organization learns whether any organization holds a given agreement number and cannot use a number another organization holds.

The newsletter delivery status route is gated by the financial_intelligence_suite entitlement, a finance product gate, so the entitlement that decides who may read campaign delivery state is unrelated to the data and to the communications obligation.

Any job id that does not start with campaign-, and any campaign id that is not found, returns status processing with zero counts and a start time of the moment of the request, so a job that does not exist is reported as running.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A job id that is not a campaign job, or a campaign of another organization, is answered 404 instead of a fabricated processing status with a start time of now; the failed-recipient list names a recipient id, not an e-mail address.

records.title: The status response lists the e-mail address of up to ten failed recipients to any steward holding the entitlement and records no audit of the disclosure.

Case studies are global marketing rows read by every organization and the public, yet create, update and delete sit at the organization admin role floor, so the admin of any one organization can publish, rewrite or remove content shown to all organizations; no source names the platform staff mandate that should hold this write.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Case-study writes need content_manager and the item route (read and write) is limited to it; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.

records.title: The public case-study list and the member item read filter on neither visibility nor publishedAt, and the list status filter reads a status column that case_studies does not have, so unpublished rows and rows marked authenticated are returned to anonymous callers and to members of every organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The public list is limited to public, already published rows for both the rows and the count, and a status other than published is refused; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.

records.title: The carbon dashboard and infrastructure routes return emissions totals, regional breakdowns, renewable percentages and optimization advice as literals in the handler, with success true and status 200, for any authenticated caller, so invented measurements are presented as monitoring results.

remaining: The superseded carbon-validate test asserted the fabricated 200/400 and was removed

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Carbon routes already answer 501; upstream's change, existing test.

records.title: The carbon dashboard takes organizationId from the query string, defaults it to union-eyes and echoes it, so the response names an organization chosen by the caller and not the session organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the carbon dashboard no longer reads an organization id from the query string and no longer returns figures; it answers 501.

records.title: The carbon validation route computes a certificationEligible result and a message of Eligible for certification from numbers the caller supplied, with no source for the data points and no record of the check, so an unverified figure yields a certification-shaped answer.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Claim validation answers 501: no claim is assessed and no certification outcome is given. The dashboard and infrastructure routes do the same.

records.title: The collection routes of preventive_withdrawals and right_of_refusal_events declare ownerColumn workerId, and neither table has a workerId column, so the factory resolves no owner column and applies no owner condition: the declared owner scope is not applied, and the item routes of the same tables declare no owner scope at all.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Existing implementation, verified by a new test: neither collection declares an owner column the table lacks, so no declared-but-unapplied owner condition remains.

records.title: Any steward of the organization reads, creates and rewrites any member preventive withdrawal and right-of-refusal record, and accepts memberId, memberName, cneesstFilingId and the outcome fields from the body, without holding the member case; the withdrawal holds the physician name, medical certificate date, reassignment and income replacement amounts, and the refusal holds the reprisal complaint details.

right_of_refusal_events has no status column, so the fixed administrator delete of the factory removes the regulatory record of a refusal and any reprisal complaint permanently; only the audit record of the delete remains, and no source names a retention rule.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The right-of-refusal item route declares retainOnDelete, so the refusal record and any reprisal complaint are never removed through the generic delete (409).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: No retention rule is named by a source, so the record is retained rather than archived; a governed withdrawal action is still to be defined.

records.title: The pay equity routes store any body field, including status, results and adjustment amounts, so an officer can record an exercise as adjustments_paid without the intermediate states; the contest deadline and the next maintenance date are plain date columns whose statutory rules (sixty days from posting, every five years) exist only as schema comments, so no source computes or enforces them.

Every cognition engine persists its snapshots as JSON files under ops/ue-cognition at the root of the server checkout, one directory per entity shared by every organization, and keeps tenancy only by filtering subject.orgId after reading every file; there is no table, no row level security and no durability across hosts or restarts, so the derived figures a steward and an administrator read are neither tenant-isolated at rest nor reproducible.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: No route or cognition library writes the local file system any more (upstream's change); a contract test now fails if one does.

records.title: The risk, workload and key-indicator GET routes and the precedent search compute a snapshot and write it to a local file on every call, then record a separate auditLog event; the write is not in the audit transaction, a GET changes stored state, and a failed audit leaves the snapshot behind.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Same: the read routes no longer write files, so there is no write to audit separately; pinned by the contract test.

records.title: Any steward of the organization requests a risk score, recommended action and rationale for any grievance of the organization, and a precedent search that returns the title of any grievance of the organization, without holding the case or being assigned to it; forCaseId of a precedent search is never checked against the organization.

computeMemberEngagement has no caller in the application or in any other package, so the engagement route and the disengaged-member counts of the executive summary and key indicators read a store that nothing writes, and report an empty list and zero counts with status 200 as if they were measurements.

The workload route returns, for every active steward of the organization, a burnout signal, utilization ratio and recommended reassignments to any steward, so a steward reads a colleague burnout signal and caseload that no source says the colleague or the union agreed to share.

The key-indicator snapshot computes estimated admin hours saved and a dollar return from constants (hours saved per precedent retrieval, per early warning and per reassignment, and a loaded hourly rate), not from measured time; the route comment calls the artefact the one handed to buyers, so an assumption is presented as a result.

The cognition health route reports the platform engine registry, ontology and contract versions and engine counts per domain to any officer of any organization; platform runtime posture is a platform operator concern and no source names which organization role may see it.

Meetings, minutes, decisions, attendance, action items and documents of every committee are readable by any member of the organization, because every read sits at the member role floor and nothing consults committee_memberships; a closed or sensitive committee has no confidentiality.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The five committee read routes (meetings, meeting detail, attendance, action items, documents) require the committee to be the organization's and the reader to be staff or an active member of that committee; any other member gets the not-found answer. Tests cover staff, an active member, an outsider, no identity and another organization's committee.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The committee directory entry itself stays readable by every member (without notes), and the minutes read is steward-level but not checked against membership.

records.title: Attendee member ids, action item assignees, document ids and document file URLs are accepted from the body and stored without being checked against the organization membership, the document register or an allowed storage host, so a record can name a person or file that does not belong to the organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Attendance member ids and an action-item assignee must be current members of the organization (400, nothing written), and a linked documentId must be a document of the organization (404). Existing committee tests pass.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: A linked fileUrl is still accepted from the body without a storage-host allow-list.

records.title: The generic meeting update excludes only minutes and their approval fields, so the recorded decisions, the agenda items and the meeting status of a meeting whose minutes were approved can still be rewritten by a steward; the approved record is not frozen.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A meeting update that touches decisions, agenda items, agenda or status is conditional on the minutes not yet being approved; when they are, the update answers 409 (404 only for a missing meeting). Other fields (location, link) stay editable. Existing committee tests pass; a source-contract test pins the predicate.

records.title: The user who recorded the minutes may also approve them, because approval needs only the officer floor, which includes every higher role, and no check compares the approver with the recorder.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0038 adds committee_meetings.minutes_recorded_by and a check that the approver is not the recorder. Recording the minutes stores the recorder and approval refuses that person (403); a meeting recorded before the column existed falls back to its last editor.

records.title: A synthesis requested for one committee with no committeeIds in the body gathers the completed minutes of every committee of the organization and files the result under the committee in the path, so the minutes of committees the requester may not follow are summarized into another committee record.
The meeting and intelligence list routes pass parseInt of the limit and offset query strings straight to the query: there is no maximum, and a value that is not a number reaches the database as NaN.
The committee row returned to every member includes the notes and customFields columns and the contact e-mail, which no source marks as steward-only.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The committee routes omit the internal notes and custom fields from every response.

records.title: The intelligence POST stores and returns a snapshot whose summary reads Full AI synthesis pending integration, with empty themes, positions and recommendations and a null model, as a successful 200 result, so a stored placeholder is presented as a synthesis.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: POST stored a snapshot whose summary said synthesis was pending and whose themes, positions and recommendations were empty. It checks authority and then answers 501; nothing is stored. The snapshot list is unchanged.

records.title: The generic campaign create and update accept any body field, including status, sentAt, completedAt and the stats counters, so a steward can record a campaign as sent or completed and set its delivery and open figures by hand; no state machine or delivery process owns those fields.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A campaign create accepts author fields only, and a PATCH blocks status, send times, delivery statistics and the audience count; campaigns are read at the steward floor because they carry segment queries and bodies.

records.title: A campaign row stores a segment id, a free-form segment query and an audience count, and no route in the campaign group evaluates the audience, checks the communication preferences or consent of a recipient, or sends; authoring is detached from the consent and delivery rules the platform keeps elsewhere.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The schedule and send-test paths answer 501: they were the campaign row under another name and no sender reads them, so nothing was scheduled or tested.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: There is still no delivery path that checks consent before sending a campaign.

records.title: The campaign analytics, schedule and send-test paths are the generic campaign item route: analytics returns the campaign row and no analytics, schedule is an unvalidated update of the same row, send-test sends nothing, and a DELETE of any of the three archives the campaign.
message_templates has no status column, so the fixed administrator delete removes a template permanently; campaigns that referenced it lose the link (set null) and no source names a retention rule.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: No schema change was needed: the tables already carry is_active. The shared CRUD factory gains archiveColumn, so DELETE archives the template (is_active false, audited) instead of removing it, and the collections list active templates only. The B53 retain-on-delete pin was replaced by an archive pin (disclosed).

records.title: The template duplicate path is the generic template item route: GET returns the template, PATCH rewrites it and DELETE removes it, and nothing duplicates a template.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The duplicate path was the generic CRUD item over message templates (its DELETE removed the template and nothing was duplicated); it answers 501 and the roster-facade ratchet pins it.

records.title: newsletter_distribution_lists has no status column, so the fixed administrator delete removes the list permanently, and newsletter_list_subscribers deletes with it (on delete cascade), erasing the subscribed, unsubscribed and unsubscribedAt rows that are the suppression and consent trail of the list.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: DELETE of a distribution list now archives it (is_active false), so the cascade that erased the subscribed, unsubscribed and unsubscribe-reason trail can no longer fire through the API; the collection lists active lists only.

records.title: The subscriber list route returns the whole subscriber row, with e-mail address and profile id, of an organization list to any member of the organization, and records no audit of the disclosure.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Distribution lists and their subscriber e-mail addresses are read at the steward floor, and the subscriber list is bounded to 5000 rows. Test disclosure: the subscribers route test's mock chain gained limit.

records.title: The SMS message, campaign and conversation creates insert the body as a row, including status, twilioSid, price, sent and delivered times and counts, and send nothing: the Twilio send lives in a service that no route of the group imports, so a steward records messages as sent and delivered that were never sent.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The SMS message, campaign and conversation collections keep their officer-floor read, and their POST (which inserted rows carrying status, provider id, price and delivery times for messages never sent) now answers 501 and writes nothing. Contract test pins the read and the refusal.

records.title: Callers below steward are held to their own rows by the low-role guard, but any steward reads the phone number and message text of every member conversation of the organization, without holding the member case.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: SMS messages and conversations are read and written at the officer floor.

records.title: sms_campaigns has no owner or personal column, so the low-role guard leaves it open: any member of the organization reads every SMS campaign with its message text, recipient filter and total cost.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: SMS campaigns are read and written at the officer floor.

records.title: The conversation read path is the generic SMS message collection route: it ignores the conversation id, GET lists every message of the organization, and POST inserts a message row; nothing marks a conversation read.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The conversation read path no longer lists every message of the organization or inserts a message row: both methods answer 501 at the officer floor. The F07 read-authority contract test listed this path among the CRUD floors and was adjusted to drop it (disclosed); the new test pins the 501.

records.title: Open and click tracking read the campaign stats object, add one in the handler and write the whole object back as separate statements under the system role, so concurrent events lose counts and the system-role writes leave no audit record.

The unsubscribe route updates the message log, the campaign stats, the communication preference and the consent record as separate statements with no transaction, so a failure part-way leaves a recipient marked unsubscribed in one table and subscribed in another.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The message log, campaign stats, preference, list subscriptions and consent record are written on the one transaction handed to the callback (they used the shared connection, so there was no transaction at all). The unit-test mocks were adapted to pass the mock db as the transaction and to include the newsletter tables, and the real-SQL pglite test now creates those tables and still passes (disclosed).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The public GET still changes state; it is guarded by a signed, action-bound token.

records.title: A link without a campaign id updates the recipient communication preferences of every organization but writes no consent_records row, so the revocation has no evidentiary record and no organization attribution.

The unsubscribe route changes the campaign message log, the preference and the consent record and never touches newsletter_list_subscribers, so a member who unsubscribes from a campaign link stays subscribed on the distribution lists.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A campaign-link unsubscribe also marks the recipient subscriptions to the distribution lists of that organization unsubscribed, in the same transaction. Proven on real SQL (pglite) not to fail; contract test pins the update.

records.title: polls is READ_ONLY and poll_votes is DENIED in the CRUD governance table, so no route of the group can create a poll or record or read a vote; the member poll capability exists in schema and URL shape and cannot run through any of these routes.
The poll item path is configured as a collection route, so GET ignores the poll id and lists every poll of the organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The poll item route was mounting the collection handlers (GET and POST), so no poll could be read, changed or removed by id; it is now an item route on [pollId] with the same lifecycle guard, and the vote totals are blocked from PATCH.

records.title: The generic survey create and update accept any body field, including status, publishedAt, closesAt, responseCount, viewCount and completionRate, so the published state and the response counters are set by hand and not derived from the responses.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A survey moves draft, then active or published, then closed, never backwards; the server stamps the publication time once; response counts, views and completion are never client-written and a new survey cannot be created already published.

records.title: The survey list and item reads sit at the member floor and apply no status or publication filter, so a draft survey is readable by every member of the organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The generic factory gained belowStaffReadCondition, applied to GET for a caller below the steward floor. Surveys add status != draft, so a member reads published surveys only; staff still read drafts.

records.title: The survey response read returns respondent name, e-mail, user id, IP address and user agent of every response to any steward, whatever the survey allowAnonymous setting says; an anonymous survey is not anonymous.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The responses route exports POST only and its header states no individual identity, address or response row is returned to a steward; no read exposes respondents (upstream's change).

records.title: The responses route ignores the survey id of its path: GET lists the responses of every survey of the organization, and POST takes surveyId from the body and checks nothing about the survey, so a response is accepted for a draft or closed survey, a second response is accepted when allowMultipleResponses is false, and authentication is not required when the survey says it is.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the response create verifies the survey belongs to the caller organization, is active and open, and strips respondent identity for an anonymous survey; the list is a count-only steward read of the path survey.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The POST still takes the survey id from the body rather than the path.

records.title: No route under app/api writes survey_answers, and the results route is the only one that reads the table, so a response can be created and no answer can be recorded; the survey capability cannot be completed through these routes.

The survey results route filters responses and questions by the survey id of the path and applies no organization predicate, does not request a tenant context, and also selects every row of survey_answers of every organization into memory and discards it; the isolation of the count and the question list rests on an ambient database policy the route does not set, and the full-table read is a cross-tenant read of answer text.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The survey, its responses and its questions are all read with the caller's organization predicate (upstream's change, existing test).

records.title: The certifications/generate, certifications/renewal-reminders, completions/certificates and notification-preferences paths are the training_courses generic CRUD under action-sounding names: they generate no certificate, send no reminder, list no certificate and store no preference, and a POST creates a course.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Certificate generation, renewal reminders, completion certificates and notification preferences were the training-course factory; all answer 501. The admin certification manager that posts to renewal-reminders now receives the 501 instead of a course row.

records.title: The programs/[id]/enrollments and sessions/[id]/attendance item routes read the path id as a training_courses id, so no program enrollment or session attendance is read or written: PATCH rewrites any course field and the administrator DELETE removes the course row permanently because the table has no status column.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The program enrolment item answers 501 for every method, so a program id can no longer rewrite or delete a training course.

records.title: The completions route is described as completed registrations only but is configured with no completed condition: GET returns every course_registrations row of the caller and POST inserts any registration, completed or not.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The completions list reads only completed registrations of the caller's organization.

records.title: The completions POST writes course_registrations through the factory with no beforeCreate hook, so it skips the organization checks on courseId and sessionId that the registrations route added, and a steward can insert a registration for any member id that references a course or session of another organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A completion is a locked transition of an existing registration of the organization that must be attended and passed, audited in the same transaction; nothing is inserted (existing implementation, now pinned).

records.title: The registrations, completions and certifications collection reads add memberId equal to the session user id at every role, including steward and administrator, while a steward POST can create rows for any member id: no office can list or verify the training records of another member, and the creating steward cannot read the row back.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The factory gained staffReadsAll: with an owner column, a steward or above reads every member's registration or certification on GET while a member keeps their own; writes keep the owner scope.

records.title: The registrations POST is open to a member and its beforeCreate hook forces only memberId, so the member body also stores completed, passed, finalGrade, certificateIssued, certificateNumber, approvedBy, feePaid and feeWaived on their own registration.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A registration forces the member identity and the registered state and ignores every client-sent completion, payment, attendance, grade, certification and subsidy field; its course and session must belong to the organization (upstream's change, existing test).

records.title: The registrations POST checks only that courseId and sessionId exist in the organization: it does not check that the session belongs to the course, that registration is open, that the session has capacity, or that the member is not already registered, and it does not update the session registration count.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0040 adds a unique index (organization, member, session) that refuses to apply over existing duplicates, and a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that locks the session row and refuses a registration beyond max_enrollment (SQLSTATE 23514); a cancelled place frees a seat and a re-save of a registered row is not recounted. The CRUD factory gains mapCreateError so a lost race answers 409 (full, or already registered). Proven on PGlite.

records.title: The sessions GET returns every column of every session of the organization to any member, including the virtual meeting URL and access code, session budget, actual cost, accommodation hotel and internal notes of sessions the member is not registered for.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A session read omits the virtual-meeting access code and the session budget and actual cost (existing implementation, pinned by the F07 contract test).

records.title: The sessions POST stores courseId from the body without checking that the course belongs to the session organization, and the registration, attendance and completion counters and the average rating are plain body-writable columns, so a steward can attach a session to another organization course and write its statistics.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The training session create checks that the course is the organization own (shared reference helper, 404 otherwise) and accepts only an allow-list of descriptive fields: registration, waitlist, attendance, completion, rating, evaluation, cost, status and cancellation figures are no longer body-writable. Contract test pins the allow-list and the check.

records.title: The certifications POST is a free-form insert: courseId, sessionId and registrationId are optional, nothing checks that the member completed anything, and verified defaults to true, so a steward can create a verified certification, including its verifier, revocation and badge fields, with no link to a completed course.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A certification is created only from a completed, passed registration of the organization for a course that issues one, as a pending candidate with no verifier, verification date, badge or certificate URL (upstream's change). Only a source contract pins it; the route has no behavioural test.

records.title: course_code, session_code and certification_number are unique across all organizations rather than within one, so a code used by one organization makes another organization insert fail and the conflict reveals that the code exists.

The education admin screens call operations the route files do not export or do not perform: POST on the attendance and enrollments item routes that export only GET, PATCH and DELETE, PATCH and DELETE with an id query on the session, program and certification collection routes that export only GET and POST, and renewal reminders on a route that runs the course create, so the screens cannot mark attendance, enroll, edit or delete sessions, programs and certifications, or send reminders, and ignored filters (memberId, sessionStatus, includeProgress) return unfiltered rows.

Both reminder queries name columns the training schema does not define (course_sessions session_date, session_time, location and duration_hours; member_certifications certificate_number; training_courses continuing_education_hours) and compare the boolean provides_certification to a certification name, so against the declared schema the job fails at its first query and sends nothing; the route test mocks the database and cannot show it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both reminder statements now name only columns the training schema declares (start_date, venue, lead_instructor_name, certification_number, the organization_members row that carries the name and e-mail) and join every table on the organization; they run against tables created from the declared schema, with positive and negative cases (cancelled, inactive, revoked, other organization). Route test adapted only to the new row field names.

records.title: The reminder job selects every registered member and every expiring certification holder across all organizations without consulting communication preferences or consent, and records no sent marker, so a member who opted out is still e-mailed and a second run on the same day sends the same reminder again.

The reminder job returns success true and the message "Education reminders processed successfully" whatever the counts, so a run in which every send failed (including an unconfigured e-mail service) reads as success, and the failure list in the response carries member e-mail addresses.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A run with failed session-reminder or expiry-warning sends answers 500 through jobResponse naming the failed batch, with the sent/failed counts and collected errors in the body; the message no longer claims success. The route writes nothing, so it is classified as a read-only POST for the audit ratchet.

records.title: The reminder job sends one message at a time with a 100 ms pause and no cap on recipients, across every organization in one request, so the run time grows with the member count and has no resume point if the request is cut off.

The content training list and the content statistics report completions as the number of registrations with attended true, not completed true, so a member who attended without finishing counts as a completion and the figure shown to every member does not match the completed flag of the registration.

The content training list has no row limit, and the content templates list takes its limit from the query string with no upper bound and no validation, so a caller can request an arbitrarily large page and a negative value reaches the database as a SQL error.

The content templates GET returns cms_pages rows of every status (draft, review, archived and published) to any member of the organization, with the author user id, and ignores the allowed_roles restriction of the row, although the status workflow reserves drafting to content managers and publishing to administrators.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A member reads only active courses; draft and archived ones are visible to staff.

records.title: The content status transition checks the role for each step but not who prepared the item, so one administrator can move an item from draft through review to published alone, and republishing rewrites published_at.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0038 adds cms_pages.submitted_by. Moving an item to review records who did it, and publication is refused for that person, with the last-editor fallback only for earlier rows. Existing status tests pass.

records.title: The remittance run detail route is open to any member of the organization, takes no financial mandate and reads through the shared db import instead of an explicit withRLSContext call, and returns the run, its items and every artifact of the run, including the stored remittance CSV and JSON whose content holds the external employee id with gross pay, dues, benefit, pension and net pay of every employee; the payroll run detail beside it requires the secretary_treasurer role and a live view mandate, and the dashboard layout restricts the whole area to administrators.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The remittance run detail needs the financial roles and a live view mandate for the run, reads inside one tenant RLS transaction, and returns only the evidence manifest, never the stored CSV or JSON (existing implementation, now pinned).

records.title: The replay route checks the secretary_treasurer role and the replay entitlement only and never calls requireLiveFinancialMandate, so it neither requires a live financial mandate nor limits the run to the records a view grant names, yet it reads every payroll item of any run of the organization, returns per-employee gross, net, dues, benefit and pension differences, and appends evidence artifacts; prepare, approve, execute, view and remittance all require a mandate.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A replay first requires a live financial view mandate for the run (resource-scoped, as the run detail does) and only then reads any payroll item. Tests adapted: assertions that no transaction was opened now assert that nothing is written, because the mandate check is itself a transaction; the not-found test asserts the mandate was requested. New test: a role holder with no mandate is refused before any read.

records.title: Every replay request inserts a new replay row, three evidence artifacts attached to the source run, an evidence link and, when the replay differs, an open error-severity inconsistent_replay_results event against the source run, with no idempotency key and no unique replay key; approveRun counts open error events for the run and refuses approval until each is acknowledged, so repeated or deliberately different replays, which any caller of the replay route can request at any run status, add approval blockers and evidence rows to the run they only read.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A replay identical in run, mode, rule version, engine version and result is answered with the replay already made, adding no replay row, artifacts, evidence link, compliance event or audit duplicate; a different requested mode is a new replay. Tests added for both.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: A genuinely different replay still opens an error-severity event that must be acknowledged before approval; whether a replay should gate approval is a payroll-governance decision, and replays are still allowed at any run status.

records.title: The replay mode enum holds only exact and simulated, and the route stores simulated for new_rule and exact for both exact and new_engine, so a replay under a different engine version is recorded as an exact replay and the stored mode cannot tell an engine change from a faithful re-run.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0040 adds new_engine to employer_execution_replay_mode, so an engine-change replay is stored as new_engine and not as a faithful exact re-run. Proven on PGlite; the requested mode still travels with the diff for idempotency.

records.title: The seal action of the payroll run PATCH route, named execute in its mandate action and in its audit and compliance record ("Official payroll run executed (posted)"), only sets status posted, executor and timestamp on the run: no ledger entry, payment, deduction or remittance is written, and the remittance route refuses a run that is no longer approved, so a posted run reads as executed while nothing was done with its amounts.

Timesheet ingest never writes member_employment_id or job_classification_id on an entry, payroll preparation therefore opens a blocking critical missing_employment_mapping event for every official run, approveRun refuses approval while a critical blocking event is open, and no route of the employer execution API sets the mapping or resolves a critical event, so an official payroll run cannot reach approval through this API.

The evidence seal of payroll, remittance and replay evidence is sha256 of the entity type, run id and manifest hash with no key, signature or external anchor, stored as an artifact named evidence-seal.sig beside the manifest it covers, and the chain verification compares stored parent seal hashes and depths only and never recomputes a manifest or seal hash, so anyone able to write the artifact rows can rewrite a chain that still verifies.

Payroll preparation stores the period from the request body instead of the period of the validated timesheet batch, derives the rule version from the first entry shift date, reads the batch and the already-approved check through the shared connection outside the transaction that inserts the run, takes no lock, and names the run with a millisecond timestamp under a non-unique run code index, so two concurrent requests both pass the check and both create official runs for one batch.

The remittance CSV writes the external employee id taken from the uploaded timesheet file into the first column with no quoting and no neutralisation of a leading formula character, and the three remittance items (dues, benefits, pension) each report the number of payroll items as their member count, even when the amount of the group is zero, so the package can carry spreadsheet formulas and member counts the data does not support.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The uploaded external employee id is neutralised against a leading formula character and quoted in the remittance CSV, and each remittance group reports the number of members who contribute to it rather than the payroll item count.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The per-group member count is pinned by source only; no behavioural test drives the remittance route with a zero-amount group.

records.title: Any steward can ingest the timesheet file whose rows become the dues, benefit and pension amounts of a payroll run, with no financial mandate and a role floor below the secretary_treasurer role the later duties need; the csv content and the employee external ids are unbounded free text that is never matched to a member or employment record, and the parser splits on commas without quoting.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The list is officer-level and bounded to 200 batches; a new batch needs calendar dates in order, a file name of at most 255 characters and a CSV of at most 2,000,000 characters. Its employer, worksite and unit references were already checked against the organization.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The ingest still sits at the steward floor rather than a financial mandate, and no behavioural test of the route exists (contract test only).

records.title: A steward can persist a compliance event with any event code, severity, summary, details and blocking flag against any payroll or remittance run of the organization, with no financial mandate; the codes are free text, so an event can imitate one the system raises, and an open critical blocking event or an open error event stops approveRun, while no route in this API resolves a critical event.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Raising a compliance event is a financial-role act; a manual flag may be info or warning only, can never block an approval, cannot take an engine event code (it is prefixed manual_), and its summary and code are bounded; unknown body fields are refused.

records.title: The compliance event list and the timesheet batch list are open to any member of the organization, unbounded and unpaged, without a financial mandate: they return every compliance event with its details JSON and every batch with the uploader id, file name and validation summary, although the dashboard layout restricts the area to administrators and the payroll run reads require a mandate.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The compliance event list moves from the member floor to the financial roles and is bounded to 500 rows; the payroll and remittance run lists already require the financial roles and a live view mandate.

records.title: Any steward reads, unbounded and without a read audit record, the names, e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, notes and custom fields of every employer representative in the organization, through the employer rows (primary and labour-relations contacts, business numbers, notes, customFields) and the employer contacts list.

The employer create and update accept parentCompanyId from the body through the generic factory, and the column is a foreign key to employers.id with no organization condition, so an employer of one organization can name an employer of another organization as its parent company, and the foreign key outcome tells the caller whether that id exists.

The employer delete sets status archived only: archivedAt stays empty and nothing checks the employer for open timesheet batches, contacts or communications, and the timesheet ingest looks the employer up by id and organization without testing its status, so an archived employer keeps receiving payroll input.

The communications POST route only inserts a row: it imports and calls no mail, SMS, letter or notification provider, takes the status from the caller, stamps sentAt when the caller says sent, hard-codes the sender name System, and then emits the employer.communication_sent audit event, so a record of type email with status sent reads as a delivered message although nothing was sent.

The communications POST route stores employerId, grievanceId, recipientContactId and templateId from the body without checking that any of them belongs to the organization, although the contacts route verifies its employer; employer_id has no foreign key, grievance_id and recipient_contact_id are foreign keys with no organization condition, so a communication can be attached to another organization grievance or contact, or to an employer that does not exist.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Logging an employer communication checks employerId, grievanceId, recipientContactId and templateId against the caller organization before any write (404, nothing written or audited), and the list is limited to 200. The existing route test mock gained the limit step and a new test covers a foreign grievance (disclosed).

records.title: Any steward of the organization lists every employer communication, subject and body included, with the grievance each is linked to, unbounded and without holding the grievance or a case office, so grievance correspondence is readable beyond the stewards who represent the member.

After the transaction that commits the row and its atomic audit record, the contacts and communications POST routes emit a second audit event through auditLog; in the canonical state that write appends the audit chain row through its own withRLSContext call and does not swallow a failure, so the route catches it and returns a 500 although the row is already committed, and the contacts event carries the contact name in its details.

The contacts POST route stores isPrimary from the body and clears no other contact of the employer, and the table has no unique primary-contact rule, so an employer can hold many primary contacts and a consumer cannot tell which one is current.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0038 adds a partial unique index so an employer has at most one active primary contact; it refuses to apply over an employer that already has two. The create keeps its in-transaction demotion and answers a lost race with 409. Proven on PGlite, including the refusal over existing duplicates.
