records.title: The audit log read returns every column of the latest hundred audit rows of the organization (IP address, user agent, session and correlation ids, old and new values, error text and metadata) to any officer, ignores the limit the page sends, offers no filter or page and is itself not audited.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The organization audit-log list names eight columns (who, what, which resource, severity, outcome, time) and no longer serves the captured old and new values, network address, user agent, session and correlation ids, metadata, error text or archive path. The read is still audited in the same transaction.

records.title: An administrator writes entries into the audit trail with a free resource type, a resource id and metadata keys that are not checked against any record of the organization; the entry is marked compliance.manual_entry but shares the trail and the table with system-recorded actions.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A manual entry is recorded as compliance.manual_entry attributed to the administrator who wrote it, with the declared fields kept as untrusted details, so it cannot pass for a system record (upstream's change, existing test).

records.title: Any member of the organization reads every commercial contract of the organization (value, signer, billing account and subscription ids, renewal and termination terms) and the priced line items of any contract through an unbounded full-row select, behind a module entitlement and a member role floor; no office is named for contract terms.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Contract list and line items are read at the officer floor.

records.title: The contract create takes billingAccountId and subscriptionId from the body and inserts them without checking that they belong to the organization, so a contract can be bound to another tenant billing account or subscription; the contract and line items also accept caller-set prices and a total contract value as free text.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A contract create checks that its billing account and subscription belong to the caller's organization (400 malformed, 404 otherwise) before anything is written; a contract provisions entitlements from its lines.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Contract line items still provision entitlements from administrator-typed feature keys with no catalogue check.

records.title: createContract calls auditLog inside its transaction, but auditLog writes through its own connection and logs a failed write without throwing, so the contract and its line items can commit with no audit record, or the audit record can remain after a rollback.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Contract create, activate and terminate write their audit record in the same transaction (persistAtomicAudit) instead of a separate best-effort logger call. Test disclosure: the service test now mocks persistAtomicAudit in place of the logger.

records.title: The compliance alert and report reads catch every error and answer success with an empty list, so a failed query is reported to the steward as no alerts and no reports.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A failed alert or report query answers 500 instead of an empty success, and both lists are bounded to 500 rows.

records.title: No route, service or job inserts into compliance_alerts or employer_reports, so the alert and report reads, and the compliance metrics the leadership dashboard computes from the alerts, are over tables that nothing populates.
The alert and report lists have no limit or page, and the report list returns the whole free-form JSON document of every report of every employer of the organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The alert and report lists return at most 500 rows (the failure answer was fixed in B33).

records.title: The validate route returns compliant, warning and violation verdicts with a severity and a recommendation computed only from dates and counts the caller sends in the body; nothing is checked against a grievance, vote or certification record, nothing is persisted or audited, and any authenticated user with an organization may obtain a verdict.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The strike-vote and certification checks no longer return compliant, warning or violation from numbers the caller typed against thresholds written into the route; each reports the arithmetic, says no validated rule is configured and that the figures are unchecked, as info. Test disclosure: one test added; the existing tests did not assert a verdict.

records.title: The arbitration deadline falls back to a literal thirty days when its rules lookup returns nothing, the lookup is an unauthenticated self-call whose failure is swallowed by an empty catch, the strike vote quorum is a literal fifty percent without a legal reference and the certification card thresholds are literals for three jurisdictions, with no check at all for any other.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The literal thresholds are removed and there is no rule lookup to swallow.

records.title: The validate body is cast to an interface and never parsed: a schema is declared in the file and is not used, dates are passed to Date without a validity check, and an unknown jurisdiction or check name yields no check and no error.

The employer data firewall policy table is readable by every member and has no write path (the CRUD governance table refuses writes), and no service reads its block flags to withhold strike plans, membership lists or internal discussions from employer-facing paths.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route served a table no route writes and nothing enforces under the name of an employer data firewall. It answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed. The writeRole test for the route was rewritten to assert the 501 and the absence of the table binding, and the committed schema mutation program was regenerated because the table is now unreachable from any route.

records.title: The COPE campaign, canvassing and officials routes are one generic CRUD factory over donation_campaigns under three political names; no political campaign, canvassing or official table is reachable from the application schema, so the interfaces that call the routes receive donation rows without the fields they render.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: cope/canvassing and cope/officials served donation-campaign rows; they answer 501. cope/campaigns, the legitimate campaign collection, is unchanged. The canvassing interface component now receives the 501.

records.title: A steward creates a campaign row through the generic factory with any body field, including currentAmount (funds raised), status and the payment product and price identifiers, and any member reads those rows.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A campaign body is limited to an allow-list; the amount raised, the status and the payment-provider identifiers can no longer be set by a steward.

records.title: The assignment inserts any member uuid from the body without checking that it belongs to the organization or is eligible, into a table with no organization column that cannot be scoped to a tenant afterwards, and the request create stores any employer uuid without checking it is an employer of the organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Dispatch assignment verifies the request and every worker id against the organization with the request locked, proven on real SQL (batch B12).

records.title: The assignment ignores the status of the request and the assignments it already has: a cancelled, expired or filled request accepts more assignments and has its status rewritten, the same member can be offered twice, and filled is derived from the length of the one posted list.

The seniority, rotation, availability and skills ranking and the organization rules table exist, but no route calls the ranking and no route writes a rule, so the assignment is whatever member list the officer posts and the fairness the hall model describes is not applied.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: An assignment accepted any member ids for a request in any state, in any number, with no check that they were members, and counted the request filled from the ids of one call. It now requires an open or partly filled request of the caller's organization (row locked), active members of that organization, no worker already offered or placed, and no more offers than workers requested, with a distinct status for each refusal. Proven on real SQL. Three mock-chain tests of assignWorkersToDispatch were removed because the mocks cannot express these queries; the pglite suite replaces them.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: rankCandidates still scores a candidate list nothing supplies (no source of member skills or availability), and the assignment is an officer's explicit selection, not engine-ranked.

records.title: When the stats query fails the route logs the error and answers 200 with every count at zero, so a database failure reads on the dashboard as an organization with no claims and no members.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A failed query is an error and the member count is null for an ordinary member, not zero; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

records.title: The leadership compliance metrics report deadline adherence and documentation rate as 100 when there are no alerts, and nothing writes alerts; the grievance aggregates silently stop at the first five thousand rows and the alerts at one thousand; the figures are cached per organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Deadline adherence and documentation rate are null, not 100, when there is nothing to measure, and the card shows a dash in a neutral colour. The empty-input service test pinned the 100 and was changed to expect null (disclosed).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: No code inserts compliance alerts, and the grievance aggregates still stop at the first 5000 rows.

records.title: The CSV export is guarded by authentication alone, with no organization, role or entitlement, and its data source is not wired: production answers 501, every other environment answers 200 with an empty file; once wired the case export would carry case ids, assignees and worksites with no organization predicate in the route.

currentRun.repair: Removed the authentication-only CSV handler and its fabricated empty 200 responses in nonproduction. The route now requires admin eligibility plus an active organization context and explicitly refuses export with no-store HTTP 501 until a real scoped data source and governed export exist.
currentRun.limits: This is security and truthfulness containment, not a working CSV export. Institutional export mandate, tenant-scoped query, row bounds, atomic audit, formula neutralization, PG15/16, and real HTTP/browser acceptance remain open.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The export answers 501 in every environment; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

records.title: The enterprise data subject request route is the generic factory over a subject-owned table with no owner column, so every read and write is refused with a 403 that names a dedicated route, and the dedicated privacy route answers 501; no request can be received, and the table has no organization column to scope a request to the institution that must answer it.

The enterprise integrations route is the generic factory over oauth_providers, a per-user table of provider account ids and access and refresh tokens with no organization column, under a name that advertises an organization integration list; the governance table denies it, so it serves nothing, and lifting that denial would expose tokens at the member floor.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: enterprise/integrations was the generic factory over oauth_providers (per-user provider ids and tokens, no organization); it answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed with its last binding.

records.title: The generic CRUD route declares orgScoped true over a table that has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate and every row of the table is visible to every organization once the read is allowed; the declared scope is a no-op.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Org-scoped generic routes without organizationId or a declared parentScope now fail during route construction instead of silently omitting tenant filtering.

records.title: The debug user-role route has no environment guard: it is the generic factory over organization_members, so it returns the roster rows of the organization (name, e-mail, phone, role, hire date, membership number, exemption reason) to a steward or above, and the caller own full row to a member, instead of a role check.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The debug route answers 501 and returns no roster rows (batch B09), pinned by the facade contract test.

records.title: The Resend webhook looks the event up by provider message id and, when no message_log row carries it, logs a warning and still answers 200, so the provider does not retry and the delivery, bounce or complaint event is lost; an event that arrives before the sender has stored the provider message id is lost the same way.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: An event matching neither a message_log row nor a delivery-ledger row answers 404 retryable so the provider redelivers (covering an event that beats the sender storing the provider message id); a redelivery after the row exists applies it. Both are tested against PostgreSQL (pglite).

records.title: The webhook sets message_log.status to the status of whichever event arrives last with no ordering rule, so a late sent, delivered or opened event overwrites a bounced, failed or complained status, and it updates in place a table whose schema comment declares it an immutable delivery log with no updatedAt.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Status only advances to a higher rank (a late sent, delivered or opened never overwrites bounced, failed or complained); fact timestamps are filled when missing; existing metadata is preserved. The table comment no longer claims the log is immutable and states the real rule. Mutation-proved.

records.title: The Svix message id is used only as a detail of the delivery-ledger row: the failed, unsubscribed and complained branches increment the campaign statistics on every redelivery of the same event, and the statistics are rewritten as a whole object from a value read earlier in the transaction, so a retry or a concurrent event changes the counters wrongly.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Each statistic counts a message at most once (a counted set persisted in message_log.metadata, seeded from timestamps and terminal status for older rows), and the campaign counters advance inside the UPDATE (jsonb || jsonb_build_object over the stored value) rather than from a value read earlier. Tested with redelivery and with a counter another writer already advanced. Mutation-proved.

records.title: A complaint or suppression event updates the existing communication_preferences row of the one organization and recipient on the message log row, never inserts one and never writes a consent record or touches the distribution-list subscriptions, so a recipient with no preference row stays emailable while the audit record says the suppression was applied, and the same address is not suppressed in any other organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A complaint or suppression now creates the preference row when none exists, writes a revoked consent record and the audit entry, and applies once per message in the same transaction.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Suppression is still scoped to the one organization on the message row; suppressing the same address in other organizations and in distribution-list subscriptions needs a cross-organization address-suppression design.

records.title: The delivery-ledger callback runs after the message_log transaction has committed and its result (recorded, duplicate, unmatched, ambiguous) is ignored, so a ledger failure answers 500 after the message_log, statistics and suppression have already changed and the provider retry repeats them, and an unmatched or ambiguous ledger event is acknowledged without a trace.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: recordProviderCallback takes the caller's transaction (inserting inside a savepoint so a duplicate does not abort it); the webhook runs it in the same transaction as the message row, so a ledger failure rolls everything back and the retry repeats nothing. An unmatched or ambiguous ledger result is logged, and an event matching nothing is retried. Rollback proved with a failing audit write.

records.title: message_log.provider_message_id has neither an index nor a unique constraint, yet every webhook event selects by it with limit 1 under the system role, so each event scans the table and, if two rows ever carried the same id, the organization that receives the event is arbitrary.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 20261031 creates a unique (provider, provider_message_id) index when no pair repeats, otherwise a plain index with the duplicate count reported; both branches and idempotence executed on PostgreSQL (pglite). The webhook locks the row (FOR UPDATE) and refuses with 409 when two rows carry the id. Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

records.title: The public contact route has no local store: it forwards the submission to HubSpot and answers ok true even when HUBSPOT_API_KEY is unset or the upsert fails (both return null and the handler skips the deal), so a visitor is told the message was received when no record of it exists anywhere but a log line that omits the message text.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The contact form answers 503 instead of ok when the CRM did not record the contact or the message, so a visitor is no longer told it was received when nothing recorded it.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: There is still no local store: a submission exists only in HubSpot, and an unconfigured CRM refuses every contact submission.

records.title: The only control on the public contact route is a 20-per-hour limit keyed on cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip or the first x-forwarded-for value, all request headers a caller can set unless an edge strips them, and the route has no captcha, honeypot or origin check, so a script can rotate the header and flood the CRM with contacts and deals.

Only the message field has a length bound on the public contact form: first name, last name, organization, role and inquiry type are unbounded strings forwarded to HubSpot (limited only by the 16 KiB body cap), and the visitor e-mail address and organization are written to the application log at info level.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Every contact field has a length bound (name 100, address 254, organization 200, role and inquiry type 100) and the visitor's address is no longer written to the log; tests cover an oversized field and the log content.

records.title: The continuity archives and docs paths are byte-identical wrappers that re-export the document repository handlers behind a placeholder requireOrgAccess that always returns true and a mutation boundary that only checks that a method string exists: no archive, retention, continuity-plan or succession behaviour exists behind the names, a POST uploads an ordinary document, and the dead unauthorized branch reads as an access check that is not there.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The inheritance, archives and docs aliases (the pending-profile table and the document repository behind a guard that always returned true) all answer 501; the document repository itself is reached at /api/documents/repository.

records.title: The document repository list that the continuity paths serve has no row limit and no page, returns every non-deleted document row of the organization joined to its links, then runs a case-access lookup for each grievance-linked row and applies the linkedCase filter and the visibility policy in memory, so the cost grows with the size of the organization document store.

The continuity inheritance path advertises succession records but is the generic CRUD factory over pending_profiles, the pre-signup profile table holding the e-mail, Whop membership id and usage credits, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every read and write answers 403 and no inheritance record can be read or written.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: continuity/inheritance answered the pre-signup pending_profiles table. It answers 501; the table is no longer bound, so its governance entry was removed (an unlisted table is refused by the fail-closed default). The route test that pinned the old factory configuration was rewritten to pin the 501.

records.title: The inheritance route sets orgScoped true over pending_profiles, which has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate; the support_agent read floor and the DENIED governance entry are the only barriers, and lifting the governance entry would list the pre-signup e-mail and payment identifiers of every organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The path no longer mounts the generic factory over pending_profiles; it answers 501 and exposes nothing (existing implementation and test).

records.title: The deprecation registry served to every member names canonical replacements that have no route (/api/billing/reports, /api/strike/fund and /api/messages/[id]), repeats the sunset instant 2026-07-07 as a literal instead of the SUNSET_DATE constant, promises removal after that instant although routes it lists (payments webhook stripe, messaging preferences, financial vendors) still exist, and gives no sign that the list is hand-maintained.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Seven registry rows named replacement routes that do not exist; they now name the real route (current-user, message thread, strike funds) or REMOVED with the reason. A test checks every named replacement against the route tree. A sunset date already past is no longer advertised in a Sunset header, and the body states that it has passed.

records.title: The document-intake reaper, external-data-sync, location-retention and monthly-per-capita handlers export the same function as GET and POST, so a GET (the method a scheduler, browser prefetch or monitoring probe issues) expires intakes, deletes stored objects and location data, calls external providers or writes per-capita remittances while the route manifest records the GET as a read.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: All four aliases export POST only; so do the other ten scheduled routes (codemod f01-cron-post-only.cjs, idempotent). A contract test fails if any manifest route exports a method other than POST.

records.title: No scheduler entry in the repository invokes the document-intake reaper, external-data-sync, monthly-per-capita, observability-alerts or sla-watchdog handlers: apps/union-eyes/vercel.json schedules only calendar-sync and the ue-v2 apps.bicep cron job calls only deadline-reminders, so the jobs run only if an operator wires a trigger outside the source.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The manifest declares all 18 scheduled routes; apps.bicep generates one Container Apps schedule job per entry (POST with the cron secret, curl -f so a non-2xx fails the run). Compiles with az bicep; the contract test fails when a cron route is missing from the manifest or the bicep stops reading it.

records.title: The two handlers listed in CRON_API_ROUTES (external-data-sync and monthly-per-capita) are first checked in proxy.ts against CRON_SECRET only with a plain !== comparison and the x-cron-secret header only, while the handler accepts CRON_SECRET_KEY first, a Bearer value too, and compares with timingSafeEqual; where only CRON_SECRET_KEY is set the edge refuses a correct caller, and the edge check is not constant time.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: One shared rule (x-cron-secret or bearer; CRON_SECRET_KEY then CRON_SECRET; unset never matches) used by withApi, verifyCronAuth, the rewards route and the edge check, which now compares in constant time over SHA-256 digests via WebCrypto (edge-safe) instead of !==. CRON_API_ROUTES is derived from the manifest.

records.title: The only scheduler entry for calendar-sync (vercel.json, every 15 minutes) names the path with no method or secret, while the route exports POST only and verifyCronAuth reads only the x-cron-secret header, so a trigger that issues GET or presents the secret as a Bearer value is refused and no connection is synced.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The vercel.json entry (no method, no secret) is removed; calendar-sync is scheduled as a POST Container Apps job every 15 minutes, and verifyCronAuth now accepts the secret as a bearer token as well as x-cron-secret.

records.title: The Google and Microsoft event import loops catch and discard the error of each event, and the cancelled-event handler discards its own error but the caller still adds one to the deleted count, so a failed event is missing from the local calendar while the connection is marked synced, the audit record reports the counts and the response shows no failure.

The Google import asks for at most 2500 events in one list call and never follows nextPageToken, and the cron never passes the stored sync token, so events beyond the first page are not imported while the connection is marked synced; the due list is selected without a lock or claim and nextSyncAt moves only at the end of each connection, so an overlapping run repeats the same provider calls.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The Google import follows every page (250 per call, 50-page bound that fails instead of truncating), the cron passes the stored sync token (without the window and ordering Google rejects with one), a 410 falls back to a full sync, and the new token is stored only when every page was read and every event applied; otherwise the import throws and the connection is recorded as failed with a retry time. Per-event and token-store errors are no longer swallowed. The due connections are locked FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and leased for 15 minutes in the same transaction, each lease bound to the row's organization. Google only: the Microsoft import has the same shape and is not yet changed.

records.title: The intake object finalizer selects only rows whose deletion_attempts are below INTAKE_MAX_DELETION_ATTEMPTS, so an abandoned object whose deletion keeps failing is never selected again after the limit, stays in storage, and the response reports only the failures of the current run.

The external-data-sync handler returns a plain object in every case, including the outer failure branch that sets success false, so the response is HTTP 200 whatever fails, and each sync method writes the external_data_sync_log row as completed even when records failed and never stores the collected error list, so the log does not show a partial or failed run.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The handler answers 500 for a run with any failed source and for the outer failure; every sync method writes the log row through syncLogOutcome: partial (not completed) when records failed, with the bounded collected error list in error_details.

records.title: syncContributionRates (and its sync-log rows) selects, updates and inserts through the plain tenant db handle while the wage, union-density and COLA methods run inside withSystemContext, so the contribution-rate part of the scheduled job runs without the system authority the other three parts were given and does not commit with a system transaction.

The 24-hour member location retention is enforced only by the location-retention handler, whose comments say it runs hourly, but no scheduler entry in the repository invokes it (vercel.json lists only calendar-sync and apps.bicep only deadline-reminders), so expired location points and geofence events are deleted only if an operator wires a trigger outside the source.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: location-retention is an hourly POST Container Apps job generated from the manifest.

records.title: The deletion log written by the retention job records the run time as both the oldest and the newest deleted record date instead of the real dates, carries no organization, no list of affected members and no audit_log record, and the location tables have no organization column, so the evidence of what was deleted cannot show whose data or from when.

The retention job loads every expired user id from both tables without a limit and deletes user by user inside one system transaction, so a backlog (for example after the job did not run) is one long transaction holding locks on the live location tables.

The monthly per-capita job inserts and recalculates per_capita_remittances rows and marks them overdue for every organization with a parent, while the capability registry records the affiliate remittance capability (UE-FIN-AFFILIATE-REMITTANCES) as NOT_IMPLEMENTED and asks for a qualified model with institutional recipients, so remittance amounts and overdue states are produced without that model or any named financial officer decision.

The per-capita handler returns success true whatever the counts, the calculation catch block drops an organization whose calculation failed without a log or a count, the save step counts a failed write in errors with no record of which organization, and the handler runs markOverdueRemittances a second time after processMonthlyPerCapita already ran it, so the top-level overdueMarked value is the second sweep (normally zero) rather than the number marked.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The calculation catch now records, logs and returns the failing organization; the save step returns the failing organization ids; the route answers 500 with counts and ids through jobResponse when any failed, and no longer runs markOverdueRemittances a second time.

records.title: The observability sweep writes each alert execution with status success, channels email and in_app and executionTimeMs 1, but the e-mail leg is only a notification_tracking row with status pending that no sender reads (notification-service names the table only in a comment and the process-notifications cron is a 501 stub), so the execution history shows an e-mail alert as delivered that was never sent.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The never-read pending notification_tracking row is no longer written and an execution records only the channel that delivered (in_app, with the recipient count) and its measured time. The alert goes to the organization's active administrators and president; an alert nobody can receive is a failed execution and a failed job (500), not a success. Reruns in the same hour alert nobody twice. No e-mail is sent or claimed; delivering alerts by e-mail is not part of this fix.

records.title: The in-app alert is addressed to the pseudo-user system:observability-alerts and the tracking row names no recipient, and the alert rule is created with no recipient list, so no organization administrator is the target of an SLA-risk, ingestion-failure or payment-failure alert.

Each run counts the last 60 minutes and, because the rule frequency is every_occurrence and no earlier execution is consulted, emits a new execution, tracking row, in-app row and audit record for the same condition on every run, so a single failure window produces repeated alerts and unbounded rows.

The SLA watchdog emits sla_breached, sla_at_risk and sla_breach_risk on the in-process event bus under claim_events, an in-memory bus that drops an event with no subscriber, and no code subscribes to claim_events, so no steward, notification or record is produced for an overdue claim; the response counts breached and at-risk claims as though they had been handled.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The in-process bus events are replaced by a durable inbox alert for the steward each late or at-risk claim is assigned to, written inside that organization's own context and deduplicated by a unique index over (organization, user, claim+kind+deadline) from migration 20261103: a rerun, retry or overlapping run adds nothing; a new deadline or escalation alerts again. Unassigned claims are counted in the result. Real-SQL tested; mutation-proved (dedupe, recipient). Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

records.title: The deadline is computed from claims.updated_at (falling back to created_at) as though it were the time of the last status change, and the claims table has no status-changed column, so any edit of a claim restarts its SLA clock and a claim that is touched often never breaches.

The watchdog selects every non-terminal claim of every organization with no limit, recomputes each deadline twice, and hands per-organization pilot metrics to promises it does not await, each recorded with no idempotency key as a metric insert and a separate audit insert, so a run answers before the writes finish and a run every minute adds new metric rows each time.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The watchdog keyset-pages the claims scan under a page cap, assesses each claim once, awaits the metric writes keyed by organization and hour, and reports a failed metric or alert write as a failed job (existing implementation, existing route and pglite tests).

records.title: The interview list, the interview item (with its events and attached documents) and the document list return published and archived interviews to any member of the organization with no sensitivity level or consent condition: the whole row, including the full interview text, the retiring employee name, the retirement reason, the AI summary, the risk score and the user ids, and the transcripts and file URLs of the attachments, are returned for privileged, legal_sensitive and executive_confidential interviews, although SENSITIVITY_MIN_ROLE assigns those levels to officer and admin and the search, summary and AI routes enforce it.

remaining: Native run
Derived graphs, aggregates, succession and forecast engines still ignore sensitivity (see related defects)

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Reads of interviews apply the sensitivity floor and consent condition (upstream's change), proven on real SQL by an existing test.

records.title: Publication inserts an active knowledge_base row holding the full interview text and the retiring employee name for every sensitivity level and consent state (isPublishAllowed is defined and tested but never called), and the re-index route rewrites that row from the interview; the knowledge-base list and item routes return active rows to any authenticated user of the organization and of its child organizations with no sensitivity, consent, entitlement or role condition, so the classification and consent attached to the interview do not follow the copy.

remaining: Native run
Institutional confirmation of which levels permit indexing
