records.title: The /api/exports, /api/exports/[id], /api/exports/csv, /api/exports/excel and /api/exports/pdf routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over the reports table: the csv, excel and pdf path segments are cosmetic, no handler reads any source table, builds a CSV, workbook or PDF, streams a file or sets a content type, and the reports table has no format, file or job column although a report_format enum of pdf, excel, csv, json and html exists, so a POST to /api/exports/pdf answers success with a report definition row and a GET answers a list of definitions, and nothing is exported.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: exports, its item, csv, excel and pdf routes were report-definition CRUD that produced no file; all answer 501.

records.title: The export suite reads of the reports table are open to any member of an entitled organization: the table has no owner or personal column and the routes declare no ownerColumn, so the low-role guard stays open and a member receives every report definition of the organization, including definitions the author kept private (isPublic false), written by other users, in the financial, members and claims categories, with the whole config JSON that names the data sources, fields and filters of each report.

The export suite create and update take the whole request body into the reports row: a steward can create a report of reportType system, mark it a template or public, and set runCount, lastRunAt and templateId, and the update has no owner condition and blocks no field, so any steward can rewrite any report of the organization, including its createdBy, updatedBy, config, runCount and lastRunAt, which makes the author and usage columns of a report definition unreliable.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A report body writes only name, description, type, category, configuration and template reference; creator, counters, last run, organization and template flag are the server's.

records.title: The reports table has no status column, so the administrator delete of an export suite report removes the row (hard delete) and the in-transaction audit record it writes lists an empty field set, which leaves no stored copy of the name, category or config of the deleted report definition.

The evidence export, described as an evidence pack summary suitable for procurement and security review, returns policy_checks (grievance creation, status transition, escalation, arbitration seal and evidence immutability as enforced, cross_org_access as denied), org_isolation (enforced true, enforced at the db, route and audit layers, cross_org_read_attempts_blocked true) and an sbom marked available as string and boolean literals of the handler: the handler reads no database, test result, policy engine, sealed bundle or build artifact, so each assertion is returned whether or not the control holds, and the build timestamp, commit and version are environment fallbacks (process start time, local, 0.0.0).

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Removed fabricated policy, isolation, SBOM and build assertions; without a verified sealed artifact the endpoint explicitly refuses issuance (HTTP 503) with not_attested status and null evidence.

records.title: The evidence export labels the pack with the orgId query parameter (default unscoped) and never reads the organization of the session, so a caller can have the pack that asserts cross-organization access is denied issued under the identifier of any other organization, or of no organization, and the isolation assertions are not tied to the caller organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Only the canonical authenticated organizationId is used; a mismatching orgId query is forbidden before any response or audit attempt.

records.title: The evidence export role gate is a deny list of the two spellings member and MEMBER: every other organization role string passes, including the deprecated guest role and any role string that is not in the canonical list, and the response gives the deployed version and commit.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Replaced denylist of member spellings with canonical withApi minimum officer role and required organization context.

records.title: The evidence export records each issue only by incrementing a process-local counter (recordEvidenceExport), with no audit row, actor or organization, so who obtained the pack and when is lost on restart and is not reproducible across instances.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Every permitted export attempt writes evidence.export.unavailable through persistAtomicAudit inside a tenant-bound transaction; failure aborts the response.

records.title: The /api/external-data and /api/external-data/lrb routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over external_accounts, the chart of accounts that accounting providers synchronize, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every GET and POST answers 403 before any query; the lrb path name suggests labour relations board data but no board source is read by either route, and the table-level register of the repository still describes both routes as the live select and insert path of the table.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both routes answer 501 (they were the factory over external accounts under a labour-board name, refused for every caller).

records.title: The external document download returns a read-only storage link in the JSON body with the default sixty-minute lifetime (generateSasUrl is called without an expiry), not bound to the caller, address or grant: the grant, the expiry and the revocation are checked only when the link is issued, so the link keeps working for the rest of its hour after the document grant is revoked or expires and can be passed to a person who holds no grant, and the audit row records the issue of the link, not a read of the blob.

The external document download releases the document version with the highest version number at the time of the request: the external_document_access_grants table has no version column and the handler binds the grant to the document only, so a revision uploaded after the grant was made, which no one reviewed for disclosure to the outside party, is released under the earlier grant.

The extensions item read selects the whole api_integrations row and returns it as it is to any member of the organization: the credentials jsonb column (documented as encrypted, though no code in the application writes or encrypts it), the SFTP host, port and path and the API endpoint of an HR, payroll or accounting connection are returned with no projection and no redaction, unlike the sibling SSO list, which masks its secrets.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The item read is an administrator's and, like the PATCH response, omits the credentials document and the SFTP host, port and path.

records.title: A steward can change the apiEndpoint, the fieldMapping that maps Union Eyes member fields to the external HR or payroll system, the enabled flag and the sync frequency of an organization integration, while removing the same integration needs an administrator; the endpoint is accepted as any URL up to 2000 characters, the mapping as any JSON object, and the audit record names only the fields changed.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Rewriting an integration's endpoint and field mapping needs an administrator, as the delete already did.

records.title: The extensions delete removes the api_integrations row outright, and integration_sync_logs references it with onDelete cascade, so deleting an integration silently erases its whole sync history (records processed, failed, errors, triggering user) while the audit record keeps only the integration id and name.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Deleting an integration first confirms it belongs to the organization (404 otherwise), then refuses with 409 when any synchronization history exists, so the cascade can never erase it; the integration is disabled instead. The existing extensions test was adapted to the new query sequence and gained the history case (disclosed).

records.title: The extensions route reads, changes and deletes api_integrations rows under the name of an extension registry, but no route creates a row and nothing outside the route and the schema reads the table or its apiEndpoint, so enabling an integration, setting a sync frequency or repointing an endpoint is audited as integration.update and returns the updated row while no synchronization exists that the change could affect.

The event item read returns the whole calendar_events row to a steward or above, including meetingPassword, meetingUrl, agenda and attachments, whatever the row isPrivate and visibility columns say, because the generic factory and the route consult neither; below steward the only narrowing is memberId equal to the session user, so confidential events that name no member are unreachable to members and fully open to every steward.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The legacy event item delegates to the canonical calendar route, which applies private and confidential visibility and selects no meeting password or access code.

records.title: The public event registration component fetches /api/events/{slug} without credentials and renders ticket price and free status, but the route requires an authenticated session at the member floor, compares the path value to the uuid primary key of calendar_events, and calendar_events has no slug, ticket price or free flag, so the public page can never load an event through it and a slug that is not a uuid reaches the database as a uuid comparison.

The occurrences route file is byte-identical to the event item route: its path value is the event id, and it reads, updates and deletes the calendar_events row itself, so a call that advertises one occurrence of a recurring event changes or removes the whole series row; recurrenceExceptions and parentEventId are never consulted, and the recurrence service that can add an exception or delete future instances is imported by no route.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: events/[id]/occurrences was a byte-for-byte copy of the event item route; it answers 501.

records.title: The entitlement list returns every feature key whose org_entitlements status is active and ignores expiresAt and the backing contract, whereas the server-side entitlement check refuses an expired entitlement and verifies that the contract is active, so a client that gates premium features from this list shows a module as held after its entitlement has expired or its contract has ended.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The entitlement list now names only the feature keys that the server-side checkModuleEntitlement allows (not expired, backing contract active) and is limited to 200 rows. Contract test pins the check.

records.title: The entitlement list answers 200 with an empty feature list for a caller whose organization cannot be resolved, which a client cannot tell from an organization that holds no entitlement, and it re-resolves the organization with getCurrentUser instead of using the organizationId its wrapper already placed in the context, reading org_entitlements through the shared db import with no tenant context.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The enterprise integrations path no longer answers an empty 200 for a caller without an organization; it answers 501.

records.title: The SSO provider list is open to every member and returns every column except the certificate and client secret, so any member reads the identity-provider entity ids, endpoints, OIDC client ids, the attribute mapping, the role mapping that says which directory groups become administrator or steward, the required groups, the metadata and the user id of the administrator who created each provider.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The provider list (issuer, endpoints, client id, attribute mapping) is an administrator read; credential columns were already reduced to a boolean.

records.title: The SSO provider create casts the body to an interface and checks only that name, providerType and attributeMapping are present: providerType is any string although the schema comment allows saml and oidc, the entity id, SSO URL, issuer and certificate are not parsed or checked, the required fields of the chosen type are not required, there is no unique index on organization, entity id or issuer and no proof the organization owns the identity domain, requireGroups cannot be set, and autoProvision and enabled default to true.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0038 adds unique partial indexes (organization and SAML entity id; organization, OIDC issuer and client id), refusing to apply over duplicates; a duplicate create answers 409. The create now accepts requireGroups (at most 50 short names). Proven on PGlite.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: No proof that the organization owns the identity domain: that needs a DNS or e-mail verification process with the identity provider, which a schema cannot supply.

records.title: No sign-in, token-exchange, provisioning or SCIM code reads sso_providers: the register route is the only reader and writer, so a provider an administrator registers with enabled and autoProvision true and an audit record of sso.provider.create never takes effect, and the decryption helper meant for the OIDC token exchange has no caller; the response reports a configured provider that nothing uses.

The register offers only a list and a create: no route changes, disables, rotates the secret of or deletes a provider, so a mistaken or compromised configuration can be corrected only by direct database work and the enabled flag set at creation cannot be turned off through the application.

The equity monitoring, self-identification and snapshot routes advertise the collection and statistics of special-category equity data but are the generic CRUD factory over member_segments, the saved member-search table: no self-identification answer, consent, statistic or snapshot is read, computed or stored, the dashboard receives a page of segment rows where it expects statistics and snapshots, and a create from the form or the generate-snapshot button lacks the name and filters the table requires.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: equity/monitoring, self-identify and snapshots answered the generic factory over member_segments. Special-category equity data is neither collected nor monitored there, so they answer 501 and expose no segment rows.

records.title: The member-floor reads behind the equity paths return every member_segments row of the organization, including segments whose isPublic is false, because the table has no user or member owner column and the factory adds only the organization predicate, so any member reads the saved filter criteria (status, role, employer, worksite, bargaining unit, seniority) that stewards built privately.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The equity routes answer 501 (batch B09), so no private segment is returned to anyone.

records.title: The self-identification form puts a consent text before the member that promises encryption, aggregate-only reporting with a ten-member minimum, withdrawal and deletion at any time and seven-year retention, and then submits dataCollectionConsent true as a literal in the client body; the route stores no consent record, has no encryption, minimum cell size, withdrawal, deletion or retention behavior, and takes memberId and organizationId from the body that it ignores, so the assurances given at the point of consent are not implemented anywhere.

The self-identification create requires a steward, so the member the form is addressed to receives 403 on submit, while a steward or above is allowed to post a row on the member behalf with any body; a voluntary self-report that the union says is the member own choice is therefore reachable only by staff.

The only snapshot table, equity_snapshots in the financial-service schema, stores counts of Indigenous, visible-minority, disability and LGBTQ2+ members, executive-board and steward counts by group and average hourly pay by gender with no suppression flag, minimum group size or reader restriction, so a snapshot of a small board or worksite would publish counts that identify individuals; the table is revoked from the application roles today, which is why no route can reach it.

The incident item route reads at the member floor (readRole member) while the incident collection requires health_safety_rep, and the factory returns the whole workplace_incidents row: workplace_incidents has no userId, memberId, email or other column the low-role guard treats as personal (injuredPersonId and injuredPersonName are not on its list), so the guard stays open and any member of the organization who holds an incident id receives the injured person name, job title and employee id, body part, nature of injury, treatment, witness statements, investigation report, WSIB claim number and amount, photo and video links and the metadata JSON, with no audit of the read.

remaining: Native run

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Sensitive incident item reads now require the same health_safety_rep floor as the incident collection; member-floor item access is removed.

records.title: The hazard item route reads at the member floor (readRole member) while the hazard collection requires health_safety_rep, and the factory returns the whole hazard_reports row, including reportedByName and reporterContactInfo of a non-anonymous reporter, the assigned person, the risk assessor and verifier names, resolution cost, notes and the createdBy user id, to any member who holds the hazard id; the table has no personal column the low-role guard recognises, so the guard stays open.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Item reads now require health_safety_rep, matching collection authorization and preventing member-level exposure of reporter contact and hazard details.

records.title: A report filed as anonymous is still attributed to the session user: the factory sets createdBy to the authenticated user id on every create and re-asserts it after the beforeCreate hook, the hazard and incident create hooks blank only the reporter name and contact (and the incident hook never writes the isAnonymous column, which stays false; the flag is stored only inside metadata), and every read returns the whole row, so the collection reader (health_safety_rep) and, on the item routes, any member holding the id receive the user id of the person who reported anonymously; the audit record of the create also names the user.

remaining: Native run
Institutional confirmation of the anonymity policy

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both incident and hazard POST declare anonymousCreate, which sets createdBy and the mandatory audit actor to the anonymous sentinel rather than the session user; PGlite regression covers both paths.

records.title: The incident create hook maps severity through a three-entry table (minor, major to serious, critical) and incidentType through a seven-entry table, and every other value is replaced without error by minor and other: a client that sends near_miss, moderate, serious or fatal as the severity is stored as minor and answered with success, a vehicle, fall, electrical, exposure or occupational_illness type is stored as other, and an unparseable or missing incidentDate is replaced by the time of the report, although the same hook rejects a blank description; the dashboard critical-alert count and the trend buckets read the severity that was substituted.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: All declared incident types and severities (including fatal/serious/near_miss) are mapped without downgrades; missing or invalid incidentDate is refused instead of replaced with report time; explicit event time persisted as Date.

records.title: The incident create hook never writes the structured injury, witness and reporter columns (injuredPersonName, bodyPartAffected, injuryNature, treatmentProvided, witnessNames, witnessStatements, reportedByName, isAnonymous): it copies injuryDetails, witnessNames, witnessContacts, reporter name and reporter contact, and the anonymous flag, into the free-form metadata JSON, which every incident read returns whole, so injury, witness and contact data cannot be classified, redacted or reported per field and the columns the schema defines for them stay empty for rows created through the API.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Incident writes injury, witness, reporter and anonymity data to their typed schema columns, not generic metadata. Unsupported sensitive contact/injuryDetails fields are rejected rather than silently persisted as untyped JSON; anonymous reporter name suppressed.

records.title: The hazard create hook sets hazardLevel to moderate when the body names neither hazardLevel nor a known priority, and hazardCategory to other when it names neither hazardCategory nor a known hazardType, and answers success; a hazard submitted without a priority is recorded at moderate rather than refused, and a priority or type outside the maps is replaced silently.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Hazard category and level must be explicitly valid (or valid documented aliases); no fallback to other/moderate for missing or unknown classifications.

records.title: incident_number, report_number, inspection_number and item_number are unique across the whole table, not per organization, and the incident and hazard create hooks take incidentNumber and reportNumber from the body when present (the inspection and PPE creates take every column from the body), so a caller can choose a number another organization already holds, which the database refuses, or pre-empt a number, and a unique violation is the only signal; the generated numbers embed a random uuid rather than a per-organization sequence.

The incident and hazard update routes and the inspection create and update routes store any body column the factory does not strip (only the primary key and organizationId are removed, blockedPatchFields is not set), so an administrator can set status, closedDate, resolutionDate, verification fields, riskScore, authorityNotified, reportableToAuthority, authorityReportNumber, wsibClaimStatus, wsibClaimAmount, scorePercentage, itemsPassed, itemsFailed, criticalHazards, createdBy and incidentNumber directly, with no state machine and no check that the investigation, resolution, verification, authority notification or inspection that the field asserts happened; the statistics routes compute compliance and resolution figures from those caller-stated columns.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The incident, hazard and inspection item routes block a status or outcome PATCH (existing implementation, pinned by the F07 contract test).

records.title: The administrator delete of an incident or hazard sets status archived, and nothing treats archived as removed: the list and item reads add no status condition, so an archived row is still returned and readable by id, hazards/stats and the dashboard count a hazard as open unless its status is resolved or closed (archived counts as open), the dashboard critical-alert count excludes only closed incidents, and incident totals include archived rows.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: An archived incident or hazard is neither listed nor returned by id (the new readCondition), and the statistics, trends and dashboard no longer count it as open, critical or part of a total.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The counts are pinned by source only; no test runs the statistics against rows holding an archived status.

records.title: The incident and hazard list routes read only page and limit; the incident list table sends status, severity and search and the hazard list sends status, priority and search, and the generic collection handler ignores every one of them, so the screens show unfiltered pages while the filter controls appear to work.

The PPE list reads at the member floor and returns the whole ppe_equipment row, including issuedToId, issuedToName, issuedDate and issuedByName, to every member of the organization; the table has no column the low-role guard treats as personal, so the guard stays open.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The PPE register, which names the member each item is issued to, is read at the health-and-safety representative floor.

records.title: The dashboard wraps every query in a catch that logs the failure and returns success true with fixed clean metrics (totalIncidents 0, criticalAlerts 0, openHazards 0, inspectionComplianceRate 100, daysWithoutIncident 90, trainingCompliance 100, all trends stable), so a database, row-level-security or schema error is shown to the member as a safe workplace with no incidents and full compliance instead of an error.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Dashboard errors throw a non-success error rather than returning a fabricated clean dashboard; all eight SQL reads execute inside the authenticated organization's RLS transaction.

records.title: The dashboard computes trainingCompliance as the constant 92 when the organization has any safety_training_records row and the constant 100 when it has none, from a count and no compliance calculation, and the component renders it as a percentage with a progress bar and a badge that changes at 90, so a canned training compliance figure is presented as a measured one.

remaining: A real training-compliance measure needs status and completion columns the table does not have

engineeringCorrection.explanation: No training compliance rate is claimed without completion and due-date evidence; unmeasured values are null, and the tenant-bound dashboard regression covers this.

records.title: The dashboard metrics are labelled as workplace measures but computed from record creation and defaults: inspectionsDue is the count of inspections created in the window (not inspections that are due), inspectionComplianceRate is completed over created, daysWithoutIncident is measured from the latest created_at of any incident row (including archived rows and not the incident date) and is 90 when the organization has no incident row, hazardTrend is up when more than three hazards are open and down only at zero, and incidentChange is 0 when the previous window has no incidents.

health-safety/stats and the dashboard read safety_training_records, and no route, service or job of the application inserts or updates that table (the runtime role is granted SELECT only on it and the only code that names it is these two routes), so trainingDue and the training compliance figure are computed over a table that application code cannot populate and read as 0 and 100 for every organization.

The statistics and findings routes turn missing measurements into zero: avgResolutionTime is 0 when no incident or hazard has a closing date, complianceRate and avgScore are 0 when no inspection has item counts or a score, and each inspection finding with no score_percentage returns complianceRate 0, so an unmeasured inspection is shown as 0 percent compliant and a not-yet-resolved set as a zero-day resolution time.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The inspection findings list reports a missing score as null (shown as a dash) instead of 0%. The statistics and dashboard routes already reported unmeasured values as null (existing implementation, existing tests pass).

records.title: avgResolutionTime of the incident and hazard statistics is computed from closed_date and resolution_date, which no route sets when a status changes (create stores neither, and update stores only what the body states), and the incident statistics count a status of resolved although the schema defines only reported, investigating and closed for incidents, so an incident or hazard closed by a status update has no resolution time and the figures omit it.

Each aggregate route builds its organization filter as organizationId ? organization_id = id : 1=1: the filter falls back to an always-true predicate, so the organization boundary of the aggregates depends on withApi having refused a request with no organization (requireOrg defaults to true) and on row-level security, and not on the route itself.

The incident trend route ignores the organization of the session: it takes organizationId from the query string, uses it as the only organization predicate, and when the parameter is absent runs the aggregate over workplace_incidents with no organization predicate at all, so which rows are counted depends only on row-level security applied to the connection; the route never compares the supplied id with the caller organization and no handler code limits the query to it.

currentRun.repair: Both daily and monthly aggregates now derive organizationId solely from authenticated context, require it, bind the exact organization in withRLSContext and include an unconditional organization_id SQL predicate. The caller's organizationId query string is ignored and unsupported periods are refused.
currentRun.limits: New source and adversarial mocked regression are committed but not yet unit-, PG15/16-, or real HTTP/browser-verified. Full health-safety persona authorization and aggregate correctness remain subject to acceptance.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Incident trend aggregates ignore caller-supplied organization identifiers, bind the authenticated organization to RLS and predicate both day and month SQL paths on organization_id.

records.title: The ICRA report route that serves the executive PDF refuses every request with 422 Assessment not yet completed unless icra_assessments.status equals completed, and no code in the application or its SQL migrations ever writes completed (the start route writes in_progress, the stepwise and one-shot submit routes write submitted, and review, claim and the Stripe fulfilment write no status), while the checkout route sells the briefing and diagnostic tiers whose copy promises a boardroom-ready PDF and the Stripe fulfilment only raises reportTierId, so a buyer who pays $1,200 or $6,500 CAD can never download the PDF the purchase advertises and the route answers 422 for every paid assessment.

remaining: Native run

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The report gate accepts submitted as well as completed, so a paid report is no longer refused for a status nothing writes; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

records.title: The ICRA checkout route selects reportTierId and the capability columns of the assessment and never reads status, so a buyer holding the capability of an assessment that is still in_progress, with no answers and no stored profile, is given a Stripe session for the $1,200 or $6,500 CAD tier, and the Stripe fulfilment then raises reportTierId on an assessment that has no profile payload to patch.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Checkout now reads the assessment status and answers 409 with no Stripe session unless the assessment is submitted or completed, so a buyer is never charged for a report the report route would refuse.

records.title: The ICRA answer, capability exchange, results, one-shot submit, e-mail results and telemetry routes limit requests with lib/rate-limit.ts, an in-memory Map per server process whose default key is the first x-forwarded-for value plus a user-agent hash and whose per-route keys read the same x-forwarded-for header, so the allowance multiplies with the number of instances, resets on restart and, unless an edge overwrites the header (which no route verifies), is chosen by the caller by sending a different header value or user agent; the one-shot submit allowance of 3 per hour and the e-mail allowance of 5 per hour are therefore not enforced limits on a determined caller.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Every ICRA limiter now uses the shared (Redis) limiter, failing closed in production, and keys on one trusted client address: the edge header, else the forwarded-for entry at the configured number of trusted hops from the right (TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS, default 1), never the client-typed first entry. A ratchet fails if a public route imports the per-process limiter. Test disclosure: the guard test that expected the leftmost forwarded-for entry was replaced, the exchange 21-call test was replaced by two limiter tests, and the answer, submit, results and telemetry tests now mock the shared limiter.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: x-real-ip is still trusted when present, which is correct only behind a platform that overwrites it; the deployment must be configured so.

records.title: The ICRA start, one-shot submit and checkout routes create rows and Stripe sessions for anonymous callers with no bot challenge: start and checkout read no challenge token, and the one-shot submit calls verifyTurnstileToken, which returns success with notConfigured true whenever TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is unset, so the only controls are the per-address limits (20 and 10 per hour for the durable guard, keyed on cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip or x-forwarded-for request headers), and each start call inserts an icra_organizations row and an icra_assessments row.

The ICRA resume GET on /api/icra/start, the profile GET and the PDF report GET apply no rate limit or guardPublicIntake bucket, so an anonymous caller can issue unbounded capability probes and database lookups against any assessment id and, for the report, unbounded PDF renders for an assessment whose capability and tier it holds.

The ICRA one-shot submit validates only that the three acknowledgement booleans are true and then stores the whole client consent object in icra_assessments.consent, including a client-supplied acceptedAt and doctrineVersion and any extra keys, where the stepwise start route stamps both server-side; it also stores locale without validation (a column of 16 characters), reads the body with req.json() under no size cap, and keeps any number of orgContext keys whose names are not checked, so the stored consent record is not evidence of what the server presented or when.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The one-shot submit builds the stored consent on the server from the three acknowledgements (time and doctrine version stamped here; client time, version and extra keys dropped), accepts only the en-CA and fr-CA locales, reads the body as text under a 64 KB cap (413 beyond), and refuses organization-context keys that are not short lower-case identifiers or exceed 40. Unit and source-contract tests added; existing route tests still pass.

records.title: The stepwise ICRA flow never requires consent: the start route accepts a missing or partial consent object and stores consent null, the answer route stores answers and free-text notes with no consent check, and the stepwise submit route scores and stores the profile without ever testing the consent column, so assessments, sensitive free-text notes and a scored profile are collected and kept for respondents who never acknowledged the anti-surveillance, data-handling and explainability statements that the one-shot route requires.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The stepwise flow requires all three acknowledgements to start (400 otherwise, consent stamped by the server), the answer route refuses to store anything for an assessment with no recorded consent (409), and so does the stepwise submit. No application caller of these routes existed. Existing tests were adapted: assessment fixtures now carry a recorded consent, the start 500 test sends consent, and the submit tests mock the coverage helper (disclosed); new tests cover the refusals.

records.title: The stepwise ICRA submit route refuses only when no answer row exists (answerRows.length === 0) and otherwise computes and stores a maturity band, composite and continuity profile from however few answers were recorded and sets status submitted, where the one-shot route rejects any answer set that does not cover every routed question, so a profile built from one answer is stored and returned as the organization continuity profile and can be bought and reported on.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The stepwise submit scores nothing unless every question the routing engine requires for an unclassified organization has an answer (400 with the missing count otherwise), using the same routed-submission validator as the live flow. Proven against the real question bank: one answer is refused, a full set is accepted.

records.title: The ICRA e-mail results route accepts any syntactically valid address in the body, with no proof the sender controls it, and sends a branded message from the platform that embeds the caller 30-day bearer capability in the link fragment; any capability holder (and a capability is issued free by the start route) can therefore make the platform send mail to arbitrary third parties, limited only by the per-process in-memory allowance of 5 per hour keyed on a forwarded header, and the event handed to the sink carries an unsalted SHA-256 prefix of the typed address.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The link is mailed only after the respondent acknowledges that anyone holding it can open the results (a required checkbox in English and French; the route answers 400 without acknowledgeLinkAccess), on a durable rate limit. The capability, the ownership proof and the no-storage rule are unchanged.

records.title: The ICRA event sink inserts into an icra_events table that no schema file or migration in the repository defines (its own header says to add the table to the migration), inside a try that swallows every error, so on a database without the table the telemetry, submission and e-mail events are silently dropped while the telemetry route still answers 204; where the table exists, the stored ip_hash is an unsalted SHA-256 of the forwarded address truncated to 32 characters, reversible by enumerating addresses, and the metadata column takes caller-chosen keys and values (telemetry) or the raw error string (submission_error).

The ICRA claim route matches icra_assessments.claim_token, but no code sets that column for an ICRA assessment: the only producer of a claim token is the workbook branch of the Stripe webhook, which writes the workbooks table, and the ICRA fulfilment branch writes reportTierId and the profile payload only (the claim route header says issuance is wired separately), so every claim answers 404 and a paid assessment can never be bound to an organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The paid-tier fulfilment now issues the single-use claim credential (32 random bytes, 30-day expiry, bound to the buyer e-mail) in the same transaction as the tier upgrade, guarded so an existing or consumed credential is never replaced, and a replayed delivery issues nothing.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Nothing delivers the credential to the buyer (the same gap exists for workbooks) and there is no ICRA claim page, so a buyer still cannot present it; delivery needs the e-mail sender and a claim route in the UI.

records.title: The ICRA claim route binds a paid assessment to the organization returned by getOrganizationIdForUser (an active membership in any role) for any signed-in user who presents the claim token, with no role or office test and no check that the caller organization is the purchaser, and it clears the claim token but leaves capabilityTokenHash and capabilityTokenExpiresAt unchanged, so the pseudonymous holder keeps full read and write access to an assessment that now belongs to an organization and the audit row names the organization of whoever presented the token.

The ICRA report review route authorizes an approval or rejection of the report narrative with the shared platform cron secret alone and takes reviewerRole from the request body (governance_reviewer, exec_sponsor, or facilitator for any other value), so the recorded reviewer role is an unverified claim by whoever holds a secret that is not tied to any person, and the audit actor, when one is written, is the constant system:icra-report-review.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The shared cron secret no longer authorizes a review: the caller must be a signed-in platform administrator (401 / 403 otherwise, nothing written). The reviewer role is the verified governance_reviewer authority; a role asserted in the body is refused unless it matches, and the audit actor is the reviewer's own user id instead of a constant. For an unclaimed prospect assessment the reviewer's identity is still not persisted (no tenant to audit against, and the decision record has no reviewer field).

records.title: The ICRA report review route writes its audit record only when the assessment has a claimedOrgId, a column set only by the claim route whose claim token no code issues, so in practice every review decision is committed with no audit record, the decision (reviewer role, status, summary and time) living only inside the assessment organizationContext JSON that the same route rewrites.

The ICRA start resume GET, the profile GET, the capability exchange and the e-mail results routes pass the path, query or body assessment id to a uuid column comparison without validating its shape (the unhandled database error escapes as a 500 where the result and report routes validate with a UUID pattern first), and the answer route calls buildAnswer inside its try, so an out-of-range or non-numeric answer value, or a note sent in public-sector mode, is reported as 500 Failed to record answer and a server error log instead of a 400.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A path value that is not a UUID is a 404 in the answer, claim, profile, submit and exchange routes before any limiter or query; an answer value the question cannot take, or a note the deployment forbids, is a 400 and touches no row. Test disclosure: the ICRA route tests now use a real UUID where they used the string a1.

records.title: The ICRA checkout route builds the Stripe success and cancel URLs from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL with a fallback of http://localhost:3000, and charges either the STRIPE_PRICE_ICRA_BRIEF or STRIPE_PRICE_ICRA_DIAGNOSTIC price id when set or the literal 120000 and 650000 cent amounts otherwise, while the displayed prices in the gate component are separate literals, so an unset URL sends a paying buyer back to localhost and a Stripe price that differs from the literals charges an amount the page does not show.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Production with no application URL refuses to open a session instead of redirecting a buyer to localhost (existing implementation and test).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: A configured Stripe price id can still differ from the amount the application displays; nothing compares them.

records.title: The integration framework stores credentials as the JSON object credentialRef (a caller-chosen string, or the literal managed) and never resolves it: provider-policy states credentialRef is a placeholder never resolved to a vault-backed secret, the base adapter initialize requires config.credentials.apiKey (or clientId and clientSecret for OAuth providers) which that object never contains, and toPublicConfig returns credentialsStored true as a literal for every row, so an activated integration reports stored credentials that no sync can use and a steward is told the integration is ready to synchronize when every sync attempt fails at adapter initialization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The public configuration no longer reports credentialsStored: true for every integration: it reports false, with credentialsResolvable false, because only a reference is held.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: A credentialRef is still accepted and stored and nothing resolves it to a secret; a vault-backed resolution path does not exist.

records.title: The integration sync route accepts dryRun in the body, passes it into SyncOptions and records dryRun in the audited details, but neither the sync engine nor any adapter reads it, so a steward who sets dryRun true expecting a rehearsal is recorded in the audit trail as having requested a dry run for an operation that is executed as a normal synchronization.

The sync engine prevents concurrent runs with a process-local Set keyed organization, provider and type, and the integration factory caches adapter instances in a process-local Map keyed organization and provider that the sync route never evicts, so two instances can run the same synchronization at once and a reconfigured integration can keep serving the adapter built from the earlier configuration until the process restarts.

The integration sync route records its outcome audit row (completed or failed) in a separate transaction after the sync engine has already written provider data, and recordOutcome catches any failure of that write and only logs platform_operation_outcome_not_recorded, so a synchronization that changed organization data can leave the audit trail holding only the requested intent row with no outcome, and the response to the steward does not say the outcome was not recorded.

The integration configure route on an existing provider row writes enabled input.enabled ?? false, settings input.settings ?? {} and webhookUrl input.webhookUrl ?? null into the update, so a steward who changes only the credential reference silently disables the integration and clears its settings and webhook URL, and a configure call with enabled true switches the integration on without the concurrency predicate that the activate route applies.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: An update changes only the fields supplied: sending only a credential reference no longer disables the integration or clears its settings and webhook URL. Switching enabled through configure now carries the same IS NOT DISTINCT FROM concurrency predicate as the activate route (409 and no audit when the state changed), the row is read FOR UPDATE, and the audit records the resulting state, the previous state and which fields changed.

records.title: The /api/integrations/api-keys route is a generic crudRoutes configuration over integration_api_keys, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every GET and POST answers 403 before any query, while the storage authority register still describes the route as the crudRoutes-backed live path with a server-derived organization, and the subordinate authority register states that nothing authenticates from key_hash, so the register text and the route disagree and no route can create, list or verify an integration API key.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The API-key route answers 501 explicitly: no key is issued, listed or revoked through it.

records.title: The Shopify redemption flow cannot complete: createDiscountCode names the discount UE followed by the first 12 hex characters of the redemption id with the dashes removed and uppercased, while the webhook extractor extractRedemptionIdFromDiscount requires UE followed by a full dashed 36-character UUID, so every orders/paid event is answered ignored with no_redemption_discount, a redemption never reaches ordered, providerOrderId is never set, and the fulfilled and refunded events, which look the redemption up by provider order id, never match; the member credits were already deducted by initiateRedemption before the Shopify call.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The code issued and the code parsed are defined together (shopify-redemption-rules): UE plus the 32 hex characters of the redemption id, lossless. The parser also accepts the dashed form and resolves a legacy 12-character code only as a prefix inside the shop's organization among redemptions awaiting payment, and only when exactly one matches, so codes already issued still complete. Round trip unit-tested; the full paid, fulfilled, refunded lifecycle runs against PostgreSQL (pglite).

records.title: The Shopify webhook receiver answers 200 with received true and error Internal processing error for every thrown failure (so Shopify, which retries only on non-2xx, never redelivers a paid, fulfilled or refund event that failed), and processWebhookIdempotent records the receipt after the handler for ignored results too, so an event ignored because the redemption was not yet found (an orders/fulfilled that arrives before orders/paid is processed) is stored as processed and a redelivery of the same webhook id is skipped as already_processed; the receipt check, the handler and the receipt insert run in separate transactions.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A failure answers 500; an event that cannot be applied yet (a fulfilment or refund for an order not recorded as paid) answers 503 with Retry-After; neither records a receipt, so the redelivery is applied. A receipt is recorded only after the handler, only for a final outcome, and tolerates a concurrent duplicate. The handlers are idempotent on their own state (an order already applied is a success), so the separate receipt transaction cannot lose or double-apply an event. Mutation-proved.

records.title: The Shopify refunds/create handler computes the refunded amount from the refund line items but processRedemptionRefund ignores it: it sets the redemption to refunded and returns the whole creditsSpent through an applyLedgerEntry refund, so a partial refund of any size returns every credit of the redemption, the refund amount is kept only in the stored payload, and a later refund event for the same order is treated as already refunded.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A refund returns its share of the credits (floor of creditsSpent x refunded line-item subtotal / order line-item total), a later refund returns its own share, each Shopify refund id is applied once, the redemption becomes refunded only when everything spent has come back, and the total returned never exceeds the credits spent. Refunds are recorded in the stored payload and in the audit entry. Mutation-proved.

records.title: The Shopify webhook receiver stores the full request payload in webhook_receipts.payload_json, a table with no organization column that records every event of every organization, and the orders/paid handler writes the Shopify customer id, e-mail address, first and last name and the line items into reward_redemptions.provider_payload_json and logs the discount codes, so personal data of the purchaser is retained in global and per-redemption JSON with no retention rule or field minimization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The receipt keeps only the topic, shop domain and the order or refund id; the redemption keeps order facts (number, currency, totals, product and variant ids, quantity, price) and no customer id, e-mail, name or line-item title; discount codes are no longer logged. Migration 20261102 irreversibly redacts what was already stored in webhook_receipts and reward_redemptions (executed on PostgreSQL pglite, repeatable).

records.title: The Shopify webhook handlers read and update reward_redemptions and the credit ledger through the plain db import with no withRLSContext or withSystemContext around the handler (the system context in webhook-service covers only the receipt check and insert), while reward_redemptions carries a fail-closed organization policy for the union_eyes_runtime role and the union_eyes_system privileges on it are revoked, so with no app.current_org_id set the lookups can match no row and every transition throws or is ignored as redemption_not_found even if the discount code format matched.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Every lookup and write of the handler runs inside withRLSContext bound to the shop's organization, and the redemption's organization is checked against it. The organization comes from the shop domain through migration 20261101: a unique index on the lower-cased domain and a column-level SELECT (org_id, shop_domain) grant with a read-only policy for the system role; the token and secret references stay unreadable (executed with real roles and RLS on pglite). The runtime-role behaviour under the real application roles is still to be qualified on native PostgreSQL.

records.title: The Shopify webhook receiver verifies the HMAC with one global SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET for every organization and parses the X-Shopify-Shop-Domain header but never reads it (the route destructures only topic, webhookId and hmac), so the shop that sent an event is not checked against any organization; the pre-signature rate limit is keyed on the whole x-forwarded-for header string, so a caller who varies that header receives a fresh allowance for each unsigned request.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The shop domain header must belong to exactly one organization or the signed event is refused (403, logged), each shop has its own rate-limit allowance, and the pre-signature limit is keyed on one normalised address instead of the whole forwarded-for string.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The HMAC still uses one global SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET for every organization; per-organization secrets (shopify_config.webhook_secret_ref) need the secret store. The address key is only as trustworthy as the front proxy that sets the header.

records.title: The /api/federations/[id]/affiliates, /dashboard, /meetings and /remittances routes are four copies of the federation item route (crudRoutes over the federations table, read at member floor and written at steward floor): each one resolves the path id as the id of a federations row of the session organization and returns that same row under all four names, so no affiliate list, dashboard aggregate, meeting record or remittance is read, no child or parent organization is derived or checked, and the federation_remittances table that holds the remittances is not touched by any of them; a federation officer calling the remittances or dashboard path receives the federation profile row (contact fields, per-capita rate, settings, bylaws links) with status 200 and no figure the path name promises.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Affiliates, dashboard, meetings and remittances under a federation were copies of the federation item route; all answer 501.

records.title: The federation collection and item routes configure a steward write floor and an administrator delete floor, but the CRUD governance table lists federations as READ_ONLY, so every POST, PATCH and DELETE answers 403 before any row or audit record is written and no dedicated route in this tranche creates, edits or retires a federation: the register cannot be maintained through the HTTP surface and the configured write roles are never reached.

The /api/federations/benchmark/grievances route is the generic crudRoutes collection over the grievances table with orgScoped true, not a benchmark: it computes no count, rate or aggregate, derives no federation or affiliate scope and applies no minimum group size, and the only thing that stops it returning identifiable grievance rows (grievant name and email, title, description) is the OWN_ROWS_READ entry for grievances in the governance table, which today refuses every caller with 403 because the grievances table has no userId or memberId owner column and its POST is refused by the same table; the route answers no benchmark to any caller and carries no protection of its own against listing grievance rows if that table entry changes.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: federations/benchmark/grievances answered grievance rows as a benchmark; it answers 501.

records.title: The /api/locals and /api/locals/[id] routes are crudRoutes over bargaining_units, an employer-linked certification record (employer, worksite, unit type, certification number and body, contract dates, member count, chief steward, bargaining chair) with no parent organization, federation or local-union identity column, so a caller who expects the locals of a federation receives the bargaining units of the session organization with status 200 and no local union record, no affiliation to a federation and no hierarchy between the two.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: locals and locals/[id] served bargaining units as local unions; both answer 501.

records.title: The locals reads are open to any member of the organization: bargaining_units has no owner, personal or contact column, so the low-role guard stays open and a member receives every unit of the organization with the internal notes text, the custom fields JSON, the certification and contract dates, the member count and the user ids of the chief steward and the bargaining chair, none of which the member role is shown to need.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The locals facade answers 501 (batch B15).

records.title: The locals create and update take the whole request body into the bargaining_units row (the factory strips only the primary key and the organization id on update): a steward can set status, employerId, worksiteId, chiefStewardId, bargainingChairId, currentCollectiveAgreementId, the certification fields, memberCount and updatedBy, and the route applies no organization check to the rows those ids point at, so the only validation of employerId, worksiteId and the officer ids is the existence constraint of the foreign key, not that the referenced employer, worksite or profile belongs to the session organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The locals routes no longer write bargaining-unit fields at the steward floor; they answer 501.

records.title: The administrator delete of a locals record sets status to archived and updatedAt and leaves the archivedAt column of bargaining_units empty, and the in-transaction audit record lists only the field status, so an archived unit has no archive timestamp and no stored copy of its name, certification or officers before the change.

The external grievance upload accepts a blobPath (or a fileUrl inside the application storage account) from the representative and checks only that it starts with documents/<organization id>/ and is not under the intake prefix, then creates a document, a version, a grievance link and an external document grant that copies canView and canDownload from the matter grant: the file is never shown to belong to the representative, to the grievance or to a document the representative may see, so a representative whose matter grant allows uploads and downloads can attach the stored file of any other document of the organization (a member document, another grievance, a privileged file) to their grievance under a new document id and then obtain it through the external download route; the route has no caller in the application and no route lets an outside party place a new file in storage, so attaching existing storage is the only thing the endpoint can do.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: An upload names a stored object only if no document, and no version of one, in the organization already holds it; an object another record holds answers 409 and inserts nothing. Tests added for both holders.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: An unattached object under the organization prefix is still accepted: nothing yet proves it was uploaded by this representative for this matter (an upload-intake record bound to the representative is needed).

records.title: The external grievance upload stores the representative-supplied mimeType, documentType, filename and fileSize on the document row without comparing them to the stored object (no allow-list of types, no size ceiling, no check that the claimed size or type matches the blob), applies no malware scan on this path (the scan sits in putBlob, which resolveStoredBlob never calls) and reads the whole blob into memory with downloadToBuffer to compute its hash, so a stored object of any size or type is attached as the type and size the caller wrote and an oversized object is pulled into the request process.

Each external route records the access decision (external_authorization.allowed or denied) through auditLog, a call separate from the read or write that follows, and the read itself (the grievance projection, the document list or the document metadata) is not recorded; outside canonical V2 auditLog catches a failed database insert, logs it and returns, so the grievance data is still released to the outside party when the audit row could not be written, and the document metadata route writes two decision rows for one request.

The external routes take the organization from the organizationId query parameter and open the row-level-security context for that organization (withRLSContext) before any authority or grant is checked, and on a refusal the decision audit is written into the audit trail of the organization the caller named: outside canonical V2, whose binder requires an active membership in that organization, any signed-in user can name any organization id and have a denied-authorization row written into that organization audit log, and the tenant transaction is opened for an organization the caller has no relationship with.

The projection returned to the external representative reads caseNumber, subject and summary from the grievance row, but the grievances table has none of those columns (it has grievanceNumber and description), so caseNumber and summary are always null in the response and the representative receives no case number and no summary of the grievance, only the id, title, status, step and the filing and response dates.

The feature flag route with ?flag=<name> evaluates any flag name the caller supplies against the global feature_flags table and returns its enabled value, with no role floor and no restriction to the published LRO and AI names, so any signed-in user can enumerate operator-controlled flags (including kill switches and flags targeted to their own organization or user) by guessing names; the response also echoes the caller user id and organization id.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A single-flag probe answers only flags the application defines (plus pilot-mode); an unknown name is a 404 and is not evaluated.

records.title: The feature_flags schema documents the flag types as boolean, percentage, organization and user, but the evaluator switch handles boolean, percentage, tenant and user and answers disabled with reason Unknown flag type for anything else, so an organization-targeted flag stored with the documented type organization is never enabled for any caller and the route returns false for it without an error.

The jurisdiction rules route serves, for every jurisdiction that has a workers compensation board entry, a rule named WCB Claim Filing Deadline under the category arbitration_deadline whose deadline_days is the claimDeadlineDays constant, and that constant is documented in its own notes as the period within which the employer must report an injury (Alberta 72 hours stored as 72 in a field named days, Saskatchewan and Manitoba 5 business days, New Brunswick 3 days) while getClaimDeadlineDays describes it as calendar days; the fallback of 30 can never apply because the function always returns a number, and the ComplianceChecker component reads the first arbitration_deadline rule and renders the arbitration scheduling gap as compliant or violation against that number.

currentRun.repair: Separated workers-compensation board reference from arbitration deadlines; removed unverified WCB days and default 30-day arbitration deadline; server and client fallback now return informational verification-required outcome, not fabricated compliant/violation determinations.
currentRun.limits: Not a jurisdictional rulepack or legal advice. Statutory deadlines require counsel-validated rules, versioned authority and runtime/browser verification. Source and tests unverified.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The rules route serves the board as a reference with verification required and no deadline number under an arbitration category (existing implementation and test).

records.title: The British Columbia termination notice schedule ends with a tier whose maxYears is 8 while every other schedule ends with maxYears null, and calculateTerminationNotice matches a tier only while yearsOfService is below maxYears, so for any British Columbia tenure of 8 years or more no tier matches and the required notice is 0 weeks: the compliance check never reports a termination_notice violation for such an employee, whatever notice was given, and the jurisdiction rules and labour standards profile publish the schedule with no tier above 8 years.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: British Columbia now has an open-ended top tier at the statutory maximum of eight weeks, and a test asserts that every jurisdiction ends in an open tier and that tiers are contiguous and non-decreasing. The lower British Columbia tiers were not changed here; they were not checked against the statutory text.

records.title: The labour standards compliance check declares every body field optional and each rule block runs only when its own fields are present, so an empty body, a body missing the tenure or notice pair, or a daily-hours figure below the meal-break trigger returns a 200 summary with totalFindings, violations and warnings of 0 and an empty findings list; the response does not list which checks were evaluated, accepts negative and absurd hour counts, and gives no sign that nothing was checked, so a request that tested nothing reads as a clean result.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The response carries the number of checks evaluated and, when none applied, a notice that this is not a finding of compliance.

records.title: The break, overtime, termination notice, statutory holiday and workers compensation tables behind the jurisdiction rules, labour standards list, profile and compliance check are literals compiled into the application: apart from the anti-scab entries they carry no effective date, version, source document or verifier, no office is named as having determined them, and the routes return them with statute and article citations and violation severities as if they were governed law, so a stale or wrong constant is served as authority until the code is edited.

The labour standards profile returns minimumWage as { hourly: 0, effectiveDate: 'varies' } with a comment that it is populated by live data, but the handler reads no live source, so every jurisdiction profile publishes a zero hourly minimum wage to unauthenticated callers as a real field of the profile.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: No source of minimum wage rates exists, so none is published: minimumWage is null with minimumWageStatus not_published instead of a zero rate that reads as a real one. Live rates are not provided by this change.

records.title: The jurisdiction rules route maps a known CA-XX code and otherwise casts the raw query string to a jurisdiction, never validates it against the known set, and indexes plain-object tables with it, so an unknown code answers success true with an empty rule list (no error), an inherited property name such as constructor selects a function from the tables and raises a TypeError that the handler reports only as a generic 500, and a category that matches no rule also answers success with an empty list.

The /api/jurisdiction/clc-compliance and /api/jurisdiction/validate-deadline routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over bargaining_units: neither path checks a CLC rule or validates or calculates a deadline, a GET lists the bargaining unit rows of the organization (certification numbers and dates, contract expiry, next bargaining date, chief steward and chair user ids) at the member floor, and a POST inserts a bargaining unit from the request body and answers success, so a client that posts to validate-deadline expecting a validation gets a stored unit and no verdict.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: jurisdiction/clc-compliance and validate-deadline served bargaining-unit rows with no validation; both answer 501. The deadline calculation paths the UI uses are separate routes and are unchanged.

records.title: The intelligence, investigations and investigations/audit routes wrap another route behind a requireOrgAccess function that returns the literal true and, for POST, a validateMutationBoundary whose schema checks only that request.method is a string, so the 401 and 400 branches are unreachable and the wrappers read as an access check that is not there; every real check comes from the delegated handler.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The two investigation aliases lost their always-true guard along with their delegation.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Other wrappers (governance, intelligence, the oci paths and the communications tracking handlers) still carry a requireOrgAccess that returns true for every request.

records.title: The /api/investigations route re-exports the case collection handlers: GET lists claims (claim number, member id, member name and e-mail, description, desired outcome, assignee, status, AI and merit scores) and POST at the steward floor creates a claim, so no investigation record, investigator assignment, confidentiality marking, party list or investigation-specific audit exists behind a name that suggests a confidential workplace investigation.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The investigations path was an alias of the case collection (a create made a case); it answers 501 and the roster-facade ratchet pins it.

records.title: The /api/investigations/audit route re-exports the audits list: it takes no investigation id or filter and returns the 100 newest audit-log rows of the whole organization (action, resource type, outcome, severity and the acting user id as auditor) to any officer, so a path named for the audit of an investigation discloses the organization-wide activity trail and cannot show the audit of one investigation.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The investigation audit path no longer returns the organization audit log under another name; it answers 501.

records.title: The knowledge-base list and item routes filter only by the organization and its parent and by is_active: they never read is_public or allowed_organizations, so the access-control columns of the table do not limit a read (the publish route stores exit-interview copies with is_public false and they are still returned), they apply no union_knowledge_suite entitlement although publication requires it, the list q parameter matches the full content of rows whose content it does not return (a search oracle over exit-interview text), and neither read writes an audit record of who opened which document.

The knowledge-base item GET writes: after the read it runs UPDATE knowledge_base SET view_count = view_count + 1 WHERE id under withSystemContext, which bypasses row-level security, with no organization predicate, not awaited and with no audit record; the id was matched under an organization predicate by the select just before, but the write itself is an unscoped system-context statement that a read-only route should not hold.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The system-context counter update names the organization of the row that was read.

records.title: The geofence GET takes latitude and longitude from the query string and, when the point is inside the fence, checkGeofenceEntry inserts a geofence_events row with the member user id, the geofence id and the precise coordinates through the shared db handle, with no call to hasValidConsent, no tracking-enabled check, no transaction and no audit record, so a member who never opted in or revoked consent has a precise position stored by a GET, and that row can be neither read nor deleted through the consent routes (revocation answers 404 when no active consent exists).

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A geofence entry still answers inside or outside for the point the caller supplies, but a geofence_events row is stored only when the member holds a valid opt-in (the strike permission for a strike fence) and tracking is enabled; the response states whether anything was recorded. Existing test adapted: the opted-in case now queues the consent and configuration reads; three new tests cover no consent, tracking disabled and a missing strike permission.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The insert still uses the shared database handle without a transaction or an audit record, and the entry check runs from a GET.

records.title: The consent DELETE revokes consent and deletes the member location points and geofence events only after an update that matches a consent row whose status is not opted_out, and it answers 404 and deletes nothing when the member has no such row, so a member whose positions were stored without consent (geofence entry check), whose consent was revoked earlier, or who never had a consent row, has no route that erases the stored rows and depends on the retention handler that no scheduler invokes.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: When there is no active consent to revoke, DELETE now erases whatever location tracking and geofence rows remain (consent expired or already withdrawn, an unfinished retention sweep) and audits the erasure; it answers 404 only when there is neither a consent to revoke nor data to erase, and then keeps no log row. revokeLocationConsent itself is unchanged.

records.title: The location track POST inserts the precise position through the shared db handle with no transaction, no persistAtomicAudit, no location_tracking_audit row and no log of the write, although consent grant and revocation are audited, so no record shows when positions were collected for a member; getConfig creates a default configuration row with tracking enabled on first use as a side effect of this write path; and a missing consent, a disabled configuration and any database failure are all answered 500 with the raw error message.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The position insert and an audit record (purpose, strike or event, never the coordinates) commit in one transaction; a member who has not opted in gets 403, a disabled tracker 503, and any other failure a 500 without internal text. Test mocks extended for the new collaborators; three new route tests.

records.title: The location consent row is unique by user id alone with no organization, strike or event column, and tracking checks only that an opted-in row exists plus the strike or event flag for strike, picket and event points: the free-text consentPurpose and the purpose description are never compared with the purpose of a point, meeting and organizing points need nothing beyond an opt-in, and strikeId and eventId are accepted as any uuid and not verified to belong to the organization, so a consent given for one purpose in one organization authorizes collection for every other purpose, strike and event.

The consent POST stores the consentText, purpose and purposeDescription exactly as the request body gives them, under a fixed consentVersion of 1.0: the zod schema declared for the route is never applied (the body is destructured unchecked and only checked for presence), the server holds no copy of the text the member was shown, and the same request can claim any text, so the stored consent record, which the privacy model calls the exact text shown to the user, is attested by the caller and not by the application.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The body is parsed with a typed, bounded schema: purpose, description and text are non-empty bounded strings and the two allowance flags must be booleans (a string "false" was stored as consent); an invalid or non-JSON body is a 400 that records no consent.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The consent text and purpose are still supplied by the client; a server-owned notice with a version the member acknowledges needs a client change.

records.title: The consent status GET calls hasValidConsent, which updates the consent row to expired through the shared db handle, with no transaction and no audit record, when the stored expiry has passed, and reflects the unvalidated context query parameter without checking that it is strike or event, so a read changes the consent state and leaves no trace.

The geofence POST applies no schema (the declared zod schema is unused): name, type, coordinates and radius are checked only for presence and simple comparisons on the raw body values, so a string coordinate passes the range checks and then fails at toFixed with a 500, the radius has no upper bound, so a geofence the size of the planet makes every position inside it, the geofence type is any text, and strikeId is stored without being verified to belong to the organization.

The /api/healthwelfare/plans route is the generic crudRoutes configuration over per_capita_remittances and has nothing to do with health and welfare plans: a GET returns the organization remittance ledger at the member floor (member counts, per-capita rate, total amount, approver and rejecter user ids, rejection reason, payment method and reference, remittance and receipt file URLs), and a POST is refused because the table is READ_ONLY in the CRUD governance table, so every member reads financial remittance records and no plan exists behind the name.

records.title: The /api/meeting-rooms/[id]/bookings route is the generic item configuration over meeting_rooms: its id is a room id and a GET returns the room row (not its bookings, which live in room_bookings and are read by nothing here), and a DELETE sent to a bookings path to cancel a booking removes the room itself at the administrator floor, so a client that treats the path as a booking collection cancels no booking and takes the room out of service.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the bookings path answers 501 for GET and POST, reads and writes no room or booking row.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The room_bookings table is not migrated; the booking rules in lib/services/room-booking-rules.ts are not wired in.

records.title: The operational metrics GET admits any signed-in user of any organization, or any caller that presents the AI service key, and then counts claims, claim status changes in the last 24 hours, claims not closed that were last updated more than five days ago, and claim-update messages containing error or failed across every organization: requireApiAuth is called with no options (so no organization and no role is required), none of the four database reads carries an organization predicate, and they run through the shared database client outside any organization context, on a connection whose role the migration that introduced the runtime roles records as rolbypassrls = true, so row-level security does not narrow them.

remaining: Native run
Real request and error figures from the observability system

records.title: The operational metrics GET names the lifetime claim count of all organizations request_count (its own header says request_count is a proxy that returns a placeholder), derives error_rate from the number of claim updates whose message contains the text error or failed divided by the number of status changes in 24 hours, and runs its five reads under Promise.allSettled so that a rejected read is replaced by 0 (or an empty queue list) and the response is still 200 with window 24h, so an unreachable database or job queue reads as a healthy zero and the figures are not request counts or error rates.
