records.title: The operational metrics GET compares the x-service-key header with AI_SERVICE_KEY using ===, which is not a constant-time comparison (lib/api/secret-compare.ts holds secretsEqual for this purpose and the route does not use it), accepts that one shared key as authority over the figures of every organization, and when the data queries throw returns 500 with detail set to String(err), so the text of a database or queue error reaches every caller that passed the check.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The service key is compared in constant time and no error text is returned; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

records.title: The churn-risk routes score a named member with a TensorFlow network that has no trained weights in the repository: loadChurnModel reads model.json from disk and, when it is absent (no code calls saveChurnModel), builds a new network and fits it for 50 epochs on 150 generated examples whose feature values are drawn with Math.random from hand-written ranges (the medium-risk labels are Math.random() > 0.5 ? 1 : 0), the normalisation constants are literals and confidence is Math.abs(churnProbability - 0.5) * 2; the POST stores the result with isPredictionFromML true and returns it as aiGenerated with source ml, so a risk level for a named person is presented as the output of a trained model when it is the output of a randomly initialised network fitted on invented data, and the interventions derived from it (priority outreach, a dedicated steward) attach to that person.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The churn route scored members with a randomly initialised network pre-trained on generated examples and stored the score. GET and POST now answer 501 behind the officer floor. The extensive route test, which exercised that scoring with mocks, was replaced by a test of the 501 and of the absence of the generated-example model. Two round-48 ratchet tests that pinned the former handler's organization-input properties (body schema without organizationId, organization-context check) were rewritten to assert that the route now accepts no organization input at all and touches no stored prediction.

records.title: The churn-risk SQL names columns and values that no schema file in the repository defines: the POST reads profiles.organization_id, full_name, union_tenure_years and member_age (profiles is the billing profile and has none of them) and claims.resolution_notes, counts claims with status withdrawn (a value the claim_status enum does not have) and inserts user_id, model_type, model_version, prediction_value, confidence_score, predicted_at, response_time_ms and features_used into ml_predictions, and the GET filters ml_predictions on model_type and predicted_at and joins profiles on user_id, while the declared ml_predictions shape, which the storage authority register calls canonical, has none of those columns, so on a database built from the repository these statements are rejected and the route answers 500 instead of a prediction; the intervention strings the POST stores and returns also carry garbled characters (UTF-8 emoji decoded as Latin-1 text).

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The churn route answers 501 and contains no SQL (batch B10).

records.title: The churn-risk routes build a risk profile of a named member from that member case history (claim count, resolution rate, days since the last claim, a satisfaction figure the SQL itself labels simulated and infers from claim status and a resolution-notes text match, and a count of withdrawn claims), store the case-derived features in ml_predictions.features_used and return the member name, risk score, contributing factors such as inactive for N days or N negative feedback incidents, and tenure to any officer, with no record of what members are told, whether they consented, which office may act on a score or how long a score is kept.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The churn-risk route answers 501 (batch B10); no member is profiled from case history.

records.title: The churn-risk invocation audit is a separate write outside the data transaction and ahead of the checks that decide whether the call is valid: auditAIInvocation writes an audit_logs row through auditLog and its own tenant context before the GET checks the organization and before the POST validates the body, so a rejected request leaves an AI invocation record with outcome success, the GET (a read method) writes a row on every call, and the POST prediction row and its persistAtomicAudit record commit in a second, unrelated transaction; the auditRefId returned in the response metadata names the first record, not the committed prediction.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The churn route performs no invocation audit write at all now that it answers 501 (batch B10).

records.title: The churn-risk handlers are registered with withRoleAuth at the officer floor but ignore the context it supplies (the parameter is named _context) and resolve the user and organization a second time with getCurrentUser, the GET counts claims per member with a subquery (WHERE member_id = p.user_id) that carries no organization predicate and runs through the shared database client outside any organization context, the limit query parameter is parseInt of the raw string with no number check and no upper bound, and neither handler applies guardAiFeature although the sibling model routes apply one.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The churn route answers 501 and reads no claims (batch B10), so its second identity resolution and unscoped claim read no longer exist.

records.title: The SLA breach risk POST returns computeSlaBreachProbability, a sum of literal weights over four caller-supplied values (priority, hoursRemaining, transitionCount, hasPreviousBreaches; featureRefs is only required to be a list of strings of two characters or more), clamped to 0.01 to 0.99, together with a constant confidence 0.78, bounds of plus and minus 0.08 and a model object with type, version and trainedAt taken from a model_metadata row the route inserts with scoring heuristic_v1 when none exists, so arithmetic over unverified inputs is presented as a model prediction with a confidence and a training date, and a steward can obtain any score (including 0.80 and above, which the realtime alerting sweep counts as an imminent breach signal) by choosing the inputs.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The score is presented as a rule-based heuristic: no confidence, no interval and no training date are returned or stored. Its priority and time remaining are read from the case in the caller's organization (404 for a case that is not), so a caller can no longer choose the inputs that decide an imminent-breach alert; values sent for them are ignored.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The transition count and previous-breach flag are still caller-supplied (they add at most 0.34, so with a case that has time left they cannot reach the 0.80 alert threshold); deriving them needs the claim history.

records.title: The SLA breach risk POST accepts caseId as any GUID, never reads claims or grievances to check that it exists or belongs to the organization, and does not store it on the ml_predictions row (the table has no case column; the id appears only in the audit record details and the response), so a score is not attached to a case, the GET cannot list the predictions of a case, and the feedback route cannot check that a prediction belongs to the case it is later said to be about.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.subject_id. The case is verified against the organization (B08) and is now stored on the prediction row, and the audit entry and feedback carry it.

records.title: The SLA breach risk POST and feedback POST take modelVersion from the caller (default sla-risk-v1, any non-empty string), look up model_metadata by organization, type sla_breach_risk and that string, and insert a new model_metadata row when none exists (the POST with the caller featureRefs as parameters, the feedback with empty parameters), so a steward creates unbounded model rows, the version recorded for a prediction is whatever was typed, and feedback can be recorded against a version the prediction was never made with.

The SLA feedback POST lets a steward submit feedback for the same prediction any number of times (nothing records that a prediction already has feedback), takes actualBreach and resolutionHours from the request body with no check against the case, and folds each submission into a running mean absolute error by reading the model_metadata parameters JSON and writing it back without a row lock or version check, so two concurrent submissions overwrite one another observation count and a steward can move the quality score and the retrain recommendation at will.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.model_version, written by the prediction route. Feedback now defaults to the version the prediction recorded and refuses (409) a different one, so the version binding no longer depends on a column that was missing. The route test zod mock gained optional() on min() (disclosed).

records.title: The SLA feedback routes compute meanAbsoluteError, a qualityScore written to model_metadata.accuracy, retrainRecommended after 30 observations with an error above 0.25, a trainingDataQueue of the last 200 submissions (each with its free-text comment and submitting user id) and a retrainSignal, and the GET returns them as the model feedback summary, but no code reads trainingDataQueue or retrainSignal and the scoring function that produced the predictions is a fixed formula that never reads model parameters, so no retraining can follow from the signal and the accuracy figure describes a formula that stays as it is.

The SLA feedback POST updates model_metadata inside withRLSContext, which when UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 is 1 runs the transaction as the union_eyes_runtime role, and the round-58 migration revokes every privilege from that role on model_metadata and grants SELECT and INSERT only (the storage authority register records the same required privileges), so under that configuration the UPDATE is refused with a permission error, the whole transaction including the audit record rolls back and the steward receives a server error for every feedback submission, although the route is the one the register lists as the feedback path.

The SLA feedback POST calls trackPilotEvent after the transaction has committed and awaits it with no error handling: trackPilotEvent inserts into pilot_events through the shared database client imported from @/db outside any organization context (the route holds no tenant transaction at that point, and pilot_events carries a direct organization row-level policy), so when that insert fails the steward receives an error for feedback that was already committed and audited, and a retry records the observation a second time; the pilot_events activity record is therefore written in a separate transaction from the feedback and its atomic audit record, so the audit trail of the submission is split across two commits that can disagree.

The SLA breach risk GET lists the latest 25 stored sla_breach_risk prediction rows of the organization at the member floor with no guardAiFeature feature gate and no enforceAISafety call (the destructured handler argument is only organizationId), where the POST of the same file and both methods of the feedback route apply both, so an organization that has switched the AI feature off still serves its stored predictions to every member.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The list is read at the steward floor behind the same AI feature gate and safety check as the POST, and reads nothing when the gate refuses.

records.title: The ml/query POST forwards the free-text question of a steward (up to 500 characters), an arbitrary context value validated only as z.any(), the organization id and the shared AI_SERVICE_TOKEN bearer to the service at AI_SERVICE_URL, and merges the JSON the service returns (which its own contract says may include the generated sql and result data) into the response unfiltered, with no record of what the service may receive, no data-class or consent decision and no check of what comes back, while nothing in the repository implements the /api/query endpoint to show that it applies the organization id it is sent; the question and context can name members and cases.

The ml/query POST records its audit through logApiAuditEvent, which only writes a logger.info line (the question cut to 100 characters and the confidence), after the external call and not persisted, and it calls enforceAISafety with userRole member and dataClass internal although the route requires steward and answers over claims, steward workload and settlement data; enforceAISafety reads only the user id, organization id, requested entity organization and canMutate, so the declared role and data class are labels and not controls, and a question that is answered leaves no durable audit record.

The ml/monitoring/metrics GET queries ml_predictions for predicted_at, prediction_correct and assignment_accepted and model_metadata for model_name, precision, recall, f1_score, last_evaluated_at, baseline_accuracy and baseline_confidence, none of which the declared tables have, and joins model_metadata to the per-model figures on model_name with no organization predicate (the table is organization-scoped, and the query runs through the shared database client rather than a tenant transaction), so on a database built from the repository the route fails with a column error, and were the columns present the join would mix the model rows of every organization into one organization figures.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Query uses actual schema columns and organization predicates for model metadata and prediction subqueries.

records.title: The ml/monitoring/metrics GET substitutes literal figures for what was not measured and reports them as model health: precision, recall and f1 are COALESCEd to 0.80, the status CASE returns critical whenever accuracy is NULL and healthy only at 0.85 and above, and the mapping code turns a missing value into 0, a missing status into healthy, a missing trend into stable and a missing last_evaluated_at into the current time, so a model with no measurements is reported with 0.80 quality figures and a fresh timestamp.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: No invented precision, recall, F1, health or trend; unevaluated values explicitly null/unknown.

records.title: The drift, usage, claim-outcome, timeline, workload-forecast and recommendations routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over ml_predictions, so each lists every stored prediction row of the organization whatever its type (page of 50, at most 100) and inserts a caller-supplied row, while its name advertises drift monitoring, usage monitoring, an outcome prediction, a timeline forecast, a workload forecast or recommendations, and nothing is computed, filtered by type or monitored behind any of them.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: ml/monitoring/drift, monitoring/usage, predictions/claim-outcome, predictions/timeline, predictions/workload-forecast and ml/recommendations were the generic factory over ml_predictions under six model names; all answer 501 and ml_predictions has no generic binding (its governance entry was removed). The monitoring alerts route (GET queried columns and a table that no schema defines and stated a fixed PSI 0.28 drift alert; POST wrote to a table no migration creates) also answers 501; its three POST tests were replaced by one assertion of the 501.

records.title: A steward can insert an ml_predictions row of any prediction type, value, bounds, confidence and horizon through the six generic prediction routes (the body is copied into the insert), and the same table is what the SLA breach risk list returns for type sla_breach_risk, what the SLA feedback route accepts a prediction id from, what the realtime alerting sweep counts under withSystemContext (sla_breach_risk rows from the last 60 minutes with predicted_value at or above 0.80, which raises an organization alert) and what the insights generator reads as the latest 20 predictions, so a caller-chosen row is stored with no provenance and is consumed as a model output.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: ml_predictions moves from OPERATIONAL to READ_ONLY in the generic CRUD governance, so the six generic prediction routes can no longer insert or alter a prediction row; only the dedicated scoring routes write it. Covered by the existing governance and route-coverage ratchets.

records.title: The declared ml_predictions shape (prediction_type, prediction_date, predicted_value, bounds, confidence, horizon, granularity) conflicts with the SQL files that create the table: db/migrations/20260324_add_remaining_missing_tables.sql, db/migrations/20260507_fixup_create_break_glass_activations.sql and db/migrations/manual/067_advanced_analytics_q1_2025.sql each create it with model_name, model_version and target_date NOT NULL and no default, and migrations-platform/0019 only adds the declared columns (and sets NOT NULL on them only when the table is empty), so on a table created from those files the inserts of the SLA breach risk route and of the generic prediction routes, which supply none of the legacy columns, are refused by the database.

The ml/monitoring/alerts routes name columns and a table that the repository does not define and the GET holds SQL that is not valid: it reads ml_predictions.model_type, predicted_at, prediction_correct and confidence_score (the declared table has prediction_type, prediction_date and confidence), joins a table ml_alert_acknowledgments that no schema file or migration creates, ends two SELECT lists with a trailing comma before FROM and orders by alert_timestamp, which no CTE selects, so the GET answers 500 and the POST, which inserts into ml_alert_acknowledgments, fails with a missing relation, on a database built from the repository.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The alerts route answers 501 and contains no SQL (batch B10).

records.title: The ml/monitoring/alerts GET emits a P1 finding with the literal text Data drift detected: Case Complexity PSI = 0.28 (threshold: 0.25) for Claim Outcome Prediction whenever the organization has created more than 100 claims in the last 7 days, whatever the data is (no population stability index is computed), and builds every alert id from the model type and TO_CHAR(NOW(), YYYYMMDDHH24MISS), so a drift figure is asserted from claim volume alone and the id of each alert changes every second, so an alert cannot be referred to twice.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The monitoring alerts route answers 501 (batch B15); no literal drift value or per-second alert id is returned.

records.title: The ml/monitoring/alerts POST requires alertId to be z.guid, while every id the GET generates is text such as perf_<model>_<timestamp>, so no listed alert can be acknowledged; the insert is keyed ON CONFLICT (alert_id) alone, so an acknowledgement of one alert id by one organization blocks the same id for every other organization (the update applies only to the organization own row and a conflict is answered 409), and the POST accepts any GUID the caller types, acknowledging an alert that does not exist.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The same route answers 501, so there is no acknowledgement to key on an id alone.

records.title: The ml/monitoring/alerts GET joins ml_alert_acknowledgments on alert_id with no organization predicate and runs the whole read through the shared database client rather than a tenant transaction (the POST uses withRLSContext), so an acknowledgement written by another organization for the same alert id would be shown as acknowledged, with the acknowledging user id and time, in this organization list.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The alerts route answers 501 and reads nothing (batch B10).

records.title: The /api/metrics route is a generic crudRoutes configuration over analytics_metrics that lists the organization stored metric rows at the member floor and accepts a steward-supplied row, while lib/observability/metrics.ts documents the Prometheus (prom-client) metrics as available at GET /api/metrics and lib/public-routes.ts names /api/metrics as a role-scoped infrastructure route, so a scraper pointed at the documented path receives JSON rows of business metric records (including their metadata column) rather than metrics in the exposition format.

The /api/movement-insights/trends route is a generic crudRoutes configuration over analytics_metrics (the organization own metric rows, readable at the member floor and insertable by a steward), while the movement insights dashboard page documents anonymized cross-union trends with a minimum of 5 organizations per trend, no individual organization identifiable and a consent status, reads movementTrends and dataAggregationConsent, and admits only the MOVEMENT_INSIGHTS_ROLES office list, so the API path serves none of the consent, minimum-population or office controls its name and its dashboard describe and returns organization rows under a movement-trends name.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: movement-insights/trends served stored analytics rows, not the consent-gated aggregate the dashboard uses; it answers 501.

records.title: The notification list GET wraps its three queries in a try block whose catch logs and returns an empty notifications array, unreadCount 0 and zero totals as a normal 200 (the comment says the in_app_notifications table may lack expected columns), and a non-numeric page parameter becomes NaN, fails the query and takes the same path; the count GET catches every error with an empty catch and returns count 0; so a failed read is shown to the member as no notifications and no unread items, and the dashboard top bar that calls the count route cannot tell the two apart.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The swallowing try/catch is removed from the list and count reads, so a failed read is a failure; page and limit are parsed strictly (400).

records.title: The notification create POST lets a steward insert a row for any non-deleted member of the organization with a caller-written title, message, type, action label, action url and data object taken from an unvalidated body (no schema, no length or shape bound, an unparsable expiresAt becomes an Invalid Date that fails at insert and answers 500), and in_app_notifications has no created-by or sender column and the insert sets none, so the recipient sees a steward-authored message in the same inbox and with the same presentation as a system notification; the acting steward appears only in the audit record, whose details hold the recipient and type but not the text, and nothing limits which members or how often.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Strict schema bounds title, message, type, label, link (same-site path only) and data size and requires a future expiry; the author is stored in data.origin (client origin overwritten); 100 per hour per steward; the audit carries a content digest.

records.title: The notification PATCH reads read from the body without a schema: a value that is truthy but not a boolean (such as the string false) sets readAt to now and stores the text in the boolean column, a value PostgreSQL cannot parse as a boolean fails at the update and answers 500, and setting read to false never clears readAt, so the stored read timestamp can contradict the flag; the audit record stores the raw read value that was sent.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Only a real boolean is accepted; readAt is set when read and cleared when unread; the audit stores a boolean.

records.title: The notification test POST inserts one in-app row for the calling steward with a fixed title and the message that it verifies that the notification setup is working correctly, but it calls no push, e-mail or SMS channel and reads no device or preference, so a success proves only that a database row was written; every call adds another row with no expiry and no de-duplication, and the response is the stored row, not a delivery result.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route states it tests the inbox only, reports each channel's real state, reuses a recent unread test row, and expires new rows after an hour.

records.title: The push device collection reads at the member floor and restricts a read to the caller own profile, but its POST requires the steward floor, so a member (the only person who holds the phone) is refused with 403 when the retired /api/notifications/device route sends them to /api/mobile/devices to register; for a steward the insert copies every body field into push_devices apart from the forced profileId (enabled, quiet hours, timezone, lastActiveAt, id, createdAt), an unknown platform value fails the push_platform enum and a user without a profiles row fails the foreign key, both as 500.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The person who holds the phone registers it at the member floor, every row is the caller's own, and the token is never returned (batch B02).

records.title: Devices are kept in two unrelated tables: push_devices (written by the generic device route) and mobile_devices (written by the sync route), each with its own token, preference and active columns, and neither route exports a PATCH or DELETE or has an item route, so a device or token can never be disabled, archived or removed by its owner or an administrator, a device that passes to another account is refused with 409 by the ownership check on every later registration, and the only code that reads either table for delivery (services/fcm-service.ts over push_devices and lib/mobile/mobile-engine.ts over mobile_devices) is imported by no route, worker or script outside its tests.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both device tables now have an owner removal route (PATCH preferences and DELETE for push devices, DELETE for mobile devices), audited.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The two tables are not consolidated, and no sender reads either table (services/fcm-service.ts and lib/mobile/mobile-engine.ts remain unimported by any route or worker).

records.title: The mobile sync GET selects every column of mobile_devices and the POST returns the inserted row, and the device collection GET and POST return the whole push_devices row, so each response carries the device push token (a delivery credential for that device) together with the jailbreak flag, compliance issues, last compliance check and metadata columns; the rows are limited to the caller own devices, but nothing projects the token or the security flags out of a response that a browser or script can read.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: omitFromResponse removes the push token from every push-device response; the sync route projects an explicit safe column list that excludes the token, the jailbreak flag and the compliance columns.

records.title: The /api/mobile/sync route lists and registers mobile devices and synchronizes nothing: it never touches the mobile_sync_queue table that the mobile engine defines, and its POST refuses a body without deviceToken, deviceId and platform, while the only in-repository caller, the Sync now button in SyncStatus, posts just deviceId (or the text unknown) and platform pwa with no deviceToken, so that request is always answered 400 and the control reports an error whatever the device state.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route accepts the body its only caller sends (a browser needs no token), says in every response that no synchronization was performed, and the Sync now button shows success only when the response says it synced.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: No synchronization is implemented: mobile_sync_queue is still never read or written.

records.title: When the same user posts an existing deviceId the sync POST updates deviceToken, appVersion, osVersion and lastActiveAt but not organizationId, so a user who registers the device while acting in a second organization receives the row still bound to the first organization (the GET filters by the current organization and will not list it) while the audit record is written for the second one; a deviceToken already held by a different deviceId, and a platform, name or version longer than its varchar column, are not checked and surface as raw database constraint failures answered 500.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Re-registration updates organizationId, a token held by another device is a 409, and every field is length-validated against its column before any write.

records.title: The /api/mobile/push/subscribe and /api/mobile/push/unsubscribe routes are the same crudRoutes configuration over push_notifications, the push campaign table: the browser client posts the PushSubscription (endpoint and keys) to subscribe and { endpoint } to unsubscribe, neither of which names the NOT NULL campaign columns, so a steward request fails at insert and answers 500 and a member request is refused 403 at the steward floor, no subscription or opt-out is ever stored or removed, and the client never inspects the status, so it marks the browser subscribed after subscribe and unsubscribed after unsubscribe although the server did nothing.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Web push subscription has no store and no sender, so both routes answer 501 and read or write nothing, instead of CRUD over the campaign table that failed and left the client believing it had subscribed.

records.title: The push campaign GET paths return the push_notifications rows of the organization to any member (member read floor, no owner column, and the table has no user column for the low-role guard to apply), including draft and scheduled campaigns with their name, title and body, targeting (target type, target criteria with roles, statuses, tags and custom fields, topics), the uuid array of targeted push_devices rows, delivery counters and the creating user id, so every member can read unpublished union campaigns and how they are aimed.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The only paths that served push_notifications to a member are removed; the table is no longer classified for generic CRUD, so it is DENIED by default.

records.title: The push campaign POST copies the whole request body into push_notifications at the steward floor, so a steward can create a row with status sent, sentAt, targetType all and any totalTargeted, totalSent, totalDelivered, totalClicked and totalDismissed values, and the row then reads as a delivered campaign with engagement figures although no route, worker or script that is imported by the application sends a push (services/fcm-service.ts has no importer outside its tests) and no push_deliveries row exists.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: No route can create a push_notifications row any more, so a row cannot be written as sent with delivery counters.

records.title: The /api/mobile/notifications route is the generic factory over the notifications table (the scheduled deadline-reminder queue: type, priority, related entity, scheduled time and send status), not the in_app_notifications inbox that /api/notifications serves, so a mobile client that lists notifications receives a different dataset with no read flag or read route; a member sees only their own rows but a steward or above reads every user scheduled notification of the organization, with message text and the related grievance, claim or deadline reference.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The mobile path runs the same handlers as /api/notifications (shared in lib/notifications/inbox-handlers.ts, each path behind its own visible guard), so it serves the in-app inbox (own rows) instead of the scheduled queue table.

records.title: The scheduled-notification POST copies the body into the notifications table at the steward floor with no check that the target userId is a member of the organization (the sibling /api/notifications POST makes that check), so a steward can store a row addressed to any user id string, set its status to sent and its sentAt, priority and related entity, and that row reads as a delivered notification although the notification-processing cron that would send scheduled rows answers 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Create now goes through the inbox POST, which checks the recipient is a member of the organization, validates input and cannot set a sent state; the scheduled-queue table has no generic route.

records.title: The top-level /api/negotiations route is a second copy of the /api/bargaining/negotiations collection: the crudRoutes configuration over the negotiations table is identical in both files (member read, steward write, organization scoped, no blockedPatchFields), so the same confidential negotiation records are reachable by two paths and a role, confidentiality or field restriction added to one path leaves the other open.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both paths take their read floor and writable fields from one shared rules module, so a restriction cannot be added to one path and missed on the other.

records.title: The negotiation POST lets a steward store strikeVotePassed, strikeVoteDate, strikeVoteYesPercent, mandateExpiry, estimatedCost, maximumCost, status and confidentialityLevel from the request body, and the route reads no vote, poll, mandate or costing record to verify them, so a steward-typed strike-vote result or cost ceiling is stored as the negotiation record and is then returned to every member by the member-floor GET.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: writableFields excludes strike-vote, mandate, cost, status, confidentiality and agreement-link fields on create and update (400), and negotiations are read at steward level instead of member.

records.title: meeting_rooms rows store requiresApproval, allowedUserRoles, blockedDates, operatingHours, min and max booking duration and advanceBookingDays, and the room routes let stewards set them, but no route reads or writes room_bookings and the only booking code, lib/services/calendar-service.ts, returns true from checkRoomAvailability and builds an in-memory booking with the comment that production would insert into room_bookings, so a room configured to require approval or to exclude a role enforces neither and a booking is never stored.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The bookings route answers 501 and reads and writes nothing; the booking rules are implemented and tested in room-booking-rules.ts.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The physical room_bookings table lacks the columns the application declares and has no runtime grant; booking needs that migration before the rules can be wired in.

records.title: A PATCH sent to /api/meeting-rooms/[id]/bookings updates the meeting_rooms row whose id is the path value at the steward floor, copying every body field except the primary key and the organization (status, isActive, requiresApproval, allowedUserRoles, blockedDates, contact person, e-mail and phone, imageUrl, metadata, createdAt), and reads or changes no room_bookings row, so a client that patches a booking changes the room itself and a booking id addresses nothing.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The bookings path no longer edits the room row or exports PATCH or any room CRUD; it answers 501 for every method and reads or writes nothing.

records.title: The four OCI routes (intake, assessment, results and report) are wrappers over the OCRA alias handlers, which re-export the ICRA handlers, and each wrapper calls a local requireOrgAccess function that returns the literal true for every request and, for the intake and assessment POST, a validateMutationBoundary whose schema checks only that request.method is a string, so the 401 and 400 branches are unreachable and the file reads as an organization access check over a flow that is in fact anonymous and authorized only by the assessment bearer capability; the OCI paths add a third public name for the same handlers, with the same limits, consent gaps and defects, and no behaviour of their own.

The OCRA e-mail results path re-exports the ICRA e-mail results handler, which accepts any syntactically valid address typed by the caller, with no proof that the caller controls it, and sends a branded message from the platform through the e-mail provider that embeds the caller 30-day bearer capability in the link fragment, so any holder of a capability (the start path issues one to anyone) can make the platform mail the capability link to a third party under a second public path name, limited only by the per-process in-memory allowance, and no decision names who may receive an assessment link.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The OCRA path re-exports the ICRA route, so it carries the same acknowledgement requirement and limiter.

records.title: The peer benchmarks route (member floor) takes the organization to benchmark from the organizationId query parameter and the clause suggestions route (officer floor) takes it from the organizationId body field, and both handlers destructure the session organization as an unused underscore variable and never compare it with the requested id, so the library reads whichever organizations row the request names (and, for benchmarks, the member counts of its peers) and the only boundary left is the row-level-security policy on the organizations table, which the route cannot show was applied to the connection it ran on; a request that names another organization returns that organization data wherever the policy does not hide the row.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both routes compare or suggest for the caller's own organization. A target named in the query or body that is not the caller's reads as 404 and nothing is read; a caller with no organization is refused. Peer benchmarks now work without naming a target. The peer-benchmarks test that required an organizationId parameter was replaced by three tests of the new behavior; the suggest-clauses fixtures use the caller's organization.

records.title: The federation discovery route (officer floor) passes a province, a sector and a member-count estimate from the body to a query over every active organization of type federation or congress, ordered by member count and limited to 10, with no organization predicate, and returns each match with its id, name, organization type, province and member count, so an officer of any organization is offered a directory of other organizations by design, and the only thing that narrows it is the organizations row-level-security policy that lets a tenant transaction see its own row; no source decides what a prospective affiliate may see of a federation.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Discovery already lists federations only for an officer-floor caller and (batch B12) now scores the sector.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: It remains a directory of federations by name and member count, readable by any organization's officer; whether that directory may be shown to every organization is an institutional decision.

records.title: The functions behind federation discovery, peer benchmarks and clause suggestions wrap their whole body in a try that logs the error and returns an empty array, and the peer benchmark and clause suggestion lookups throw Organization not found for an id they cannot see before that catch, so a database failure, an unknown or invisible organization id and a genuine absence of matches all reach the route as an empty list and are answered 200 with success true and a total of 0, and the caller cannot tell a refused or failed lookup from an empty result.

The federation matching function accepts a sector and never reads it (the route documents matching on sector and the filters use only organization type, status and province), adds the reason Similar size category whenever both member counts exist whatever their ratio (the score term is the ratio times 20, but the reason is pushed for a ratio of 0.001 as for 0.9), and awards fixed weights of 40, 30, 20 and 10 points, so the matchScore and matchReasons shown to the officer as grounds for choosing a parent federation are literals that do not follow from the data they name.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The sector now scores (25, case-insensitive match against the federation's sectors) and "Similar size" is stated only when the smaller count is at least half the larger. The reason text "Similar size category", which was given for any ratio, is gone and its test was changed to the new text.

records.title: The clause suggestion scorer awards 40 points to federation-shared clauses and 50 to congress-level templates and lists the source organization name from the sourceOrganization relation, while the shared clause library policy deliberately gives federation and congress sharing levels no visibility beyond owner, shared-with or public and the organizations policy lets a tenant see only its own row, so those weights can apply only to rows the policy shows (owned, shared with the organization or public), every other source name resolves to Unknown, the sector and province bonuses are added to rows that the filters already restricted to the same sector and province, and the relevance reasons shown to the officer describe a federation hierarchy the data access does not provide.

The peer benchmark function obtains the national average through fetchNationalAverage, which returns the literal table from getFallbackAverage (member count 2500, per-capita rate 45, staff 8, budget 1250000, grievance resolution 45 days) when CLC_API_KEY is unset, when the CLC API answers 404 or an unexpected body, and on any thrown error, and the route returns it as nationalAverage with no flag that it is a fallback; the peer average is computed as a sum divided by the count of peers with a positive member count, which is 0 divided by 0 when every peer has none, and nationalAverage falls back to the peer average when null.

The smart defaults route returns recommended features, suggested integrations and suggested API, document and storage limits from literal tables keyed on an unvalidated organizationType query value (any unknown value falls back to the local table) and a member count taken with parseInt (NaN, zero and negative values are treated as the default of 100), and the feature and integration names, for example benchmark-suite, cross-federation-collaboration, inter-union-messaging, provincial-lrb, wage-data and microsoft-365, appear in no other source file of the repository while no code reads the suggested limits, so the response presents hard-coded suggestions as intelligent defaults for capabilities that no route, registry or limiter defines.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route served a literal table of features, integrations and limits by organization type that nothing defines or applies. It answers 501; its test of the table was replaced by an assertion of the 501.

records.title: The federation discovery, peer benchmarks and clause suggestions routes record their audit trail with eventBus.emit(AppEvents.AUDIT_LOG, ...) after the work is done, an in-memory event bus whose only retained state is a 1000-entry history, and no code anywhere in the application subscribes to system.audit_log, so no audit row is ever written for these reads of other organization data, the emitted event carries no organization id of the actor, and the comment Emit audit event describes a record that does not exist.

The onboarding events route lets any steward or higher write a pilot event and an atomic audit row named onboarding.event.org_created, onboarding.event.user_invited or onboarding.event.role_assigned for a targetUserId and role that are free strings in the body, without creating the organization, sending an invitation or changing any role and without checking that the target user belongs to the organization or that the role exists, so the pilot event table and the audit log hold attestations that a milestone happened which the caller merely asserted.

The onboarding events payload accepts metadata as an unbounded record of unknown values and the handler spreads it after targetUserId and role when it builds the stored pilot event metadata, so a caller can overwrite the targetUserId and role of the event row with different values than the ones the audit row records, and the same unbounded object is written twice (event metadata and audit details) with no size or key limit.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The onboarding event payload bounds targetUserId (255) and role (64), limits metadata to 20 keys of short scalar values, and stores caller metadata before targetUserId and role so it can never replace the values the audit row records.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The event is still a caller-asserted milestone (tracked by the companion defect).

records.title: The onboarding transfers path advertises a transfer operation but is a wrapper that calls the onboarding events recorder behind a requireOrgAccess function that returns the literal true and a validateMutationBoundary that checks only that request.method is a string, so a POST to /api/onboarding/transfers records an org_created, user_invited or role_assigned event for the session organization (the event type enum has no transfer value) and the unreachable 401 and 400 branches read as an access check that is not there; the transfers page route only redirects to the pilot onboarding dashboard.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: onboarding/transfers re-exported the event recorder behind a guard that always passed; it answers 501. The test that asserted transfers delegated to the audited recorder (and returned 200) was replaced by an assertion that the route answers 501 and does not reuse the recorder.

records.title: The onboarding root route is the generic CRUD factory over pending_profiles, the pre-signup profile table keyed by e-mail with the Whop membership id and usage credits, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every GET and POST answers 403 before any query, while the SelfServeOnboarding component posts the organization name, type, province, plan and terms acceptance to /api/onboarding and navigates to the dashboard only when the response is ok (a refusal is silent), so the onboarding form has no route that can accept it and the path name does not describe the table behind it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The onboarding root answers 501 instead of refusing every form submission through the governance denial of the pending-profiles table.

records.title: The onboarding root route sets orgScoped true over pending_profiles, which has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate: a GET at the support_agent floor would list the pre-signup e-mail, Whop membership id, billing cycle and credit balances of every organization and a POST at the steward floor would insert a profile from the request body; the DENIED entry in the CRUD governance table is the only barrier, and the continuity inheritance route is a second path over the same table, so one governance entry guards both.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The onboarding root answers 501 instead of mounting the factory over pending_profiles, and the roster-facade ratchet pins it.

records.title: The onboarding readiness path advertises an onboarding readiness check but is a wrapper that calls the onboarding root handlers, the generic CRUD factory over pending_profiles, behind a requireOrgAccess function that returns the literal true and a validateMutationBoundary that checks only that request.method is a string, so no readiness is computed anywhere, every GET and POST is refused 403 by the DENIED governance entry, and the unreachable 401 and 400 branches read as an access check that is not there.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: onboarding/readiness wrapped the pending-profiles handlers behind a placeholder guard; it answers 501.

records.title: GET /api/organizations/[id] checks only that a session user id exists, validates only the uuid shape of the path id, and reads the organizations row of that id inside withSystemContext (the union_eyes_system role that the 0108 policy for the organizations table exempts), so any signed-in user receives the whole record of any organization: contact email, phone, website and address, charter number, subscription tier, billing contact id, the settings JSON, enabled features, member counts, creator id and legacy organization id, with no membership, role or mandate check.

records.title: After the organization row is read inside withSystemContext, GET /api/organizations/[id] computes activeClaims, totalClaims and childCount with db.execute outside any withRLSContext or withSystemContext callback, so the grievances and organizations statements run on the pooled connection with no app.current_org_id set: under the 0108 tenant policy they return no rows (so the counts are zero for every organization, including the caller own), and on a connection role that bypasses the policy they return the real counts of whatever organization id the caller named; the route returns either an unisolated or a silently zero figure and cannot be relied on for either.

currentRun.limits: Exact-HEAD native PG15/16 and HTTP/browser acceptance pending.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Claims aggregates execute in explicit tenant RLS context for direct members or in a system transaction after verified platform/parent-admin authority; both paths predicate the target organization. Child counts execute in explicit system context. No bare pooled query or silent tenant mismatch.

records.title: PATCH /api/organizations/[id] reads the request body with an unguarded req.json() and copies name, slug, display_name, email, phone, website, sectors and settings into the update with no schema validation: the settings JSON column (which holds per-capita rate, remittance day and fiscal year keys) is replaced wholesale by whatever object the organization administrator sends, a changed slug is accepted with no uniqueness or format check although the path route resolves organizations by slug, a malformed JSON body or an invalid sectors value surfaces as an unhandled 500, and the unvalidated email and website are stored as sent.

When a system administrator changes parent_id through PATCH /api/organizations/[id], the update writes only parentId: hierarchy_path and hierarchy_level of the organization and of every descendant are not recomputed, the new parent is not checked to exist or not to be a descendant of the organization, and no source in the route or its audit record keeps the previous parent, so the ancestors, descendants and path reads (which follow hierarchy_path) disagree with the children read (which follows parent_id) after a parent change.

DELETE /api/organizations/[id] lets the administrator of an organization set the status of that organization to archived with no further check, although the PATCH on the same route refuses any change of status unless the caller is a system administrator because lifecycle status defines the institution standing: the delete takes no reason or confirmation, does not look at child organizations (the parent_id foreign key restricts deletion, not archiving), does not require a second approver, and the archived status removes the organization from the canonical organization choices (only status active organizations are offered) and from the billing scheduler, so one organization administrator can take the whole organization out of service.

currentRun.repair: Direct DELETE archival now refuses local administrators and returns explicit HTTP 501 even for platform administrators; no archive write occurs without an independent institutional approval workflow.
currentRun.limits: The durable two-person approval, reason, confirmation, descendant and billing lifecycle handling remain unimplemented; cannot count this as engineering-corrected or CLOSED.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route already refuses an organization's own administrator (403, platform governance required) and gives even a platform administrator no direct archive (501, institutional lifecycle workflow required), so DELETE no longer archives. The source change was upstream's; the regression test proving it (admin refused, non-admin refused, platform admin 501, nothing written, no audit, malformed id 400) is new. The organization aggregate reads now accept both driver result shapes, which also repairs an upstream pglite test that read zero claims.

records.title: The organization-scoped guard that the item and roster routes call (requireUserForOrganization, through getUserContextForOrganization) finds the caller membership with only the user id and the organization id in the where clause, with no status and no deleted_at condition, so in the legacy (non-canonical) mode a member whose status is suspended or inactive, or whose row is soft-deleted, still passes as a member of the organization with the role the row keeps: they can read the full roster, update or archive the organization when the kept role is admin, and add roster members when it is steward or above; other lookups in organization-utils require status active.

currentRun.repair: Reject suspended, inactive, and removed memberships before organization read, roster, and role authority is granted.
currentRun.limits: Source and regression committed. Unit, PG15/16 and HTTP/browser validation pending at exact HEAD.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Legacy organization guards and role lookup require active membership and deleted_at IS NULL; shared organization read-authority also excludes soft-deleted membership. Adversarial unit and native PG regression added; CI not yet verified at current HEAD.

records.title: GET /api/organizations/[id]/members requires only that the caller is a member of the path organization (any role, including member, in any status) and returns every roster row with user id, name, email, phone, department, membership number, role, status, primary flag and join dates, with no role floor, no member-directory policy (the organization/members route limits stewards to members of their assigned cases and withholds employment data below officer), no pagination and no read audit; the page and the SMS campaign builder call it.

records.title: GET /api/organizations/[id]/members selects every organization_members row of the organization with no deleted_at condition, no status filter, no limit and no ordering, so soft-deleted members are returned beside active ones with their contact details and the whole roster of a large organization is returned in one response, whereas organization/members excludes deleted rows.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The roster excludes removed members and is read a page at a time (default and maximum 200) in a stable order; proven on real SQL, including that consecutive pages do not overlap.

records.title: POST /api/organizations/[id]/members lets any member whose role is steward or above insert an organization_members row for any user_id string with any of the roles member, steward, admin, executive or observer and an immediately active status: the route does not compare the granted role with the role of the caller, does not check that the user id exists or consented, does not use an invitation or acceptance step, and the inserted row is what getUserContextForOrganization later reads as the role of that person, so a steward can create an administrator or executive membership for an accomplice account; the unique (organization, user) index turns a repeated or previously removed user id into an unhandled 500.

records.title: POST /api/organizations/[id]/members inserts without a conflict clause or an existence check, so a user id that already has a row (including a soft-deleted one) violates unique_org_membership and the exception propagates as an unhandled 500 rather than a 409, and the response of a successful insert returns the whole stored row including the generated ids.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A user already on the roster is a 409 with the one row kept, proven on real SQL against the unique membership index; invalid JSON was already a 400.

records.title: The member directory projection used by GET /api/organization/members substitutes the department Administration and the position Union Member when the stored values are empty and reports seniority 0 for an officer-level reader when none is recorded, so the response presents canned organizational facts and an unmeasured seniority as recorded data about a member.

GET /api/organization/members/search places the raw q parameter inside an ILIKE pattern with no escaping of percent and underscore and no length bound, returns at most 50 rows with no ordering and no paging parameter so members past the first 50 matches are unreachable and the page returned is not stable, and returns the email address of each match to the caller.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The search term is trimmed, bounded to 100 characters (400 beyond), and its LIKE wildcards are taken literally. Results are ordered by name then id and paged by limit (at most 50) and offset. The test mock chain was adapted to the ordered, paged query (disclosed), and a new test covers escaping, bounds and offset.

records.title: GET /api/org/current is described as the canonical organization endpoint but reads no table: it returns the session organization id with name null, slug null, subscriptionTier null and an empty features list, and an availableOrgs array that holds only that same placeholder, so a client receives a 200 organization payload that carries none of the organization data and lists no other organization the user belongs to.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: org/current reads the caller's organization (name, slug, tier, enabled features) under its RLS context and answers 404 when there is no row, instead of a placeholder with a null name.

records.title: GET /api/organizations/current requires only a session user and returns the whole organization row of the session organization to any member, whatever their role: settings JSON (per-capita rate and fiscal configuration), billing_contact_id, subscription tier, enabled features, created_by, legacy_org_id, contact email and phone and the claim counts, none of which an ordinary member is shown to need.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The route needs an active membership (404 otherwise) and returns settings, billing contact, subscription tier and provenance only to the organization's administrators; every other member gets the public profile. The sibling /api/org/current already returns a four-field projection.

records.title: GET /api/organizations/hierarchy lets any signed-in user list up to 500 organizations of every tenant (all organization types except platform) because it reads the organizations table inside withSystemContext with no membership, role or mandate check, and returns for each one the name, slug, type, parent id, hierarchy path and level, member count, active member count, child count, status, sectors and CLC affiliation; the rootOrgId query parameter only filters the rows already read, so it narrows nothing for a caller who leaves it out or names another organization, and the member counts are aggregate figures of organizations other than the caller own.

records.title: The ancestors, children and analytics routes compare the raw path segment with a uuid column and the descendants route compares it with the hierarchy text array without validating its shape (the item route validates it, these do not): a segment that is not a uuid makes the database raise an unhandled error and a 500, and an unknown organization answers 200 with an empty list (ancestors, children, descendants) instead of 404, so a caller cannot tell an organization that does not exist from one with no relatives.

The commercial transition, artifacts, intelligence and reference-profile POST handlers cast request.json() to a TypeScript type with no schema, and persist the caller strings (reason, source, notes, milestone, lessonLearned, objectionRaised, requestedFeature, deploymentBlocker, stakeholder and note) with no length bound into the responses JSONB column and, for the transition, into the audit details; the intelligence handler appends to arrays on every call, so a steward of the claimed organization or a platform-tier actor can grow the column without limit and every later read, proposal and timeline serializes it.

records.title: The artifacts, intelligence and reference-profile POST handlers write through withLockedPilotMutation, which locks the application and merges the response keys with a single UPDATE and writes no audit row, and the routes write none, so a steward of the claimed organization or a platform-tier actor can add artifact versions, intelligence notes (lessons, objections, requested features, blockers and stakeholder sentiment) and reference snapshots to a pilot application with no durable record of who did so, although the coverage manifest declares these writes atomically audited.

The reference profile route builds a testimonial, a case study and a benchmark dataset for a pilot application where the testimonial quote is a response key a steward or the applicant can set (referenceTestimonialQuote, authored and role keys are not reserved) or else the literal text that the organization established a repeatable pilot operating cadence with measurable adoption growth, attributed to the application contact name with the role Pilot Sponsor, the time saved is Math.max(6, Math.round(adoptionRate * 0.18)) hours a week (never below 6), and adoption, engagement and health come from a pilot_metrics row or else from the synthetic proposal signals and a 100 minus risk figure; the case study titled as 90-day pilot outcomes and the benchmark record are persisted by POST as a versioned snapshot with a checksum, so quoted words, hours saved and outcomes that no pilot customer said or measured are stored as reference material for the organization with no attestation or consent step.

records.title: The champions, friction, metrics and conversion-assessment routes (admin floor) read the organization from the organizationId query parameter and never compare it with the session organization, then call services that run raw SQL over pilot_events through the bare db import filtered only by that id, returning per-user ids with case, update and active-day counts (champions), user ids with the date of the last login or case (friction, full report), unique-user, case and update counts with a daily active user trend (metrics) and the counts that decide a conversion flag (readiness); an administrator of any organization can therefore read the usage telemetry of any organization whose id they know, and the only boundary left is a row-level-security policy that applies only when the request runs under the canonical tenant context.

records.title: The pilot events route lets any member write a pilot_events row of any of 25 event types (including case_created, update_added, first_case_created, org_created, user_invited and role_assigned) with an unbounded metadata object, through a bare-db insert with no audit, and for case_created and update_added only reads metadata.caseId without checking that the case exists or belongs to the organization; the champion detection (3 cases, 5 updates, 5 active days), the conversion readiness flag (3 active users in 14 days, 10 cases, 5 updates, 5 active days), the friction lists and the engagement metrics are computed purely from these rows, so a member can make an organization appear to hold champions and a conversion-ready pilot without creating a case.

The CUPE bootstrap route (system_admin floor, allowed when NZILA_MODE is pilot or demo) resolves the target organization by the slug in a fixture file (cupe-local-123) and, when the body sets reset, deletes every grievance, every organization_members row and every pilot_checklist_items row of that organization with predicates on the organization id alone, with no demo marker, row-origin check, dry run, confirmation or backup, and then re-inserts fixture members (including roles such as admin and president under fixed fixture user ids) and grievances with onConflictDoNothing, so if the organization at that slug holds real grievances or members in a pilot or demo runtime the reset destroys them and the audit row records only the counts the fixture attempted.

remaining: Mocked database only

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The reset needs a system administrator, a pilot or demo runtime and an explicit confirmation naming the organization (upstream's change, existing test).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: Seeded rows still carry no demo marker, so a reset deletes by organization and slug rather than by marker.

records.title: The CUPE bootstrap response reports seeded.worksites as the number of worksites in the fixture although the handler never inserts a worksite, increments membersInserted and casesInserted once per attempted insert even when onConflictDoNothing skipped the row, and returns onboarding checklistInitialized, completed 3 and pending 2 as literals for five checklist ids (org_profile_configured, team_invited, first_case_created, sla_watchdog_enabled and billing_connected) while the onboarding route reads and toggles only seven different ids (org-seeded, users-invited and others), so the seeded rows are never shown by the checklist route, a toggle of a seeded id answers 404, and the same literals and counts are written into the audit details.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The response now reports zero worksites actually written and separately identifies unseeded fixture worksites; member and grievance counts use INSERT RETURNING, not attempts; onboarding uses the seven canonical persisted checklist IDs and no invented completed tasks.

records.title: The demo-data route (officer floor, pilot or demo runtime) inserts four employers named for real federal departments with e-mail addresses on real government domains (lr-demo@tbs-sct.gc.ca and others) and fictional grievances with named grievants into the employers and grievances tables of the officer organization, the same tables that hold real records, with no demo marker column on either row (only a GRV-DEMO- number prefix and an lr-demo@ address prefix), so the seeded cases are counted as cases managed by the pilot metrics and listed with real grievances, and the purge deletes every row of the organization whose grievance number starts with GRV-DEMO- or whose employer e-mail starts with lr-demo@ whether or not the seed created it.

The pilot current and overview routes report organizerAdoptionRate and memberEngagementRate as the share of organization_members rows whose updated_at falls in the last 30 days (any edit of the row counts as activity), report avgTimeToResolution as the mean of COALESCE(resolved_at, NOW()) minus created_at over grievances created in the last 30 days, so an unresolved case counts as resolved at the moment of the request, count seeded demo grievances in casesManaged, and replace a figure with the stored pilot_enrollments value when no live row exists, with no indication in the response that the figure is a proxy or a stored fallback.

The onboarding checklist PATCH lets any officer mark any of seven steps (contracts-uploaded, employers-imported, integrations-configured, export-verified and others) completed or reopened with a boolean in the body and stamps completedBy and completedAt, and writes a pilot.checklist_completed audit row when all seven are true, without checking that a contract was uploaded, employers were imported, an integration was configured or an export was verified, so the checklist state, isComplete flag and audit trail record asserted steps.

The pilot overview route (officer floor) admits a platform administrator identity or, in the legacy mode, any member of the platform organization (DEFAULT_ORGANIZATION_ID) holding the officer role title, then under withSystemContext lists every actively enrolled organization with its id, name, slug, enrollment date, adoption and engagement rates, cases managed, resolution time, health score and milestones, running three queries for each enrollment and with no pagination, so the cross-organization aggregate is reachable by an officer role title of one organization and no platform-staff mandate or read audit exists.

The pilot current route resolves the session organization with withOrganizationAuth and then runs its enrollment, milestone, member and grievance reads inside withSystemContext, so the row-level policies that scope pilot_enrollments, pilot_milestones, organization_members and grievances to the caller organization do not apply and the explicit eq(organizationId) and the interpolated organization id in the two SQL statements are the only scope.

The pilot feedback POST validates easeRating, category and trigger but passes comment from the body unvalidated and unbounded (any JSON value, no length limit) into pilot_feedback.comment, and the administrator GET returns the ten most recent rows with select() including userId and the raw comment to any administrator of the organization, so free text and the identity of the member who wrote it are returned without a length bound or an anonymity decision.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The comment must be text of at most 2000 characters (trimmed; an empty one is stored as none), a body that is not a JSON object is refused, and the administrator summary no longer returns the author user id of recent feedback. New route test covers each.

records.title: GET /api/organizations checks only that a session user id exists, applies no role floor and no organization predicate of its own (the only filters are the optional parent and status query parameters), and selects every organizations row visible to the connection inside withRLSContext: in the legacy mode that transaction only sets app.current_org_id and never switches to the union_eyes_runtime role, so whether the list is confined to the caller organization depends on the database role of the connection, and where it is not, any signed-in user receives every organization with its contact email, phone, website, address, charter number, subscription tier, billing contact id, settings JSON, enabled features, member counts, creator id and legacy id, and with include_stats the active grievance count of each listed organization.

records.title: GET /api/organizations returns whatever the tenant context lets the policy show while three administration pages (the new organization page, the edit organization page and the members console) treat the answer as the list of organizations of the union for choosing a parent or an organization: under a connection confined by the 0108 policy the list is the caller own row only, so the parent picker is empty of any other organization and the parent query parameter finds no children, and under an unconfined connection it is every organization (the exposure of DEF-0B10-OPL-01); the route also applies no limit, passes the parent query string to a uuid column unvalidated so that a malformed value raises an unhandled database error and a 500, and lets withRLSContext throw an unhandled error (500) for a user with no selected organization.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A malformed parent or status filter is a 400 before any read, and the list is bounded at 1000 rows (existing test).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The administration pages still treat the list as the union's organizations for choosing a parent; for a caller with no ancestor authority it is only their own row.

records.title: POST /api/organizations is limited to a system administrator and commits the organization row and its organization.create audit row in one system transaction, but it reads the body with no schema and no guard on the JSON parse (a malformed body raises an unhandled error and a 500) and writes whatever the body states: name and slug are not checked (a missing name or a duplicate slug surfaces as an unhandled database error), the cached member_count and active_member_count counters, status, settings JSON, enabled features and CLC affiliation are taken from the body, and the parent may be any organization (the parent is only checked to exist, not for its status or its type, and the administrators of the parent have no say in a new child attached to it), so one request can create an organization with invented member counts under any parent of the hierarchy.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: POST /api/organizations stores description, province_territory, charter_number and affiliation_date; a value of the wrong shape or an impossible date is refused with 400 rather than dropped under a 201.

records.title: POST /api/organizations inserts only name, slug, display_name, type, parent, sectors, email, phone, website, status, CLC affiliation, member counters, settings and features: the description that the new organization page sends is dropped and the sector and jurisdiction that the page sends are stored only inside the settings JSON (the sectors and province_territory columns stay empty), the organization hierarchy admin component sends the type local_union, which the handler refuses with 400, and then tests data.success, a field the handler never returns, so a created organization is not shown and a refused one is not reported; the handler answers 201 with the stored row while the data the caller entered is partly absent from it.

GET /api/organizations/search checks only that a session user id exists and then runs the search inside withSystemContext (the union_eyes_system role that the 0108 policy for the organizations table exempts) with no membership, role or mandate check: any signed-in user can match organizations of every tenant by name or slug (a search with no q returns up to 50 organizations other than the platform type) and receives the id, name, slug, type, parent id, member count, status and sectors of each, so the directory discloses the size, lifecycle status and place in the parent and child hierarchy of organizations the caller has no relationship with.

priorEvidence.nativeEvidence: The hierarchy overlap query and the system role's SELECT privilege were checked against the native schema; the routes have not run natively.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The search is limited to the organizations the caller may read and exposes member counts only to administrative readers (upstream's change, existing contract test).

records.title: GET /api/organizations/search excludes the platform organization type only when no q is given: with a q the filter is an ILIKE on name or slug that returns organizations of every type and every lifecycle status (platform, archived, suspended and inactive organizations included), the q is placed unescaped inside the pattern (a percent sign or underscore matches every row) with no minimum length, the result is limited to 50 with no ordering, no paging and no signal that it was cut, and the statement selects every column of the organizations row (billing contact, settings, contacts) although the mapper returns eight of them.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The organization search always excludes the platform organization type and any organization whose status is not active (a missing status counts as active), with or without a term, matches the term literally (percent and underscore escaped), and orders by name then id. The real-SQL pglite test for the search still passes, and a source-contract test pins the predicates.

records.title: When the canonical bootstrap flag is not 1, GET /api/organizations/tree checks only that a session user exists and then reads every organization, with no limit and no filter on type or status (platform, archived, suspended and inactive organizations included), through the shared db client with no withRLSContext, no withSystemContext, no membership check and no comparison with the caller organization, and returns the id, name, slug, type, parent id, sector, jurisdiction, description, hierarchy level, member count, status and timestamps of each: the whole parent and child hierarchy of the union is treated as visible to every signed-in user, and whether the result is confined to the caller depends entirely on the row-level-security role of the connection (a confined connection with no organization context returns an empty tree for everyone); only the canonical branch limits the tree to the active private memberships of the caller.
