engineeringCorrection.explanation: The component sent status, reviewedAt, reviewedBy, rejectionReason and isFeatured; the table has approvedAt and featured only. It now sends those, the route stamps the approval with the server clock once, and the reject flow is removed because the table cannot record a rejection (the component has no importer).

records.title: GET /api/units and GET /api/units/<id> are crudRoutes over bargaining_units at the member read floor and the table has none of the user, member, e-mail or phone column names the low-role guard looks for, so any member of the organization receives every register row with its certification number, body and dates, contract expiry and next bargaining date, chief steward and bargaining chair user ids, classifications, free-text notes and custom fields object, with no field projection and no read audit.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Notes and custom fields are omitted from every unit response.

records.title: POST /api/units and PATCH /api/units/<id> are configured at writeRole steward with the whole body copied into the row, so any steward of the organization creates a bargaining unit or rewrites its certification number, certification body and dates, current collective agreement id, contract and bargaining dates, member count, chief steward and bargaining chair, and an administrator archives it, with no check that the caller represents the unit and with the audit row listing field names and no values.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A create accepts an allow-list that excludes certification, representation, status and count fields, and a PATCH blocks them; they have no source yet.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: No dedicated route records a certification or changes representation, so those fields are unwritable until one exists.

records.title: GET /api/worksites and GET /api/worksites/<id> are crudRoutes over worksites at the member read floor, so any member of the organization receives every worksite row with the site manager name, e-mail address and telephone number, the address and coordinates, the employee and shift counts, free-text notes and the custom fields object, with no field projection and no read audit, and the worksite management screen and the unit and committee screens load the whole list from the route.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The site manager's name, e-mail and telephone, the notes and the custom fields are omitted from every worksite response.

records.title: POST and PATCH on the unit and worksite routes copy the body into the row, and employer_id, worksite_id, chief_steward_id and bargaining_chair_id are foreign keys to the employers, worksites and profiles tables that carry no organization condition, so the row can name an employer, a worksite or a person of another organization (the foreign key check passes for any existing id) and the register then joins organizations that have nothing to do with each other.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The employer and worksite ids taken from a unit or worksite body are checked against the caller's organization on create and update (400 malformed, 404 not the organization's). Test disclosure: the two worksite route tests that pin the factory options now expect the reference hook.

records.title: The wcb/claims and wcb/claims/[id] routes are crudRoutes over wcb_claims configured at the steward floor for reads and writes (the collection declares an owner column workerId, the item route none), and wcb_claims is DENIED in the CRUD governance table, so assertCrudRead and assertCrudWrite refuse every call with 403 before a query or an audit row, for stewards and administrators alike; the route header describes a claim collection a steward lists and creates, the claim holds the medical and prognosis detail of an injured worker, and if the governance entry is ever lifted every steward of the organization would read and rewrite every claim (the item route has no owner condition), with no relation to the representative who holds the member case.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The WCB claim routes answer 501 explicitly instead of refusing every request through the governance denial; the table no longer has a generic route and its governance entry was removed.

records.title: GET /api/wcb/assessments and GET /api/wcb/assessments/<id> are crudRoutes over wcb_employer_assessments at the steward read floor, so any steward of the organization (not only the officers who record the assessments) receives every assessment row with the premium rate, assessable payroll, premium due, experience rating, surcharge or refund, due and paid dates, status, document ids and the metadata object, with no field projection and no read audit.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The assessment (premium rate, assessable payroll, premium due) is read at the officer floor.

records.title: GET /api/targets/summary is configured at the member floor and returns every kpi_configurations row of the organization with the whole row spread into the response (`...cfg`): the calculation record (formula, aggregation and filters), the alert recipients (user ids or e-mail addresses), the id of the creator and the dashboard layout reach any member of the organization, not the officers who create targets, with no field projection and no read audit.

currentRun.note: Source correction and adversarial route tests committed; exact-HEAD CI and VS/runtime acceptance pending.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Officer-only authorization, explicit non-sensitive projection, tenant-bound database context and mandatory read audit remove member exposure of calculation, alert recipients, creator and dashboard layout.

records.title: The summary takes the current value of a target from the latest analytics_metrics row of the organization whose metric_type text equals the target metric type (one query per target through the shared database handle) and applies neither the data source (claims, members, financial, custom_query) nor the calculation the target declares, so a target is judged against whatever row carries the same type name, and a row of another unit or period that shares the text is read as the current value; the progress figure divides that value by the target value.

computeHealth returns critical when the current value is at or below the critical threshold, at risk when it is at or below the warning threshold and on track otherwise, for every target: a target whose good direction is downward (resolution time, backlog, grievance count) is reported critical when its figure is low and on track when its figure is high, and the route stores no direction.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Migration 0038 adds kpi_configurations.direction (higher_is_better or lower_is_better, null for rows that predate it). A target can be created with a direction, and the summary lets a stored direction decide; only a target with none keeps the threshold-order inference. Proven on PGlite (check constraint) and by unit tests.

records.title: POST /api/targets stores a free-form calculation record (any key and value, defaulted to a sum), an alertEnabled flag and a data source, and the summary route reads none of the calculation or the data source and no code found reads alertEnabled to send an alert: the insert writes no alertRecipients value at all, so a target created with alertEnabled true promises an alert that no recipient list and no sender exists to deliver.

PATCH /api/targets/<id> compares the path id with the uuid column kpi_configurations.id without a shape check, so a malformed id raises a database error that the wrapper answers as a 500 instead of a 404, and the route offers no way to edit, rename or delete a target: the only change available after creation is the active flag.

currentRun.repair: Reject malformed target IDs before UUID database predicate and audit; added regression proving no DB call.
currentRun.limits: The same frozen defect also requires edit/rename/delete capabilities; these remain unimplemented. Do not count as engineering-corrected.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: a malformed target id is a 400 before any database predicate is built, with an existing test that no query or audit happens.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The route still offers no edit, rename or delete of a target.

records.title: GET /api/users/me/organizations, in its legacy branch (entered whenever UE_CANONICAL_BOOTSTRAP_V2 is not 1), links membership rows to the caller when the caller has none: it takes the e-mail address from the identity provider user (or the profile row), selects every organization_members row of any organization whose lower-cased e-mail equals it and runs an update that sets user_id to the caller on all of them, with no condition on the current user_id (a row already bound to another person is rewritten), no verified-address check, no role limit, no organization limit and no audit record; if no row carries the e-mail, a second statement sets user_id to the caller on every membership of the legacy user id of any profile that shares the e-mail; the response then lists the organizations and the roles that were taken, and the whole sequence runs inside a GET with the shared database handle.

remaining: The test that asserted the self-healing was replaced by tests that assert it never happens

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A GET never links or rewrites a membership by e-mail address or through another user id's profile; memberships are only those already bound to the caller (existing implementation, existing tests assert no update).

records.title: In the legacy branch a user id listed in PLATFORM_ADMIN_USER_IDS receives up to 500 organization records (name, slug, type, parent, sector, jurisdiction, description) whatever their memberships, and every other caller causes the route to select the whole organizations table and filter it in memory by the ids and slugs of the caller memberships, so the cost grows with every organization of the platform and the platform list is held by an environment list the application cannot audit.

The legacy branch logs the full e-mail address of the caller (email: userEmail) when it links memberships by e-mail and a three-letter preview of it in another line, together with the user id, so a log reader receives the address that the re-binding was made on.

The response replaces a missing createdAt or updatedAt of an organization, and a missing joinedAt and createdAt of a membership, with the time of the call (new Date().toISOString()), so a record without a stored time is returned with a time that never existed.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A missing stored creation, update or join time is returned as null rather than the time of the call.

records.title: The /api/v2/[...path] catch-all is exported as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE by one handler that answers HTTP 200 with a deprecation object for every method and path: the dues report page posts /api/v2/admin/reports/generate and treats a response that is ok as a generated report, the user role selector puts a role change to /api/v2/admin/users/role and shows the toast Role updated on an ok response, and the staff page posts remittance approve and reject to /api/v2/clc/remittances/<id>/approve and /reject and logs Approved remittance on an ok response, while the file that builds a 410 Gone response (goneResponse) exists and the catch-all never calls it, so a write to a removed path is reported to its caller as a success and nothing is written.

remaining: Frontend callers of removed /api/v2 endpoints now fail visibly; see functionalGaps

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The catch-all already answers 410 for every method; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.

records.title: GET on a removed /api/v2 path answers HTTP 200 with an object whose keys are _deprecated, _message, _sunset and _canonical, where the callers (the push device manager, the social media post composer, the benchmark and scheduled report consoles, the federation remittances and compliance pages) read the body as the list or figures they requested, so a console renders an empty state or no data with no signal that its endpoint was removed.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Same: 410 with no data body, upstream's change, existing test.

records.title: The catch-all calls logDeprecatedAccess(v2Path, request.method, canonical) with no user id and no organization id and does not await it, and logDeprecatedAccess swallows a failure of the audit write, so the api.deprecated_access event names a path and a method and no actor, and its loss is silent.

The deprecation module holds the sunset date as a constant (2026-07-07) that it prints in the body and the Sunset header, and nothing compares it with the current time or changes the answer after it, so the route keeps answering 200 with a sunset that has passed and no removal is scheduled in source.

GET /api/tenant/current answers HTTP 200 with an org whose name, slug and subscriptionTier are constant null and whose features list is empty, and an availableOrgs list that holds only that same org, so a legacy client that reads the organization name or tier receives a success with no data; the route reads no organization row, and no caller in the application calls it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: tenant/current answers 410 Gone, pointing at org/current. Its old route test (asserting the placeholder body) was deleted and superseded by the 410 test.

records.title: GET /api/test-auth is a plain route (no wrapper, no role floor, no production guard) that any signed-in user can call: it sends the session token as a bearer to the Django address held in the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL build variable (localhost:8000 when unset), returns the status and body of the backend health and /me/ answers, the session user id and organization, whether a token exists and the text of any fetch error (String(e)), so the response discloses backend addresses and error details and the diagnostic ships in every build.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The diagnostic is a platform administrator's: anyone else gets 403 and the backend is never called; the response carries backend statuses only, never the backend bodies. Test disclosure: two tests added, the existing one now mocks platform-admin authority.

records.title: GET /api/union-eyes/queue-status accepts either the service key header or any signed-in session (requireApiAuth with no role, no organization requirement), and returns the pending, active, failed and retry counts of the whole background queue, the per-queue counts and the task id, task name, status and completion time of the 20 most recent failed tasks, which are platform-wide operational data not scoped to an organization, to a signed-in member.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Queue counts and failed task names are for the control-plane key or a platform administrator and refuse a signed-in member (existing implementation; the contract test pins the administrator check before the queue read).

records.title: The queue status route sends every error, including the refusal that requireApiAuth throws for a caller with no session, through one catch that answers HTTP 503 with availability error and detail String(err), so an unauthenticated call is reported as an outage and the text of the underlying error (a connection string error of the queue backend, for example) is returned to the caller; when no Django address is configured the route answers 200 with availability not_configured and a null queue.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Access is the service key or a signed-in platform administrator (401 / 403 otherwise); the error text is logged, not returned. The existing queue-status test was adapted to mock the platform-admin guard and logger.

records.title: The service credential of the route is the AI_SERVICE_KEY environment value, the same key that the AI service uses, compared with the request header by a plain equality (===) and not a constant-time comparison, and the control plane sends it on every telemetry call, so one key opens the queue figures and the AI service and cannot be rotated for one without the other.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The service key is compared in constant time; a wrong, short or empty key falls to the platform-administrator path.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The control plane still authenticates with the shared AI service key rather than a key dedicated to queue status.

records.title: POST /api/triage-designations passes caseAssigneeEligible (the case policy role that may add an internal note, or ue_case_assignee_authorized in the canonical branch) as the eligibility test for a designation of either scope, while the message queue decides use of a messages designation with the conversation assignee roles (membershipStillEligible), so a messages designation can be refused to a person who is an eligible conversation assignee and granted to a person who is a case assignee and not a conversation assignee, whose designation then grants nothing.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: A messages designation is judged as a conversation assignee (live membership with a conversation-assignee role); only a cases designation uses the case-assignee test.

records.title: grantDesignation closes a lapsed live designation by setting revokedAt to now and revokedBy to the string system:expiry before the new grant, in the same transaction, and writes no audit row for the closure (only the grant is audited), so the end of an expired designation is a data change with no audit record and a revoker value that is not a user.

DELETE /api/triage-designations takes the designation id from a JSON request body (body: revokeSchema), a pattern that HTTP intermediaries and many clients drop or ignore for DELETE, and the route has no path id; no caller in the application sends the request.

The vocabulary routes serve, as reference data of the grievance system, hard-coded service-level hours (24 hours for critical, 48 high, 72 medium, 168 low), severity legal-review flags, per-role canAssign, canEscalate and canSettle flags for roles named member, steward, chief_steward, business_agent, officer and admin, and a status machine with the roles allowed to make each transition, from a package whose header calls them defaults, with no cited source, no approval and no relation to the roles the application enforces; the flags are not read by any enforcing code found, and a client that treats them as the institution service levels or permissions would present an unsourced figure as institutional.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The six vocabulary routes serve identifiers, labels, descriptions and categories only. Service-level hours, escalation, legal and settlement flags, role permissions, default priority and severity, and status transitions are no longer served as institutional reference data; the case state machine still reads them from the package server-side.

records.title: Every vocabulary route sets Cache-Control public with max-age 3600 on a response that is behind a signed-in session, so a shared cache or proxy may store and serve the response to callers without a session for an hour.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: All six vocabulary routes serve a signed-in response with Cache-Control private, so a shared cache cannot hand it to a caller without a session.

records.title: getCUPEVocabulary sets lastUpdated to the time of the call and version to the constant 0.1.0, so the full vocabulary route reports a last update of now on every request and a version that does not change when the content changes.

POST /api/voice/transcribe, at the steward floor, applies no rate limit and no entitlement check and writes no audit record, while the sibling upload route applies a rate limit and an entitlement check: a steward (or a script holding a steward session) can send repeated 25 MB recordings, each up to the 60-second function limit, to the speech service with no count and no record of who transcribed what.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Transcription is rate limited per caller, requires an organization context, and records the disclosure (language, size, type; never the audio or text) before the recording leaves; if the audit cannot be written nothing is sent.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: There is no entitlement or consent decision for sending a recording to the external service.

records.title: The transcribe response sets duration to audioFile.size (the size of the upload in bytes, with the comment Approximate), so a caller that reads duration receives a number of bytes presented as a length of time.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The transcription response carries no duration: neither bytes nor a guess is reported as a measured audio duration (existing implementation and test).

records.title: Both voice routes read the uploaded recording into memory and send it to an external Azure service (the speech service in the transcribe route, an Azure OpenAI Whisper deployment in the upload route), and the recordings are spoken claim descriptions that can name a person, an employer and a medical or disciplinary matter: neither route records a consent, names a processor agreement or region, records the disclosure or states a retention, and the upload route logs the body of a failed processor answer.

POST /api/voice/upload checks the ai_search entitlement of the organization (and labels a refusal voice_upload) for a transcription feature, and checkEntitlement only reads settings.credits and consumes none, so the check neither meters the transcription nor reflects a voice entitlement; no caller of the route exists in the application.

POST /api/workspace/telemetry accepts the allow-listed event name and logs every allow-listed payload key, of which tab and timestamp are written as the client string with no length bound or format check (route is checked against the static route list), with no rate limit, so a member can write arbitrarily long strings of their choice into the application log at any rate, and the figures the route exists to produce live only in log lines.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The telemetry body is bounded to 2 KB while it is streamed (not only by Content-Length), the payload is reduced to an allow-list of canonical event, tab and static route, and the client attests to no timestamp or workspace name (existing implementation and tests).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The route has no rate limit of its own beyond the member floor.

records.title: For a workbook with no claimed_by_user_id, resolveClaimedWorkbookAuthority returns the preclaim authority from the workbook identifier alone, so GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE on /api/workbook/<id>/memory-holders run in the system context for any caller who presents that identifier, with no session, with no guardPublicIntake or other rate limit (the route files import none), and auditClaimedWorkbookWrite returns at once for a preclaim authority so the create, update and delete are not recorded; the same identifier is returned by the public start route and placed in the checkout redirect addresses, and each write may carry a display name and notes of up to 4,000 characters.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The collection reads and writes run through the public-intake guard (rate limit; body cap on writes). Claimed-workbook writes were already audited.
engineeringCorrection.remaining: The per-holder item route is not yet behind the guard, there is no per-workbook holder cap, and unclaimed-workbook reads are not audited.

records.title: After the claim, a same-organization peer is any signed-in person for whom getOrganizationIdForUser returns the claimed organization (that function selects an organization by a client cookie after a membership check): resolveClaimedWorkbookAuthority applies no role floor, and the memory-holder routes then let that person list, create, change and delete holders in the system context, with a display name and notes naming individuals who have no notice that they are recorded, and the PATCH and DELETE audit rows are written only when a row changed.

POST /api/workbook/start accepts consent as an optional object (consentToPersist and a time), inserts the workbook whether or not the object is present or true (consent is stored as null when absent) and logs only the workbook id and locale; no route of the workbook product reads workbooks.consent before it stores a memory holder, creates a checkout session or exports, so the consent the visitor gave or withheld changes nothing the product does.

guardPublicIntake keys its per-client limit (20 starts per hour, 10 checkouts per hour) on the first of cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip or the first x-forwarded-for entry, all request headers a client can set when the application is not behind a proxy that overwrites them, and neither public route reads a challenge token, so a caller can create workbooks and open Stripe checkout sessions at a rate the limit does not bound.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The workbook start and checkout buckets key on the trusted address (they use the shared guard).
engineeringCorrection.remaining: There is still no bot challenge on workbook start or checkout.

records.title: POST /api/workbook/checkout reads the workbook through the shared database handle (import { db } from '@/db') outside withSystemContext, withRLSContext and withClaimedWorkbookAccess, so the handle is the pooled runtime connection with no app.current_user_id; the closure migration creates the user isolation policy on workbooks over claimed_by_user_id, whose select policy compares that column with app.current_user_id, so an unclaimed workbook (the only kind a buyer has before paying) is not visible to the read and the route would answer 404 for it; the start and claim routes use withSystemContext for the same table, and the runtime proof of the policy is outstanding.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The unclaimed-workbook read runs under the explicit system context, as the start and claim routes do, instead of on the pooled connection with no user context. Test adapted to the new context call; new tests cover 404 and 503.

records.title: POST /api/workbook/checkout sends the workbook identifier, which is the bearer credential for the memory holders of an unclaimed workbook, to Stripe in metadata.workbook_id and in the success and cancel addresses (/workbook/<id>?tier_unlocked=workbook_self_guided), so the credential is held by the payment processor, appears in the browser history and referrer chain of the buyer and is logged with the session id, and no source states the processor agreement or the lifecycle of the identifier.

When NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is not set the checkout success and cancel addresses fall back to http://localhost:3000, and the route tests only that the workbook is not already at the self-guided tier, so each call creates a new Stripe session with no pending-session or idempotency check and a buyer or script can open any number of sessions for one workbook.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Production refuses to open a session without NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (503) and the session is created with an idempotency key per workbook, tier and 30-minute window, so a repeat reuses it.

records.title: POST /api/workbook/<id>/claim requires a session but applies no rate limit and reads the body with request.json() without a size cap, and a request whose id and token match a row but whose claim has lapsed is answered 409 or 410 while a miss is answered 404, so a signed-in caller can try claim tokens against an identifier at the speed of the application.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: The claim runs through the public-intake guard: rate limited (429, or 503 when the limiter is down in production) and body capped (413) before it is parsed.

records.title: GET /api/workbook/<id>/export builds a PDF of the carrier register (role, criticality, tenure, successor and the free-text responsibility of every memory holder, with the cartography) for a claimant or any same-organization peer and writes no audit record of the read; loadWorkbookModules also selects the display name of every holder into memory although the template does not print it.

The start, checkout and claim routes write the workbook identifier, which is the bearer credential of an unclaimed workbook, to the application log (with the locale, the Stripe session id, or the user id and organization id), so anyone who reads the log can use the identifier on the memory-holder routes until the workbook is claimed.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Workbook routes log a one-way 12-character reference of the identifier, never the identifier, which acts as a capability. Test disclosure: the claim test expectations for the two log calls changed to the reference.

records.title: ue_authority_reviews holds the complainant, the adverse parties and the privileged classification of every review of an organization, and the only row-level-security policy on it is the organization-only policy ue_create_direct_org_rls_policy (migration 0020) while the storage-authority manifest requires SELECT on the table for the tenant runtime role; the rules that hide a review from its adverse party, show an overseer only the reviews a live monitor mandate names, and omit respondent identifiers are SQL predicates and kernel calls inside lib/authority/store/review-intake.ts, so any other query that runs in an organization context can read every review of the organization and the database enforces none of those rules.

POST /api/reviews accepts up to eight adverseUserIds and normaliseAdverse tests each only with isPrincipalId (a non-empty string of at most 255 characters with no control character) plus a self and duplicate check; registerReview then stores them in adverse_user_ids with no lookup showing that the named person is a member of the organization, no trigger checks them (the actor trigger guards opened_by only), and the own-list query excludes a stored adverse id and the kernel decideReview denies oversight to it (ADVERSE_PARTY: respondent cannot exercise oversight), so a complainant decides, by an unverified assertion, which person is excluded from seeing the review and from overseeing it.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: requireAdverseMembers checks every named adverse party is an active member of the organization (one generic refusal, no per-identity oracle) before anything is written. Real-SQL pglite test.

records.title: POST /api/reviews applies no rate limit of its own, never reads the idempotency key and never uses the ue_authority_requests idempotency store, and the table declares no uniqueness over the opener, type and adverse parties, so every call by an active member inserts a new review, the authority event row the trigger records and a canonical audit row; ue_authority_reviews is append-only (a trigger refuses DELETE and TRUNCATE), so a member or a script can create an unbounded number of permanent review rows that no route or retry path can remove.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Per-member intake is serialised with an advisory lock; a repeat of an identical open review returns that review (200, alreadyOpen) instead of another append-only row; a daily cap of 10 raises REVIEW_INTAKE_LIMIT answered 429 with Retry-After. pglite and route tests.

records.title: POST /api/reviews reads the body with request.json() before openSchema.safeParse, so the schema limits (reviewType enum, eight adverse ids, 255 characters each) apply only after the whole body has been buffered and parsed; the route sets no body-size cap and imports no public-intake or size guard.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: readBoundedBody enforces a 2 KiB cap by declared length and by streamed length, cancelling the stream, before JSON parsing; 413 otherwise.

records.title: The route takes the organization from getOrganizationIdForUser (the selected-organization cookie checked against active membership) and passes it to the store as the explicit organizationId, but calls withRLSContext(async (tx) => ...) with no context map, so outside the canonical-state mode the transaction binds app.current_org_id from the organization on the auth session or user metadata (orgId = authOrgId) instead; withRLSContext documents that only an explicit { organizationId } enforces exactly one organization, and the route never compares its two resolutions, so a disagreement surfaces only as an empty result or as a database error that the route rethrows.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: Both handlers call withRLSContext({ organizationId }) with the organization the route resolved, so the database context cannot be a second resolution.

records.title: reviewErrorResponse answers only AuthorityStoreError and the case-authorization errors; any other failure (a database or row-level-security error, the Unauthorized error withRLSContext throws, a binding error) is rethrown with `throw error` from a route that has no wrapper, so the caller receives the framework default server error with no structured body, and the route neither logs nor audits the failure.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: reviewErrorResponse maps ApiError to 401/403 and logs any other failure with logger.error, answering a structured INTERNAL_ERROR 500 that does not echo the cause.

records.title: GET /api/reviews returns, for each review a live monitor mandate allows, complainantUserId and the standard or privileged classification, and listMemberReviewIntake calls the pure kernel decide for review:monitor and writes no record of the read; the decision, the mandate that supplied it and the reviews disclosed are not stored, so an oversight read of complainant identity cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

engineeringCorrection.explanation: An oversight read persists review.oversight.read with the disclosed review ids and the privileged count through persistAtomicAudit in the same transaction; an own-only list records nothing.
